chunks.x: Registration with your professional body, and the visa that goes with it, are national processes and identical wherever in New Zealand you land. They are explained once, properly, in Eligibility & registration and Immigration & visas . How the health system is funded and structured — ACC, primary care, what things cost, how it differs from the NHS or a private system — lives in How the health system works . Ethicare Live roles & professions What we’re recruiting for now, by profession and by region. National guide Pay & conditions How national collective agreements work, and what to check before you sign. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Palmerston North: twelve areas compared
chunks.x: In most cities this chapter is about balancing commute against cost. In Palmerston North the commute is ten minutes from everywhere, so you get to choose on something better: what you want your street to feel like. When commute stops mattering Ten minutes covers almost every address here, so the usual trade-off never arrives. What separates the options is temperament, not travel. The settled heart Mature trees, character homes and the river paths close by — Hokowhitu and the walkable inner streets, where demand is steadiest. The growing edges Modern, insulated builds to the north and up the rising south side, where the same money buys more floor and, on the hills, a view. The green fringe Semi-rural blocks by the university and beyond — paddocks and quiet, still only minutes from a ward round. A rare luxury in this country: pick the street you like best and let the commute take care of itself.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Palmerston North: twelve areas compared
chunks.x: Hokowhitu The city’s most sought-after address, and deservedly. Leafy streets by the river and the Esplanade, established homes, mature trees, well-regarded schools. Ten minutes to the hospital, and a walk to the water. West End & Fitzroy Character villas and bungalows close to the city centre, walkable to The Square and to work. Popular with clinicians who want to leave the car at home. Milson Solid, friendly, good-value family housing to the north, well served by schools and parks. A lot of people’s first house here. Awapuni & Takaro Established western suburbs with the best value inside the city boundary. Straightforward family living, five to ten minutes from anywhere. Terrace End & Roslyn Close-in, mixed and affordable, on the northern side of the centre. Handy for the hospital and the Square. Kelvin Grove Newer housing on the northern edge, with the city’s growth happening around it. Warm modern homes and more space for the money.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Palmerston North: twelve areas compared
chunks.x: Fitzherbert Between the river and the university. Convenient, green and mixed — family homes alongside a student population, with the He Ara Kotahi path into town. Aokautere & Summerhill The city’s only hills, and the views that come with them. Newer, larger homes on the southern slopes, fifteen minutes from the hospital and a favourite with relocating families. Massey & Turitea Semi-rural living right by the university, with lifestyle blocks and small holdings a few minutes further out. Quiet, green and close in. Parkland and water inside the city

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Palmerston North: twelve areas compared
chunks.x: Ashhurst A friendly village at the foot of the ranges, twenty minutes east, right by Te Āpiti. Village school, real community, and the gorge tracks on your doorstep. Feilding An award-winning country town twenty minutes north, with a thriving main street and the famous Friday market. Excellent value, strong community, and an easy commute. Foxton, Foxton Beach & Himatangi Thirty minutes west, on the coast. The cheapest housing in reach of the city, dunes at the end of the road, and a much quieter life. Three things to check before you sign Insulation, glazing and heating. This is a frosty city and the housing stock is older than the north’s. Ask for the Healthy Homes compliance statement and look for a heat pump. The school zone, at the exact address. Popular state schools here are zoned and enrolment is by address — see Schools & education . Whether you need to be in the city.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Palmerston North: twelve areas compared
chunks.x: Because the commute is so short, Feilding or Ashhurst are viable, and your money goes considerably further. Worth modelling both. Most clinicians we move here rent for six months and then buy, which is a shorter runway than in most cities — because the market is affordable enough that you do not need to save for years first. How renting works — the application pack, bond, tenancy rights and the Healthy Homes standards — is national and covered once in Renting in New Zealand . Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Getting around Palmerston North: cycling, buses and flights
chunks.x: This is the shortest chapter in the guide, and that is the point. Palmerston North is flat, compact and laid out on a grid. There is no traffic problem to explain, no bridge to queue for, and no suburb from which work is a slog.

chunks.t: Getting around Palmerston North: cycling, buses and flights
chunks.x: Ten to fifteen minutes by car from essentially anywhere in the city, at any hour. There is a mild thickening around school pick-up and on the northern approaches, and that is the whole story. Parking at the hospital and in town is straightforward and cheap or free. If you are arriving from London, Manchester, Johannesburg, Dubai or Auckland, this is the change that will surprise you most. Clinicians tell us they get an hour or more back every day, and that the hour is worth more than they expected.

chunks.t: Getting around Palmerston North: cycling, buses and flights
chunks.x: Palmerston North has the best case for everyday cycling of any city we write about. It is almost entirely flat, distances are short, and there is a real network of shared paths — including He Ara Kotahi , the riverside path and bridge linking the city to the south bank and the university. The practical consequence: a sizeable proportion of the city cycles to work as a matter of course, not as a statement. An e-bike is barely necessary here, though the wind is the one argument for having one. It is also a very good city to teach children to ride in. The wind, and the bike The prevailing westerly is the only real obstacle to cycling here. On a strong day the ride home can be work. Most regular riders keep either an e-bike or a bus card for those days. Neither is expensive.

chunks.t: Getting around Palmerston North: cycling, buses and flights
chunks.x: City buses A regional network across the city and out to Feilding and Ashhurst, paid for with a Bee Card — the same card used across the Manawatū, Waikato and Bay of Plenty. Useful, cheap, and modest in frequency. The commuter train A weekday service between Palmerston North and Wellington. Slower than driving but far more civilised, and it makes the occasional day in the capital easy. Long-distance rail The main trunk line runs through the city, so the scenic long-distance service stops here on its way between Auckland and Wellington. Do you need a car? If you live centrally and cycle, you can manage with one car for a household, which is unusual outside the big cities. For the ranges, the coast and weekends away, you’ll want one.

chunks.t: Getting around Palmerston North: cycling, buses and flights
chunks.x: Palmerston North Airport Ten minutes from the centre, with direct flights to Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch. Small, easy and refreshingly quick to get through. Long-haul Via Auckland or Wellington. Wellington is under two hours by road if you prefer to drive to the airport, which many people do. Getting home Budget a comfortable half-day at each end. Broadly comparable with most New Zealand cities outside Auckland. Domestic weekends Being in the middle of the island is the underrated advantage. Half the North Island is inside a three-hour drive.

chunks.t: Getting around Palmerston North: cycling, buses and flights
chunks.x: Journey Typical time Across the city 10–15 min City → airport 10 min City → Massey University 10 min City → Ashhurst / Te Āpiti 20–25 min City → Feilding 20 min City → Foxton Beach 30 min City → Levin 45 min City → Whanganui 1 hr 15 City → Wellington 1 hr 50 City → Napier or Taupō ~2 hr 30 Times on a good run. The road east over the ranges is the one to check in bad weather. Converting your licence, buying a car, and what a warrant of fitness and registration involve are national matters, explained once in Driving & licences . Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Weekends in Palmerston North: river, ranges and the coast
chunks.x: The gift of a flat city in the middle of an island: mountains twenty-five minutes one way, coast half an hour the other, a river through the middle, and half the North Island inside a three-hour drive.

chunks.t: Weekends in Palmerston North: river, ranges and the coast
chunks.x: The Manawatū runs along the southern edge of the city, and the path network along it is the thing residents use most. He Ara Kotahi — the shared path and its bridge — links the city to the south bank, the university and a long, flat, scenic loop that works equally well for a run, a ride or a pram. Next to it, the Victoria Esplanade : riverside gardens, a rose collection, an aviary, a playground and a miniature railway. Unfashionable and entirely lovely, and if you arrive with children it will become a fixture within a fortnight. Mountains one way, coast the other Driving times from the city, to scale against each other. The two marked rows are the chapter’s whole argument: ranges twenty-five minutes east, wild coast half an hour west, and a flat city in between.

chunks.t: Weekends in Palmerston North: river, ranges and the coast
chunks.x: Arapuke Forest Park Flow trails in the pines, graded from first-timer to serious ~15 min Te Āpiti / Manawatū Gorge Bush tracks and a turbine-lined ridge above the river ~25 min The Manawatū coast Black sand, marram and driftwood under big Tasman skies ~30 min Ruapehu’s ski fields A proper mountain, close enough for a snow weekend ~2½ hours Indicative driving times. Wellington sits under two hours south — close enough for a concert, far enough that nobody commutes.

chunks.t: Weekends in Palmerston North: river, ranges and the coast
chunks.x: Te Āpiti / Manawatū Gorge Twenty-five minutes east. Walking tracks through native bush along the gorge, a ridgeline route, and a lookout among the wind turbines. The region’s signature day out. The Tararua Range Serious tramping country right on the doorstep — huts, tops and weather that demands respect. Some of the best training ground in the country. The Ruahine & Rangiwāhia North-east of the city, with the Rangiwāhia Track and its swing bridge — a beautiful half-day into bush and open tops. Arapuke Forest Park Purpose-built mountain biking in pine and native forest fifteen minutes from town, with trails for every level. The Sledge Track A short, popular bush walk with swing bridges near Ashhurst. The go-to when you have an hour and a half. Snow, occasionally The tops get a proper covering in winter. Ruapehu and its ski fields are two and a half hours north.

chunks.t: Weekends in Palmerston North: river, ranges and the coast
chunks.x: Half an hour west and you are in a different landscape: thirty kilometres of dunes, marram grass, driftwood and black sand, with the Tasman rolling in. Himatangi Beach, Foxton Beach and the mouths of the rivers are wild rather than pretty — big skies, long horizons and very few people. Neethu and her husband out for the day. Neethu was placed by Ethicare as an anaesthetic technician at Palmerston North Hospital. It is not a swimming-beach culture in the way the Bay of Plenty is; the surf is heavy and the water is cooler. What it is instead is dramatic, and empty, and twenty minutes closer than most people expect. The Manawatū coast, half an hour west Carving and story across the rohe of Rangitāne Whakapapa, on Mount Ruapehu — about two and a half hours from Palmerston North, and an ordinary winter weekend for one of the families we placed.

chunks.t: Weekends in Palmerston North: river, ranges and the coast
chunks.x: Wellington — 1 hr 50 The capital for galleries, touring acts, restaurants and the ferry south. Easy for a day or a night. The Wairarapa — ~2 hr Over or around the ranges to Martinborough’s wineries and Greytown’s main street. Whanganui — 1 hr 15 A river city with a real arts scene and some of the finest heritage architecture in the country. Taupō & Ruapehu — 2 hr 30 The lake, the volcanoes, the Tongariro crossing and the ski fields. Hawke’s Bay — 2 hr 30 Wine, art deco and warmth, over the ranges to the north-east. Taranaki — 2 hr 30 A near-perfect volcano, surf coast and New Plymouth’s coastal walkway.

chunks.t: Weekends in Palmerston North: river, ranges and the coast
chunks.x: Tourism Manawatū NZ The region’s official visitor site: events, food, trails and things to do. Council Palmerston North City Council Local services, libraries, pools, parks and community programmes. Outdoors Department of Conservation Tracks, huts and reserves across the Tararua and Ruahine ranges. Culture Te Manawa The city’s museum, art gallery and science centre, in one building. That’s the guide Nine chapters on Palmerston North. Everything national — visas, registration, tax, renting, driving, schools, te ao Māori — lives in Moving to New Zealand . When you’re ready to look at roles, see what’s open now . Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Moving to Palmerston North: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Nau mai, haere mai ki Te Papaioea. Palmerston North is the flat, green, unpretentious city at the crossroads of the lower North Island — a university town with a base hospital, the cheapest good housing in the North Island, and mountains on the horizon from almost every street.

chunks.t: Moving to Palmerston North: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Palmerston North sits in the middle of the Manawatū plain, an hour and a half or so north of Wellington, with the Tararua and Ruahine ranges rising to the east and thirty kilometres of dune coast to the west. It is a city of around ninety thousand people built almost entirely on the flat, which makes it the easiest place in New Zealand to cycle and one of the easiest to park. Two things shape it. The first is Massey University, whose main campus sits just south of the river and gives the city a young, international, research-driven character that a place this size would not otherwise have. The second is the hospital — the base hospital for the wider region, and one of a small number of centres in the country delivering radiation oncology.

chunks.t: Moving to Palmerston North: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: What the city buys you is straightforward: a clinical salary that goes further here than almost anywhere else in the North Island, a ten-minute commute, and the ranges at the weekend. What it costs you is glamour. Nobody moves to Palmerston North for the skyline. People move here, and then find they do not want to leave. Who wrote this Ethicare is a healthcare recruitment company. This guide is free to read, asks nothing of you, and does not give visa advice. Palmerston North is the city we most often have to persuade people to look at, and the one they most often thank us for afterwards. Where we think it’s the wrong answer, we say so.

chunks.t: Moving to Palmerston North: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: ~90,000 People in the city, with around a quarter of a million across the wider Manawatū-Whanganui region. ~1 hr 50 To Wellington by road, or a little under two hours on the commuter train. Close enough for a concert, far enough to be a different life. ~10 min A typical commute, from most of the city to the hospital. Fifteen if you take it slowly. 1 base hospital Serving Manawatū, Horowhenua, Tararua and the Kāpiti coast, run by Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora. 1 of a few Regional cancer centres in the country delivering radiation oncology. That is unusual for a city this size and it changes what work is available here. Flat Almost entirely. The city has kilometres of shared paths and the highest rate of everyday cycling of any comparable New Zealand city. Best value Housing, for a North Island city with a base hospital.

chunks.t: Moving to Palmerston North: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Buying on a single clinical salary is achievable here in a way it is not in Auckland, Tauranga or Wellington. ~25 min To the foot of the ranges, or to Feilding. Half an hour to the coast. Everything is close. 1 airport Ten minutes from town, with direct flights to Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch. Dressed for a celebration organised by the Kerala Society of Manawatū. Left, Neethu’s daughter; Neethu was placed by Ethicare as an anaesthetic technician at Palmerston North Hospital.

chunks.t: Moving to Palmerston North: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: The wind is a real thing The Manawatū is one of the windiest places in the country — there is a large wind farm on the hills for a reason. Most days it is a breeze; some days it is a event. You stop noticing within a season. Everyone cycles Flat streets, short distances and good shared paths mean the bike is the fastest way across town. Clinicians here are far more likely to commute by bike than anywhere else we place people. It is a student city, in the good way Massey brings cheap food, live music, sport, an international community and a real hum in term time. It also empties out in January, which locals rather enjoy. Wellington is a day trip, not a commute People do commute, and the train makes it possible, but at nearly two hours each way it is a choice rather than a habit. "Palmy" is what everyone calls it Affectionately, including the council.

chunks.t: Moving to Palmerston North: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: You will be using it within a fortnight. The ranges change the weather Snow on the Tararua tops in winter, seen from the supermarket car park. It is a flat city with dramatic scenery at the edge of it. A note on names Te Papaioea is the city’s name in te reo Māori, and this is the rohe of Rangitāne o Manawatū. The central square is Te Marae o Hine, the courtyard of the daughter of peace — a name given as a commitment that all peoples would live here together peacefully. You’re not expected to arrive fluent. You are expected to try. Te ao Māori at work covers pronunciation and the words you’ll hear on the ward.

chunks.t: Moving to Palmerston North: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Nine chapters, all of them about Palmerston North specifically. Anything true of New Zealand generally — visas, registration, tax, renting law, driving licences, schools — lives once in Moving to New Zealand . If you read nothing else, read Why Palmerston North for the full case — and what we’d ask you to weigh, and Healthcare here , because the clinical offer in this city is more interesting than its size suggests. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Why Palmerston North: the case for Palmy
chunks.x: Nobody arrives in New Zealand with Palmerston North at the top of their list. It is the city clinicians end up choosing on the arithmetic, and then stay in for reasons that have nothing to do with arithmetic at all.

chunks.t: Why Palmerston North: the case for Palmy
chunks.x: Clinical pay in New Zealand is set nationally. A nurse, radiation therapist, physiotherapist or sonographer on a given step earns exactly the same here as in Auckland or Tauranga. What changes is what the money buys. Here it buys the most. Palmerston North has the cheapest good housing of any North Island city with a base hospital. A three or four-bedroom family home with a garden, ten minutes from work and in a decent school zone, is an ordinary purchase on a single clinical salary. That sentence is not true in Auckland, Wellington or the Bay of Plenty, and we would not write it if it were not. Add to that a commute measured in single-figure minutes, free or cheap parking, and a city small enough that you are never more than twenty minutes from anything. The compounding effect on your life is larger than people expect: you get hours back every week, and you spend materially less to live better. Anu and her husband in Palmerston North. Anu was placed by Ethicare as an anaesthetic technician at Palmerston North Hospital, and is part of a close circle of colleagues there.

chunks.t: Why Palmerston North: the case for Palmy
chunks.x: Monday to Friday Ten to fifteen minutes to work, or twenty on the bike along the river path. Parking is easy. You will be home before you would have left the car park in a larger city. After work The Esplanade gardens, the He Ara Kotahi river loop, or a swim. In term time there is live music and student-priced food most nights of the week. Saturday The farmers’ market in the morning, then either the ranges or the coast — both within half an hour, in opposite directions. Sunday Te Āpiti and the gorge tracks, Arapuke for mountain biking, or the garden. Gardening works well here; the Manawatū grows almost anything. A long weekend Wellington, the Wairarapa wineries, Taupō, Hawke’s Bay, Whanganui and Taranaki are all a comfortable drive. Being in the middle of the island is the point. Winter Frosty mornings, snow on the tops, and a city that carries on regardless. cold compared with the north, and drier than Wellington.

chunks.t: Why Palmerston North: the case for Palmy
chunks.h: The six things people ask us
chunks.x: Is there enough clinical work in a city this size? More than you would expect, and this is the point most people miss. Palmerston North is a base hospital serving a large region, and it delivers radiation oncology — something only a handful of centres in New Zealand do. For medical imaging, radiation therapy and oncology-adjacent professions that makes it a significant place to work. Healthcare here sets out the detail. Will I be bored? The answer: it depends what you need. The university keeps a real cultural and sporting calendar going, the food scene is better than the city’s reputation, and the outdoors is immediate. But it is not Wellington. If you want a dense cultural life within walking distance, this is not that, and Wellington is ninety minutes away for the nights when you want it. Can I buy a house? Yes, and that is the single strongest argument for this city.

chunks.t: Why Palmerston North: the case for Palmy
chunks.h: The six things people ask us
chunks.x: On a clinical salary, buying in a good suburb within a couple of years is achievable here. Cost of living is specific about it. How bad is the wind? Real, and part of the local identity rather than a secret. Most days it is a breeze off the plain; a handful of days a year it is strong. People who have moved from Wellington find it mild by comparison. People who have moved from inland Europe notice it for a season and then stop. Is it a good place with children? Excellent, and it is why a lot of clinical families end up here. Space, short commutes, a full range of schooling, sport everywhere, safety, and enough money left at the end of the month to do things. Popular schools are zoned, so check the exact address before you sign. Is it international enough? More than the size suggests, thanks to Massey and to a health workforce that has recruited overseas for years.

chunks.t: Why Palmerston North: the case for Palmy
chunks.h: The six things people ask us
chunks.x: There are established Indian, Filipino and Pacific communities, places of worship across faiths, and you will not be the only international clinician on your ward. It is still a small city, so check what specifically matters to you.

chunks.t: Why Palmerston North: the case for Palmy
chunks.x: You want a beach There is coast half an hour west, but it is wild dune coast, not a swimming beach culture. If daily sea swimming is the dream, the Bay of Plenty or Northland deliver it and this does not. Your specialty needs tertiary volume Neurosurgery, cardiothoracics and the most complex work go to Wellington. If you need those volumes, you need a tertiary centre. You want a city that feels like a city Palmerston North is pleasant, green and functional rather than beautiful or buzzing. If the look and feel of where you live matters a great deal to you, weigh that carefully. You need frequent international flights Domestic flights are easy; long-haul means Auckland or Wellington first. It is a longer travel day than from a main centre. You want warmth This is the temperate lower North Island: proper frosts, cool grey stretches, and snow on the ranges.

chunks.t: Why Palmerston North: the case for Palmy
chunks.x: Lovely if you like seasons, wearing if you were hoping for subtropical. Where we’d steer you instead Want the culture and the coffee, and can absorb the housing cost? Wellington , ninety minutes south. Want similar value with a tertiary hospital? Waikato . Want warmth and a beach lifestyle? Hawke’s Bay or Bay of Plenty — both cost more. In our experience Palmy suits clinicians doing the maths — the gap between salary and costs is wider here than almost anywhere in the North Island, and the ten-minute commute quietly returns you a working week every year. Nobody moves for the skyline; plenty stay for the life. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Cost of living in Perth: what a clinical salary buys
chunks.x: Perth sits comfortably below Sydney and Melbourne on housing, close to Brisbane, and above Adelaide. The two things that make it different from every other Australian city are the resources cycle, which moves rents faster here than elsewhere, and the cost of the flights home.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Perth: what a clinical salary buys
chunks.x: We used to print a weekly rent and a monthly budget table here. We have taken them out. A figure that was true when a page was written is misleading a year later, and a candidate who plans a move around a stale number is worse off than one who plans around none. What does not go stale is the shape of a month, and the judgement about which lines will surprise you. For today’s actual numbers use the calculators at the foot of the page, and use them to compare Perth against the city you are leaving. That is the only comparison that decides anything.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Perth: what a clinical salary buys
chunks.x: Below Sydney and Melbourne on housing, clearly Cyclical Rents move with the resources industry Flights The line that separates Perth from every other capital The structural point: a family house within twenty minutes of a tertiary campus is an achievable plan here, which is true of very few Australian cities and untrue of Sydney entirely.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Perth: what a clinical salary buys
chunks.x: Where a month goes The proportions, for one person on a mid-range budget. Proportions move slowly; prices move every quarter. Rent takes just under sixty per cent — comfortably below Sydney and Melbourne, close to Brisbane, above Adelaide. Rent 56% Groceries 18% Power & water 9% Entertainment 9% Transport (SmartRider or fuel) 6% Internet 3% The line that decides it Rent · 56% Two things make this budget different from every other Australian city, and neither is on the chart: the resources cycle, which moves rents faster here than elsewhere, and the cost of the flights home. New-build townhouses — increasingly common across the middle suburbs.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Perth: what a clinical salary buys
chunks.h: The costs that are specific to Perth
chunks.x: Flights home This is the hard one. Five hours to the east coast at east-coast-international prices, and long-haul to anywhere else. Two or three trips a year is what most families settle on — budget for it properly, because it is the tax on living here. Summer cooling Months of dry heat means real air-conditioning use, and the further inland you live the more of it. A well-shaded home with the sea breeze does a lot of the work for free. Groceries carry the distance Perth is a long way from the eastern food supply chains, and some items cost noticeably more. Local produce, on the other hand, is excellent and well priced.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Perth: what a clinical salary buys
chunks.x: Housing is the main one, and the commute is the second: shorter travel times mean less fuel, less childcare and more of your day. There are effectively no toll roads in the state. And the best of Perth is free — nineteen beaches, Kings Park, the river paths and the sunsets cost nothing at all, which is why people here spend less on entertainment than their eastern equivalents and enjoy their weekends more. On the income side, public-health and not-for-profit roles here can salary-package part of your pay before tax — ask payroll on day one. How packaging, tax and superannuation work is national and lives in Pay & conditions . The bottom line Plan the bridge as well as the destination: temporary accommodation, a bond of up to four weeks’ rent plus rent in advance, a car, and setting up a home for a hot summer.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Perth: what a clinical salary buys
chunks.x: Then add the line most people leave out — two or three flights a year to see the people you left behind. Get today’s numbers, and compare them to home These are live and updated continuously. Put the city you are leaving in the other box. Numbeo cost-of-living calculator — the most complete comparison tool, and the one most clinicians already use. Crowd-sourced, so treat it as a ballpark. Expatistan — the same idea with a cleaner side-by-side. Worth running as a sanity check when Numbeo looks off. Australian Bureau of Statistics — official and slower, and the one to trust on the direction of travel. If what you find differs from what we say here, tell us and we will correct it. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Perth
chunks.x: Perth’s food culture surprises people who arrive expecting a quiet city. Two decades of small-bar reform, a strong South-East Asian influence, wine country twenty-five minutes from the CBD, and the freshest seafood in the country have produced something good — and much of it is eaten outdoors at sunset.

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Perth
chunks.x: Fremantle Markets on the weekend is the institution: produce, makers, buskers and the crowd, in a Victorian market hall. Subiaco, Canning Vale and the growers’ markets around the city do the serious shopping, and the local produce — particularly the seafood, the stone fruit and the south-west beef — is exceptional and locally priced. For the rest: the national supermarkets everywhere, ALDI for the cheap basket, and excellent independent grocers and fishmongers throughout the coastal and inner suburbs. Perth’s isolation means some imported items cost more; its local supply means the fresh food is better than most Australians realise. The sundowner A drink facing the ocean as the sun goes down. Perth is the only Australian capital whose sunset is over water, and the city organises around it.

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Perth
chunks.x: Northbridge The city’s Asian food quarter — Vietnamese, Malaysian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean — plus most of the small-bar scene. The Swan Valley Twenty-five minutes from the CBD: cellar doors, breweries, chocolate and produce. The shortest trip to wine country of any Australian capital. Seafood Western rock lobster, snapper, dhufish and prawns, landed locally. Fish and chips at the Fremantle fishing boat harbour is the classic first weekend.

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Perth
chunks.x: Perth’s migration history is distinctive: large British and Irish communities, one of the biggest South African populations in the country, long-established Italian and Greek families, and substantial Malaysian, Singaporean, Vietnamese and Indian communities drawn partly by the shared time zone and short flights. The practical result is that halal butchers, Asian supermarkets, South African stores and British import shops are all easy to find, particularly in Northbridge, Cannington, Morley and Willetton. For newcomers this matters beyond ingredients — those shops sit alongside the clubs, places of worship and community associations that make a distant city feel like home faster. If you are arriving from the UK or South Africa in particular, you will find an established community waiting.

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Perth
chunks.x: Perth lives outdoors and early, like most hot-climate cities: swims before work, coffee after, barbecues in the foreshore parks with free gas, and dinner outside for most of the year. Winter barely interrupts it. The calendar runs on the Perth Festival in February and March, the Fringe World festival, Sculpture by the Sea at Cottesloe, and a sporting schedule centred on Australian rules football, which is close to a civic religion here. The bakery pie — the everyday lunch, in every suburb The everyday, in one list Fremantle Markets on the weekend; growers’ markets for the serious shop. Northbridge for Asian food and small bars; the Swan Valley for a Sunday. Buy the local seafood. It is the best value fresh food in the country. Learn the word sundowner, and where your nearest west-facing beach is. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Perth at a glance: the coastal plain, the seasons and the clock
chunks.x: Before the practical chapters, orientation. Perth is unusually simple to read: a long, narrow city on a coastal plain, organised by the ocean on one side, the river through the middle, and the Darling Scarp rising behind it.

chunks.t: Perth at a glance: the coastal plain, the seasons and the clock
chunks.h: How the city is laid out
chunks.x: Where Perth sits, with the straight-line distance to Mandurah

chunks.t: Perth at a glance: the coastal plain, the seasons and the clock
chunks.x: The Swan River — Derbarl Yerrigan — widens through the middle of the city, and the CBD sits on its northern bank with Kings Park on the escarpment above. South Perth faces it across the water; Elizabeth Quay and the foreshore have reconnected the centre to the river over the past decade. The main tertiary hospital campuses sit close in, on both sides of the river.

chunks.t: Perth at a glance: the coastal plain, the seasons and the clock
chunks.x: North and south of the river mouth, the beach suburbs run for a hundred kilometres: Cottesloe, Scarborough, Trigg and City Beach in the middle, Hillarys and Sorrento further north, Fremantle at the river mouth with its port, its heritage buildings and its own distinct identity. The sea breeze reaches these suburbs first, which is why they cost more.

chunks.t: Perth at a glance: the coastal plain, the seasons and the clock
chunks.x: East of the coast the plain runs flat for twenty kilometres before rising into the Perth Hills at Kalamunda and Mundaring — cooler, greener, semi-rural and popular with families who want space. Between them sit the middle suburbs and the eastern corridor toward the airport, plus the Swan Valley’s vineyards twenty-five minutes from the city.

chunks.t: Perth at a glance: the coastal plain, the seasons and the clock
chunks.x: Hot, dry summers and mild, green winters — the same pattern as southern Europe, and the reason the wine regions work. Summer runs long and cloudless with serious heat, softened on the coast by the afternoon sea breeze known as the Fremantle Doctor. Winter is short, wet and mild; you will want a jacket, rarely a coat. Spring brings the wildflowers the state is famous for. Summer Dec – Feb 18–32° Dry heat · fire season Autumn Mar – May 14–27° Warm sea · the best months Winter Jun – Aug 8–19° Mild, green, wet Spring Sep – Nov 11–25° Wildflowers · warming up Two practical notes. Air conditioning is essential inland and useful everywhere — the difference between a coastal suburb with the sea breeze and one twenty kilometres east is several degrees on a summer afternoon. And take the fire season seriously in the hills and on the urban fringe; the warnings are precise and worth following.

chunks.t: Perth at a glance: the coastal plain, the seasons and the clock
chunks.h: The clock, and the flight map
chunks.x: Western Australia runs on UTC+8 with no daylight saving — two hours behind Sydney in winter and three in summer, which makes east-coast meetings and family calls a daily consideration. The upside is that Perth shares a clock with Singapore, Hong Kong and much of Asia, and flies direct to South-East Asia in around five hours, with direct services to Europe. For clinicians with family in Asia, Africa or the UK, the flight map from Perth is often better than the east coast’s.

chunks.t: Perth at a glance: the coastal plain, the seasons and the clock
chunks.h: Words you’ll hear in week one
chunks.x: Boorloo The Whadjuk Noongar name for the Perth area The Doctor The Fremantle Doctor — the afternoon sea breeze that saves a summer day Freo Fremantle — the port city at the river mouth, and a whole identity of its own SmartRider The tap-on card for trains, buses and ferries Rotto Rottnest Island — bikes, quokkas, and no cars, half an hour by ferry FIFO Fly-in fly-out — the rosters that take workers to the mines and back Over east Everywhere else in Australia. Said the way islanders say "the mainland" Sundowner A drink at sunset, usually facing the ocean. A local institution Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.x: Registration is national; hiring here runs through a small number of metropolitan health services. Perth’s distinguishing features are newer facilities than most of the country and a health system that has recruited internationally for decades — so the process is well-worn rather than exceptional.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.x: Western Australia runs its public system through a set of health service providers: several covering metropolitan Perth — broadly the north, the south and the central and specialist services — plus one covering the entire country and remote area of the state, and a statewide children’s service. Each employs in its own right, and the metropolitan ones each anchor a tertiary campus with a group of secondary and community sites around it. Alongside them sits a substantial private hospital sector, a large private imaging and pathology market, and Aboriginal community-controlled health organisations, which are significant in both the metropolitan area and the regions. Newer facilities Perth built or rebuilt several major hospital campuses relatively recently, so the working environment is often newer than the eastern capitals’ equivalents.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.x: One country service A single service covers the whole vast regional and remote state — one of the largest health service areas in the world by geography. Used to international staff The state has recruited overseas clinicians for decades. Relocation support, orientation and international-graduate pathways are routine here. One national register Ahpra registration works everywhere in Australia. The process, English evidence and assessment live once in Eligibility & registration .

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.h: What that means for a career
chunks.x: Perth gives you a full tertiary system in a city small enough to know quickly. You will meet the people who run your specialty in the state within a year, which cuts both ways: opportunities appear through relationships faster than in a bigger system, and the market is small enough that a very narrow sub-specialty may have only one or two possible employers. Ask us early if that describes you. The most significant structural fact is migration: the whole of Western Australia, Perth included, is classed as regional for skilled migration, which can open visa pathways and points that Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane cannot. For internationally trained clinicians that is a concrete advantage, and it is the reason many people look west first. The detail lives in Visas & the move .

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.h: What that means for a career
chunks.x: Beyond the city, the regional and remote work is unlike anything on the east coast — the Pilbara, the Kimberley, the Goldfields — with strong incentives and broad scope. The Western Australia guide covers that properly. Why people look west, and what it costs them Almost everything distinctive about Perth comes from two facts: the whole state counts as regional for migration, and the clinical market is small. Both columns follow from those, and they are worth reading together rather than one at a time.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.x: Regional for migration — the whole state Perth included. That can open visa pathways and points Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane cannot offer, which for internationally trained clinicians is a concrete advantage rather than a marginal one. Newer facilities Several major campuses were built or rebuilt relatively recently, so the working environment is often newer than the eastern capitals’ equivalents. A system used to international staff The state has recruited overseas clinicians for decades. Relocation support, orientation and international-graduate pathways are routine here, not exceptional. Small enough to know You will meet the people who run your specialty in the state within a year, and opportunities appear through relationships faster than in a bigger system.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.x: Very narrow fields have few doors A highly sub-specialised career may have only one or two possible employers in the state. Worth establishing before you move, not after. The east is a long way away Conference and CPD travel costs more from Perth — which is why it is worth asking explicitly what the CPD budget covers. Country service is part of the picture One service covers the entire regional and remote state. Ask whether rotations are expected of your post, and what they carry in allowances. The migration detail lives in Visas & the move ; the regional and remote work has its own chapter in the Western Australia guide . “ A tertiary system you can know personally, in the one capital city that counts as regional for migration. The one-line version

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.x: Pay follows WA awards and enterprise agreements — we deliberately quote no figures in this guide, and will walk you through the current agreement for your profession instead. What you can pin down at interview: Salary packaging — public-health roles can package part of your pay pre-tax; ask how much and how to start it on day one Which health service and which campus, and whether you may be rostered across sites The roster reality — shift patterns, penalties, on-call frequency and how gaps get covered Relocation support — common here, and worth asking about explicitly CPD — funded time and money, and whether east-coast conference travel is covered (it costs more from Perth) Supervision and support in your first year, especially if you trained overseas Any rural or regional rotation expectations, and what they carry in allowances Professional indemnity — what the employer covers and what

chunks.t: Healthcare in Perth: a newer system that recruits internationally
chunks.x: stays yours Two things to do early Start registration as soon as Perth is on your shortlist — paperwork, not ambition, is what moves start dates. And ask about the regional migration position explicitly: Perth’s classification is a clear advantage over the eastern capitals, so check it before you compare offers. Prefer it on paper? chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Perth: coast, river, inner north and the hills
chunks.x: Perth’s housing decision comes down to one question: how close to the ocean do you need to be? The sea breeze, the beach and the sunset are what people move here for, and they are priced accordingly. Everything else is a variation on that theme. On the map The coast Cottesloe Swanbourne City Beach Scarborough Trigg Sorrento Hillarys River belt & inner north South Perth Applecross Como Nedlands Claremont Subiaco Mount Lawley Highgate Leederville North Perth Fremantle & the south Fremantle South Fremantle Beaconsfield White Gum Valley Coogee Rockingham The hills Kalamunda Mundaring Parks & nature Beaches Landmarks Shaded areas are the suburbs named in this chapter. chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Perth: coast, river, inner north and the hills
chunks.x: Cottesloe, Swanbourne and City Beach are the established western-suburbs addresses: white sand at the end of the street, the Fremantle Doctor first, and prices to match. North through Scarborough, Trigg and Sorrento the same coast becomes more affordable and more family-shaped, with newer housing and surf-lifesaving clubs. This is where a great many clinicians end up, and where a twenty-minute drive to a tertiary campus is normal.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Perth: coast, river, inner north and the hills
chunks.h: The river belt and the inner north
chunks.x: Along the Swan — South Perth, Applecross, Como, Nedlands and Claremont — you get river views, established trees, excellent schools and quick access to the central hospital campuses. North of the CBD, Mount Lawley, Highgate, Leederville and North Perth are the character suburbs: 1920s bungalows, café strips, and the closest thing Perth has to inner-city life. Subiaco — federation-era character, ten minutes from the city. And what the back of one often looks like.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Perth: coast, river, inner north and the hills
chunks.x: Fremantle is a distinct proposition — a working port with limestone heritage buildings, markets, pubs, an arts scene and a strongly independent character. Around it, South Fremantle, Beaconsfield and White Gum Valley have become the west’s most characterful and least suburban pocket, with the southern hospital campuses close by. Further south the coast continues through Coogee and Rockingham toward Mandurah, an hour out and served by the southern rail line.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Perth: coast, river, inner north and the hills
chunks.x: Kalamunda, Mundaring and the Perth Hills give you semi-rural life, cooler air, real trees and space — thirty to forty minutes from the city, with the fire-season responsibilities that come with living on a bush fringe. In the other direction, the northern and southern growth corridors along the rail lines offer the newest and most affordable family housing in the metropolitan area, with their own hospitals and a longer but rail-served commute.
