chunks.t: Healthcare in South Australia: how the system works for clinicians
chunks.x: Registration is national; hiring is local. This chapter explains how South Australia organises its public system, where the work is, and what to ask before you sign — without naming employers, because our job is to be useful before it is to be promotional.

chunks.t: Healthcare in South Australia: how the system works for clinicians
chunks.h: How the state system is organised
chunks.x: SA Health runs the public system through ten local health networks: three metropolitan networks covering the centre, north and south of Adelaide, six country networks covering the regions, and one statewide women’s and children’s service. Each network hires in its own right — so “a job in SA” is really a job in one network’s geography, and moving between them later is a fresh application, not a transfer. Alongside the public networks sit a substantial private and not-for-profit hospital sector concentrated in Adelaide, a state ambulance service, and Aboriginal community-controlled health organisations that are significant employers and partners, particularly in the country networks and the far north.

chunks.t: Healthcare in South Australia: how the system works for clinicians
chunks.h: How the state system is organised
chunks.x: Three metro networks Central, northern and southern Adelaide — each anchored by a major teaching hospital, with the city’s western boulevard now holding one of the newest hospital-and-research precincts in the southern hemisphere. Six country networks The Limestone Coast, the river country, the Barossa-Hills-Fleurieu ring, the Yorke and mid-north, the Eyre and far north, and the Flinders and upper gulf — each with its own referral hospitals and community sites. A statewide children’s service Paediatric and maternity specialist care runs as its own network, serving the whole state from the capital with outreach into the regions.

chunks.t: Healthcare in South Australia: how the system works for clinicians
chunks.x: Tertiary and quaternary medicine concentrates in Adelaide, which for its size carries a deep hospital system — including the state’s major trauma capacity and its teaching, research and specialist services. The city’s north is the growth corridor, where demand has risen fastest; the south pairs a large university-linked hospital campus with an expanding outer-suburban population. In the country networks, referral hospitals in the South-East and on the gulfs anchor broad-scope roles: generalist skills are prized, waits for the niche are traded for breadth and responsibility, and posts frequently carry relocation support, accommodation help and retention incentives that a city advertisement won’t show. The far north runs on small resident teams, visiting specialists, aviation and telehealth — demanding, distinctive work that suits experienced clinicians who want their scope wide.

chunks.t: Healthcare in South Australia: how the system works for clinicians
chunks.x: One structural advantage worth repeating: the whole of South Australia — Adelaide included — is classed as regional for skilled migration, which can open extra visa pathways and points. The detail lives in Visas & the move . One register, ten employers 10 Local health networks, one national register Named below, and each hires in its own right — so a move between them later is a fresh application rather than a transfer. That makes your first choice the consequential one, and worth making deliberately rather than by whichever advertisement you saw first. Your registration, by contrast, moves with you anywhere in Australia. The process, English evidence and assessment pathways live once in Eligibility & registration . “ Registration is national. Hiring is network by network. Plan for both. The one-line version

chunks.t: Healthcare in South Australia: how the system works for clinicians
chunks.x: Pay here follows state enterprise agreements that differ from the east coast’s — we deliberately quote no figures in this guide, and will always walk you through the current agreement for your profession instead. What you can pin down at interview: Salary packaging — public-health roles can package part of your pay pre-tax; ask how much and how to start it on day one The roster: shift patterns, penalties, on-call frequency and how rosters are built Public, private or both — many SA careers mix the two; ask what rights of private practice exist CPD — how much funded time and money, and whether interstate conference travel counts Supervision and support — especially for internationally trained clinicians in your first year Parking and commute at your shift times — easy by east-coast standards, still worth confirming For country posts: the incentive package — relocation, housing, retention

chunks.t: Healthcare in South Australia: how the system works for clinicians
chunks.x: payments and leave for city travel Professional indemnity — what the employer covers and what remains yours to hold Two things to do early Start registration as soon as SA is on your shortlist — paperwork, not ambition, is what moves start dates. And once you land, arrange ambulance cover: it is not automatic in South Australia, and a state ambulance membership or insurance add-on is inexpensive insurance against a very expensive ride. chunks.t: Where clinicians live in South Australia: Adelaide’s villages to the country posts
chunks.x: Adelaide is small enough that this decision is forgiving — get it slightly wrong and you’re still twenty minutes from work. But the choice between the city’s villages, the Hills and a country post is a decision of a different kind, so here is the map as we’d draw it over coffee.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in South Australia: Adelaide’s villages to the country posts
chunks.x: North Adelaide, Prospect, Unley, Norwood, Goodwood: bluestone villas and cottages on tree-lined streets, cafés on the corner, the parklands between you and the wards. This is where many hospital staff start — walkable, characterful, close to everything — and where rents run highest, though “highest” here would read as ordinary in Sydney. Apartments in the CBD itself suit short first leases while you learn the city.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in South Australia: Adelaide’s villages to the country posts
chunks.x: Glenelg, and the beach suburbs running north through Brighton, Somerton, Henley and Grange, give Adelaide something rare among capitals: sand at the end of a tram line, with city hospitals a straightforward ride away. Sunsets over the gulf, esplanade coffee, jetty swims before a late shift. Summer weekends get busy and parking with them; that is the whole complaint.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in South Australia: Adelaide’s villages to the country posts
chunks.h: The Hills and the wine valleys
chunks.x: Stirling, Aldgate and Crafers sit in hill country — cooler, greener, autumn colour, a Sunday-morning fog — twenty to thirty minutes up the freeway from town. Further out, Mount Barker is one of the fastest-growing towns in the state and noticeably better value; the Barossa’s towns (Tanunda, Nuriootpa, Angaston) and the Fleurieu’s (Willunga, Victor Harbor) offer village life with vines, served by their own regional health sites and within reach of the city’s. The trade: you will drive, and on summer fire-danger days you’ll live by the warnings like everyone else.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in South Australia: Adelaide’s villages to the country posts
chunks.x: The state’s largest regional city sits in the green South-East, four and a half hours from Adelaide near the Victorian border — around thirty thousand people, a proper referral hospital, forests and famously blue crater lakes, and Melbourne nearer than Adelaide. The Riverland towns — Renmark, Berri, Loxton — hold some of the most affordable housing in the state, two to three hours from the city along the Murray. On the gulfs, Whyalla and Port Augusta anchor a region betting big on steel and hydrogen, and Port Lincoln faces the Southern Ocean across seafood country, a seven-hour drive or fifty-minute flight from town. These are real communities with real hospitals and the strongest incentives in the state — and they are far away, with fewer specialist and schooling options. The clinicians who thrive in them wanted breadth and belonging, not a smaller Adelaide. Say the hard thing early: if what you want is the city with a discount, choose the outer suburbs instead.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in South Australia: Adelaide’s villages to the country posts
chunks.x: ~A$560 /wk Indicative Adelaide house rent (3-bed median) Less Again in the regional centres — among Australia’s cheapest housing 4 wks Maximum bond, plus up to two weeks’ rent in advance If you want… Consider Because The widest job market Adelaide’s inner ring Every tertiary site within half an hour Beach life on a roster Glenelg to Grange The tram and the coast road do the commute Space and a garden Mount Barker & the Hills Value, schools, freeway access — bring a car Village-and-vines life Barossa & Fleurieu towns Regional sites nearby, the city an hour away A green regional city The South-East The state’s biggest regional hub, mildest weather Maximum affordability The Riverland River-country housing at country prices Wide scope & wild coast The gulfs & Eyre Broad roles, strong incentives, real remoteness Renting itself — applications, bonds, rights, the documents that win a tight mark

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in South Australia: Adelaide’s villages to the country posts
chunks.x: et — works the same across Australia and lives once in Living in Australia . The one SA-specific habit worth copying: arrive with your references, proof of income and offer letter as clean PDFs; a complete same-day application regularly beats a longer local history. Before you sign a lease Is the property inside the school zone you need? Zones run street by street here. How long is the commute at your actual shift times — and is there parking at both ends? Does the home have decent cooling and heating? Older stock often doesn’t. Would a short-term rental first be wiser? Most people re-choose their suburb once they know the city. Prefer it on paper? chunks.t: Getting around South Australia: the 20-minute city and the long roads
chunks.x: Adelaide’s transport story is mostly the absence of pain: no toll roads anywhere in the state, some of the shortest commutes of any Australian capital, and an airport fifteen minutes from the office. Beyond the metro map, the state is big and the car comes back.

chunks.t: Getting around South Australia: the 20-minute city and the long roads
chunks.x: metroCARD Trains, trams and buses run on one tap-on card — or just a contactless bank card. Simple, and cheap by east-coast standards. The tram One line, but the right one: free through the city centre, then out to the beach at Glenelg. It makes the coast a commute, not an outing. Trains Suburban lines reach the coast, the northern growth corridor and the south. Small network, reliable timetable. The O-Bahn Adelaide’s oddity: buses on a guided concrete track to the north-east — one of the fastest suburban runs in the country. Living car-free is practical along the tram corridor, in the inner ring and near a train line. It stops being practical in the Hills, the wine valleys and anywhere regional — plan on a car for those from day one.

chunks.t: Getting around South Australia: the 20-minute city and the long roads
chunks.x: Australians drive on the left, and Adelaide is the easiest capital to learn in: a flat grid, ring routes, no tolls, and rush hours that would make a Sydneysider laugh. You can usually drive on a valid overseas licence for a period after arriving, then transfer to a South Australian licence once you’re resident — the rules, and buying a car, live in Living in Australia . Two local notes. The power poles are concrete-and-steel stobie poles — unforgiving, which is partly why SA drivers treat them with respect. And country driving is its own skill: long distances, wildlife at dawn and dusk, and fuel stops you plan rather than assume, especially on the Eyre Peninsula and north of the gulfs.

chunks.t: Getting around South Australia: the 20-minute city and the long roads
chunks.x: From Adelaide to… By road Otherwise The Barossa ~1 hr Day-tour territory Clare Valley ~2 hrs — The Riverland 2.5–3 hrs — Whyalla & the upper gulf ~4 hrs Short regional flight The South-East ~4.5 hrs Regional flight Port Lincoln ~7 hrs 50-minute flight Kangaroo Island ~2 hrs + ferry 35-minute flight Melbourne ~8 hrs Hourly flights Adelaide Airport flies direct to every capital and a handful of international hubs; regional services cover the flying-distance towns above. If you take a country post, ask about travel allowances in the package — regular trips to the city are a cost and a normal ask. The takeaway In Adelaide, transport will be the least of your problems — pick a home near your work or a tram/train line and the city does the rest. Everywhere else in the state, budget for a reliable car before you budget for anything else. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Weekends in South Australia: wine country, coast & the ranges
chunks.x: The recruiting pitch for South Australia is really a geography lesson: almost everything worth a weekend sits within an hour or two of the city. This chapter is what people do with that — and the festival month the whole year bends around. Beyond the hour, and worth it The wine regions are all inside two hours and covered below. This is the rest of the state, to scale against each other — the trips that need a weekend or a flight, and the reason people who move here keep exploring for years.

chunks.t: Weekends in South Australia: wine country, coast & the ranges
chunks.x: Kangaroo Island Wildlife, wilderness beaches and remarkable food — a ferry, or 35 minutes in the air Ferry or 35 min flight The Limestone Coast World Heritage fossil caves and the crater lakes — one of them impossibly blue each summer ~4 hours Ikara-Flinders Ranges Wilpena Pound and 800 million years of geology in the outback light — the state’s great camping country ~5 hours The Eyre Peninsula Oyster sheds, tuna towns, sea-lion swims and Southern Ocean cliffs — the serious ocean Short flight, or a road trip Indicative driving times; the two flight options are why South Australians treat the island and the west coast as long weekends rather than annual leave. The Riverland and the Coorong sit between these, a couple of hours east.

chunks.t: Weekends in South Australia: wine country, coast & the ranges
chunks.x: Four of the world’s best-known wine regions ring the capital. The Barossa and the Adelaide Hills are inside an hour; McLaren Vale is forty minutes down the coast, where the vines run almost to the sea; the Clare Valley sits within two, its old railway now the Riesling Trail for a day’s cycling between cellar doors. The practical effect: a long cellar-door lunch is a normal Saturday, not an anniversary. Vintage, in autumn, is the prettiest time to live here.

chunks.t: Weekends in South Australia: wine country, coast & the ranges
chunks.x: The city’s own thirty kilometres of beach handle the everyday — jetty swims, esplanade runs, gulf sunsets that make the local news. Weekends stretch to the Fleurieu’s surf and coves, and to Kangaroo Island — a ferry or a 35-minute flight — for wildlife, wilderness beaches and remarkable food. Further west, the Eyre Peninsula is the serious ocean: oyster sheds, tuna towns, sea-lion swims and Southern Ocean cliffs, a short flight or a proper road trip away.

chunks.t: Weekends in South Australia: wine country, coast & the ranges
chunks.x: North of the vines the land climbs into the Flinders Ranges — Ikara-Flinders Ranges National Park and the vast natural amphitheatre of Wilpena Pound, some 800 million years of geology standing in the outback light. It is the state’s great camping and walking country, five hours up the road and worth every one. East, the Murray winds through the Riverland: houseboats, river red gums and the birdlife of the Coorong’s lagoons where the river meets the sea. South-east again, the Limestone Coast hides World Heritage fossil caves and the crater lakes — one famously, impossibly blue each summer.

chunks.t: Weekends in South Australia: wine country, coast & the ranges
chunks.x: Mad March The Fringe — the southern hemisphere’s biggest arts festival — plus the Adelaide Festival, WOMADelaide and the motorsport, all at once. The city doubles in energy for a month. Winter Illuminate lights up the city in July; the Hills do log fires and galleries; the footy fills the oval — and the Showdown derby splits every workplace in two. Spring & vintage Tasting Australia in autumn, jacarandas and show season in spring, and harvest turning the valleys gold twice a year.

chunks.t: Weekends in South Australia: wine country, coast & the ranges
chunks.x: Barossa cellar doors and a bakery crawl through Tanunda and Angaston McLaren Vale long lunch, then d’Arenberg’s coast road home via Sellicks The Riesling Trail by bike through the Clare Valley Kangaroo Island — Remarkable Rocks, sea lions and the island’s produce Wilpena Pound and the Flinders Ranges under outback stars Hahndorf and the Adelaide Hills lookouts, fog and all A houseboat weekend on the Murray from the Riverland towns The Coorong’s lagoons and the mouth of the great river Port Lincoln — oysters where they grow, and a swim with the sea lions Mad March: one Fringe show, one Festival night, one WOMADelaide afternoon Eyre Peninsula oysters, eaten close to where they grow That’s the guide Nine chapters on South Australia. chunks.t: Moving to South Australia: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: South Australia is the state where the arithmetic works: a major-hospital career in the most affordable mainland capital, with the hills twenty minutes from the wards, the sea forty, and world-famous wine country under an hour. It asks one thing in return — that you like your city elegant and unhurried rather than enormous.

chunks.t: Moving to South Australia: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: An easy, elegant capital — and a state beyond it
chunks.x: Adelaide holds about 1.4 million people — three-quarters of the state — on a grid Colonel Light laid out in 1836, ringed completely by parklands. It is Australia’s festival city: every March the Fringe, the Festival and WOMADelaide turn the whole centre into a stage, and for the rest of the year it runs on markets, laneway bars and cellar-door weekends. The health system is big for the city’s size, with one of the newest hospital-and-research precincts in the southern hemisphere along its main boulevard. Beyond the city the state changes register.

chunks.t: Moving to South Australia: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: An easy, elegant capital — and a state beyond it
chunks.x: The Adelaide Hills, the Barossa and the Clare Valley wrap the capital in vines and stone villages; the green South-East runs to the Victorian border around the state’s largest regional city; the Riverland follows the Murray through fruit and wine country; and the gulf towns and the Eyre Peninsula face some of the wildest coast in the country, with the Flinders Ranges and the outback beyond. The costs are a fierce, dry summer with real 40-degree runs, power bills among the dearest in the country, and a job market that is one city deep — most of the state’s medicine happens in Adelaide, and the regional centres are regional. This guide prices all three plainly. Who wrote this Ethicare is a healthcare recruitment company. This guide is free to read, asks nothing of you, and does not give visa advice. South Australia is where the money and the life line up best of the mainland states, and also where “will the job market fit me?” needs the most careful answer. Where we think it’s the wrong state for you, we say so.

chunks.t: Moving to South Australia: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: ~1.85M People in the state — about the population of Perth, spread across an area four times the size of the UK. ~1.4M In Greater Adelaide — roughly three in four South Australians live in or around the capital. 10 Local health networks — three metropolitan, six country, and a statewide women’s and children’s service. ~50% Of Australia’s wine is made here — the Barossa, Clare, McLaren Vale and the Hills all sit within about an hour of the city. ~30 km Of white-sand metropolitan beach, from North Haven down to Sellicks — with a tram to the middle of it. 20 min From the city to the Adelaide Hills. The sea is about forty. This is the “20-minute city” people talk about. UTC+9½ The half-hour time zone — thirty minutes behind Sydney and Melbourne, with daylight saving in summer. 1836 Founded as a planned free settlement — no convicts, a fact locals will mention — and a haven for religious dissenters. 10c Per can and bottle — the container deposit has run since 1977, and returning them is a local habit.

chunks.t: Moving to South Australia: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: The half-hour clock is real SA runs thirty minutes behind the east coast. National meetings land at odd times, football starts at half past, and every newcomer misses one call in their first month. Summer is dry and serious Heatwaves run past 40° for days, then break with a cool change off the Southern Ocean you can feel arrive. A good split system is infrastructure, not comfort. Power bills bite SA electricity is among the dearest in the country. An efficient home and a carefully chosen energy plan matter more here than almost anywhere in Australia. Mad March is a season The Fringe — the biggest arts festival in the southern hemisphere — the Festival, WOMADelaide and the motorsport all land at once. Book nothing else for March. It’s a two-degrees city “Which school did you go to?” is an Adelaide icebreaker.

chunks.t: Moving to South Australia: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: Everyone seems to know everyone — which makes reputations, good and bad, travel fast. The deli is an institution The corner deli — part milk bar, part grocer — survives here as it does nowhere else, along with Foodland, the fiercely local supermarket. A note on Country Adelaide stands on Kaurna Country — Tarntanya, the place of the red kangaroo — and the state spans many nations: Peramangk in the Hills, Ngadjuri in the mid-north, Boandik in the South-East, Barngarla on the upper gulf, Erawirung along the river. You’ll see dual naming used widely and warmly. Acknowledgement of Country opens meetings, and health services work in partnership with Aboriginal community-controlled organisations. Take the cultural induction seriously — in the far north it is central to the job.

chunks.t: Moving to South Australia: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Nine chapters, all of them about South Australia specifically. Anything true of Australia generally — Medicare, visas, Ahpra registration, tax, superannuation, schools — lives once in Moving to Australia . If you read nothing else, read Why South Australia for the full case — and what we’d ask you to weigh, and Where clinicians live , because Adelaide’s villages and the country posts are decisions of a completely different kind. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Why South Australia: the case for the festival state
chunks.x: Every state has a brochure. This chapter is the conversation we’d have instead: what South Australia gives a working clinician, what a week here plausibly looks like, and who we’d point somewhere else.

chunks.t: Why South Australia: the case for the festival state
chunks.x: Start with the sum most people never quite write down. Adelaide is the most affordable mainland capital: a three-bedroom family house rents for hundreds of dollars a week less than its Sydney equivalent, and buying one is an achievable mid-career plan. There are no toll roads anywhere in the state, commutes are among the shortest of any Australian capital, and the whole of South Australia is classed as regional for skilled migration — which can mean extra visa points and pathways the east-coast capitals can’t offer. Against that, salaries sit broadly in the national range for public health — the enterprise agreements differ state by state, and we’ll always walk you through the current ones rather than quote figures here. The point isn’t that you earn dramatically more in SA. It’s that the same career buys noticeably more life. $0 Toll roads in the state <1 hr To the Barossa, the Vale or the Hills 100% Of SA counts as regional for migration

chunks.t: Why South Australia: the case for the festival state
chunks.x: A week here can plausibly hold all of this. A city-hospital shift that starts without a toll-road crawl, because most of Adelaide is twenty-odd minutes from most of the rest of it. A swim at Henley or Brighton before a late start — the sea sits at the end of the tram line. A Thursday-evening shop at the Central Market, where the produce is better and cheaper than any supermarket. Saturday lunch at a McLaren Vale cellar door, forty minutes south, and Sunday on the Heysen Trail in the Hills before the working week resets. None of that is a holiday itinerary. It’s the ordinary shape of a week when a city this liveable is also this small — and it is exactly what people mean when they say their salary “goes further” here. The distance between your roster and your life shrinks. Sophie’s insight What I love most about South Australia is how much life it offers for the money.

chunks.t: Why South Australia: the case for the festival state
chunks.x: Having spent years in the NHS, I know how easily work can take over — and what stands out in Adelaide is how close everything is. The hills, the sea and the vines are all a short drive away, and people make time for them. My advice: think about your commute, your community and what you’ll do on your days off. Those things shape your happiness more than people expect. Sophie Careem Founder & CEO, Ethicare Resourcing

chunks.t: Why South Australia: the case for the festival state
chunks.h: When we’d suggest a bigger market
chunks.x: The market is one city deep Most of the state’s medicine happens in Adelaide. It carries fewer tertiary sites than Sydney, Melbourne or Brisbane, so a narrow sub-specialty may simply have more room on the east coast. Summer is fierce Dry heat, 40-degree runs, and a long brown February. If you wilt in heat and can’t love an early-morning life for two months a year, think hard. It’s a quiet city Adelaide is elegant, not electric. If what recharges you is big-city churn — new restaurants weekly, a giant professional scene — Melbourne or Sydney will fit better. The east coast is a flight away Melbourne is eight hours’ drive, Sydney fourteen. If your family network lands in the eastern capitals, every visit means a flight. The regions are regional The South-East, the Riverland and the gulf towns are hours from the capital, with the specialist and schooling limits that brings.

chunks.t: Why South Australia: the case for the festival state
chunks.h: When we’d suggest a bigger market
chunks.x: Rewarding — but go in with open eyes. Where we’d steer you instead If you need a second tertiary city within driving distance, look at Victoria — Melbourne plus a ring of strong regional centres. If winter sun is the whole point, Queensland is the answer — SA winters are cool and green. If you want scale and don’t mind paying for it, New South Wales carries the country’s biggest health system. In our experience South Australia suits clinicians who’ve stopped equating bigger with better — the market is one city deep, but that city gives back its evenings and weekends like nowhere else. If your sub-specialty fits, the life here is very hard to argue with. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Cost of living in Southland: the cheapest city in New Zealand
chunks.x: Invercargill has the lowest house prices of any city in New Zealand, and it is not a narrow lead. On a clinical salary that is not a small convenience — it changes what your money is for.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Southland: the cheapest city in New Zealand
chunks.x: We used to print a weekly rent and a monthly budget table here. We have taken them out. A figure that was true when a page was written is misleading a year later, and a candidate who plans a move around a stale number is worse off than one who plans around none. What does not go stale is the shape of a month, and the judgement about which lines will surprise you. For today’s actual numbers use the calculators at the foot of the page, and use them to compare Southland against the city you are leaving. That is the only comparison that decides anything.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Southland: the cheapest city in New Zealand
chunks.x: Clinical pay is national. You arrive on the same salary you would earn in Auckland, Queenstown or Wellington, into the country’s cheapest housing market. There is no regional adjustment downward: you simply keep more of it. Put concretely: a large four-bedroom family home on a proper section, ten minutes from the hospital, in a well-regarded school zone, costs a fraction of a modest apartment in Queenstown two hours north. Most clinicians we place in Southland buy within their first year or two, rather than renting for a decade while they save. What that buys beyond the house is the interesting part. Clinicians here tend to travel more, work fewer extra shifts, and reach financial decisions years earlier than colleagues on identical pay elsewhere. That is the real proposition, and the weather is the price of it.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Southland: the cheapest city in New Zealand
chunks.x: Waikiwi, Grasmere & Windsor The city’s more sought-after family suburbs, and still modest by national standards. Where most relocating clinical families start. Avenal & Gladstone Character housing near Queens Park. Lovely streets, older homes — check the insulation carefully. Rosedale & Newfield The best value in an already cheap city. Straightforward family housing at prices that surprise everyone arriving from overseas. Otatara Lifestyle blocks in native bush, ten minutes out. Land and trees for a fraction of what they’d cost anywhere north. Bluff, Riverton & Winton Cheaper again, and coastal or rural with it. Riverton has firmed up as people discover it; Bluff remains the region’s bargain. Te Anau The exception. Tourism demand and limited stock make Fiordland’s gateway town markedly more expensive and tighter than the rest of the region.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Southland: the cheapest city in New Zealand
chunks.x: Where a month goes The proportions, for one person on a mid-range budget. Proportions move slowly; prices move every quarter. Rent is forty-five per cent of it — the smallest share of any region in this collection. Rent 45% Groceries 20% Car — petrol, insurance, running 11% Power & water (winter-weighted) 10% Entertainment & leisure 9% Internet 4% Mobile phone plan 2% The line that decides it Rent · 45% Two lines run higher than the national pattern: winter power, and a car you will need. They still do not come close to closing the gap the rent line opens. Indicative prices that change over time. The rent line is the lowest in this collection, and the power line is among the highest — that trade is the whole story.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Southland: the cheapest city in New Zealand
chunks.x: Winter heating The local cost. Cool, damp and dark for a good stretch, so a well-insulated home with proper heating matters. Because houses are cheap, buying one already sorted is within reach. Getting home, and getting out The longest travel day in the collection. If you’ll fly to Europe or South Africa a few times a year, budget properly for it — and factor in the drive to Queenstown. Good outdoor kit A serious coat, boots and layers are not optional here. Nor is the gear if you intend to use Fiordland, which you will. A car, and probably two Essential across the region. The upside is that the money you’re not spending on housing covers it comfortably.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Southland: the cheapest city in New Zealand
chunks.x: Compare cities Numbeo · cost of living Invercargill prices for rent, groceries, transport and dining, against your current city. Crowd-sourced, and the sample is thin for a place this size — treat it as a ballpark, not a quote. Plan your budget Sorted budget planner New Zealand’s free, government-backed budgeting tool. Official data Stats NZ living costs The Household Living-Costs Price Index, updated quarterly. Property realestate.co.nz Current Southland rentals and homes for sale. Compare against your current city and prepare to be surprised. Sanity check Expatistan A cleaner side-by-side of two cities. Worth running when Numbeo looks off. Official rents Tenancy Services market rent Bond-lodgement data by area — the most reliable rent figure in New Zealand. How pay, tax, IRD numbers, KiwiSaver and sending money home work is national, and covered in Money, tax & banking .

chunks.t: Cost of living in Southland: the cheapest city in New Zealand
chunks.x: The summary The cheapest city housing in New Zealand , on national clinical pay, with a base hospital ten minutes away. Most people here buy rather than rent , and sooner than they planned. The costs are winter heating and the distance home — both real, and both smaller than what you’re saving. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Food, shopping and everyday life in Southland
chunks.x: Southland has a stronger food identity than any region in this collection, and almost none of it is fashionable. It comes from the sea, the farms and a hundred and fifty years of Scottish stubbornness, and locals are unembarrassed about all of it.

chunks.t: Food, shopping and everyday life in Southland
chunks.h: What comes out of the water
chunks.x: Bluff oysters are the region’s great annual event. Wild dredge oysters from Foveaux Strait, in season roughly March to August, and by common agreement among the best in the world. There is a festival, there are queues, and there is a whole local calendar built around the opening. Blue cod is the local fish and the correct order at any chippy in the region. Crayfish , pāua and mussels come off the same coast, and tītī — muttonbird — remains a customary harvest on the islands off Rakiura, sold locally in season and an acquired taste that Southlanders are pleased to watch you acquire. And cheese rolls : rolled bread with a cheese and onion-soup filling, grilled. Every café, every fundraiser, every school gala. Do not describe them as a novelty in front of a local.

chunks.t: Food, shopping and everyday life in Southland
chunks.x: Southland is intensively farmed dairy and sheep country, and the produce reflects it. Local lamb and beef, exceptional dairy, and a real culture of home baking and preserving that has survived here better than in the cities. Gore is brown-trout capital and takes that seriously too. The farmers’ markets in Invercargill and Gore cover produce, meat and baking. Between them and the coast you can eat extremely well from within fifty kilometres, and cheaply.

chunks.t: Food, shopping and everyday life in Southland
chunks.x: Invercargill A modest but improving scene — good cafés, a handful of strong restaurants, craft beer, and the best-value eating out in the country. The city centre has been steadily redeveloped. Riverton & Bluff Small coastal spots punching above their weight, particularly for seafood. Where locals take visitors. Te Anau Tourism-facing and better than you’d expect for the size, with prices to match the visitor market. Groceries All the main chains, and prices at or below the national average. Food in New Zealand is expensive by British or Australian standards — that is national, and this is the cheapest place in the country to deal with it. Specialist and imported ingredients are the weak point. There are Asian and Indian grocers in Invercargill and the range is better than the city’s size suggests, but it is narrower than any of the main centres. If a particular cuisine is central to how your family eats, check before you commit — the national chapter Finding your feet & your people covers where to look and which communities are established here.

chunks.t: Food, shopping and everyday life in Southland
chunks.x: Summer is lived outdoors, late Light until nearly ten. Barbecues at nine, cricket, the beach, the estuary. Four months of the year the evenings are enormous. Winter is lived indoors, well Dark and damp, and the region has responded with unusually good indoor facilities for its size — pools, gyms, a velodrome, indoor sport and a strong club culture. Sport and motorsport are the social glue Rugby first, but also netball, cycling, hockey, and a serious motorsport tradition. Joining a club is by far the fastest way to know people properly. Newcomers are noticed, and welcomed A small city that has worked hard to attract people tends to look after the ones who arrive. Southland hospitality is not a marketing line. Limitations Retail is functional. Serious shopping means Dunedin, Christchurch or online, and delivery takes a day or two longer than up north.

chunks.t: Food, shopping and everyday life in Southland
chunks.x: Touring music, theatre and major exhibitions mostly stop at Dunedin or Christchurch. Specialist imported groceries are limited. Most people build up a Dunedin or Christchurch order a few times a year. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Southland at a glance: climate, geography and the long summer light
chunks.x: Southland is a broad, intensely green plain, bounded by mountains to the north-west and a wild ocean to the south. Nothing about it is dramatic until you reach the edges — and then it is as dramatic as anywhere on earth.

chunks.t: Southland at a glance: climate, geography and the long summer light
chunks.x: Where Invercargill sits, with the straight-line distance to Gore and Te Anau The middle of Southland is farmland: the Southland Plains, some of the most productive pasture in the country, running from the Takitimu Mountains down to the sea. Invercargill sits near the southern edge on the Waihōpai River, with the Oreti and New River estuaries beside it and Oreti Beach’s long grey sweep to the west. North-east through the plains is Gore, an hour away, on the Mataura River — a farming and brown-trout town, and the region’s second centre. North-west, past Winton and Lumsden, the land climbs into the Te Anau basin and then into Fiordland : 1.2 million hectares of World Heritage wilderness, glacial sounds, and some of the highest rainfall on the planet. South of the city, Bluff sits on its hill above the strait, and an hour by ferry beyond it is Rakiura — Stewart Island — eighty-five per cent national park, four hundred people, and one of the best places in the world to see kiwi in the wild. East, the coast runs into the Catlins.

chunks.t: Southland at a glance: climate, geography and the long summer light
chunks.x: Summer Dec – Feb 18–22°C Mild, endlessly light Autumn Mar – May 14–18°C Often the best of it Winter Jun – Aug 8–11°C Cool, damp, dark early Spring Sep – Nov 12–16°C Windy. windy Indicative daytime highs. Snow at sea level is uncommon; frost is normal. Inland around Gore and Te Anau the range is wider at both ends.

chunks.t: Southland at a glance: climate, geography and the long summer light
chunks.h: What the numbers don’t tell you
chunks.x: The light is the thing nobody warns you about. At 46 degrees south the summer days are enormous — light from before five in the morning until nearly ten at night around the solstice. It reshapes how you live for four months of the year. The corollary is a dark midwinter, and it is fair to weigh both. It is cool rather than cold. Southland’s reputation is for grimness, but the maritime climate keeps extremes off: it rarely freezes hard and rarely gets hot. What it does do is change quickly, and blow. Locals dress for four seasons in a day and think nothing of it. The wind is constant, and spring is the worst of it. A prevailing westerly straight off the Southern Ocean with nothing between here and Antarctica. You will own a good coat within a fortnight. Houses need to be warm, and increasingly are. The regional housing challenge is heating and damp together.

chunks.t: Southland at a glance: climate, geography and the long summer light
chunks.h: What the numbers don’t tell you
chunks.x: Because homes are cheap here you can afford to buy one that is already well insulated — a clear advantage over the expensive regions. Check the Healthy Homes compliance statement, which is a legal requirement and covered in the national Renting in New Zealand chapter. The aurora australis is real and it is visible. On clear, geomagnetically active nights the southern lights appear over the southern horizon. There are local groups who chase it. Very few inhabited places on earth offer this from the back garden.

chunks.t: Southland at a glance: climate, geography and the long summer light
chunks.h: Where things are, in driving time
chunks.x: Across Invercargill 10 minutes, at any hour of any day. → Bluff 30 minutes south, for the oysters, the ferry and Stirling Point. → Riverton & Oreti Beach 15 to 40 minutes west along the coast. → Gore 1 hour north-east through the plains. → Te Anau & Fiordland 2 hours north-west. Milford Sound is around 4 hours from the city. → Dunedin / Queenstown 2 hr 15 and 2 hr respectively. Christchurch is 6 hours, or an hour in the air.

chunks.t: Southland at a glance: climate, geography and the long summer light
chunks.x: Murihiku Southland in te reo Māori — "the last joint of the tail". Rakiura Stewart Island, across the strait from Bluff. The burr The rolled Southland "r". The only real regional accent in the country. Cheese rolls Grilled rolled bread with a cheese filling. A southern institution, not a joke. Blue cod The local fish, and the correct order at any chippy south of Gore. Bluff oysters Wild dredge oysters, in season roughly March to August. A big local event. Tītī Muttonbird — a customary harvest on the islands off Rakiura. The Stags Southland’s provincial rugby side. Support is not optional. The short version A green farming plain with Fiordland at one end and the Southern Ocean at the other . The climate is cool, changeable and windy — that is the cost, and it is why the housing is the cheapest in the country. In return you get summer evenings that last until ten and wilderness most people see once in a lifetime. Where clinicians live is next. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Healthcare in Southland: working as a clinician
chunks.x: This is the chapter that separates Southland from the other far-south options. Unlike Central Otago, this region has a base hospital — and that single fact changes what a career here can look like.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Southland: working as a clinician
chunks.x: Public hospital and specialist services are delivered by Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora. The base hospital in Invercargill serves the whole region — roughly a hundred thousand people spread over an area larger than Wales — carrying acute medicine and surgery, an emergency department, intensive care, maternity, paediatrics, imaging, and a full outpatient and day-procedure service. Beyond the city, care runs through a rural network: community and district services across the plains, and rural facilities in the northern and western districts serving Gore, the Te Anau basin, Fiordland and Rakiura. Distance is a live clinical factor. Retrieval and transfer — by road, and by air from Te Anau and the island — are a normal part of the working year. Complex and highly specialised work is referred to Dunedin, two and a quarter hours away, and to Christchurch for some tertiary services.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Southland: working as a clinician
chunks.x: That relationship is close and well established. One base hospital, and the country behind it A hundred thousand people spread over an area larger than Wales. The base hospital is what separates Southland from the other far-south options — and the rural network is what makes the work distinctive. The region Acute medicine and surgery, emergency, intensive care, maternity, paediatrics and imaging sit in the city; beyond it, community and district services across the plains, and rural facilities serving the north, the west and the island. Invercargill · the base hospital Gore & the plains Te Anau & Fiordland Rakiura And beyond it Complex and highly specialised work is referred to Dunedin, two and a quarter hours away, with Christchurch used for some tertiary services. That relationship is close and well established. Invercargill Dunedin · 2 hr 15 Retrieval and transfer — by road, and by air from Te Anau and the island — are a normal part of the working year, alongside search-and-rescue interaction and a tourism injury load from the Great Walks and the sounds.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Southland: working as a clinician
chunks.x: Real hospital breadth A base hospital in a region with no competing centre means you see everything the region produces. Scope is wide and referral options are further away, so you make more of the decisions. Rural and remote reach Fiordland, Rakiura and the western districts. remote medicine, search-and-rescue interaction, and a tourism injury load from the Great Walks and the sounds. A strong agricultural caseload Farming is the region’s economy, and farm injury, occupational health and rural mental health are a real and distinctive part of the work. An ageing, dispersed population Age-related medicine, orthopaedics and chronic disease weigh heavily, with access and distance compounding them across the plains. Progression, sooner A mid-sized service a long way from a tertiary centre gives you visibility and responsibility earlier than a large hospital would.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Southland: working as a clinician
chunks.x: Several clinicians we’ve placed here have stepped up faster than they expected. Recruitment is the standing challenge Southland has worked hard to attract and keep clinicians for years. That means openness to international staff — and some gaps and pressure alongside it.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Southland: working as a clinician
chunks.x: This is the rohe of Ngāi Tahu, and Murihiku has a long history of settlement, harvest and trade along the southern coast and the islands. Iwi-led health providers are an established part of care delivery, and the region’s health equity picture — rural, dispersed, with real access barriers and a significant Māori and Pacific population in the city — is central to the work rather than adjacent to it. Practically: karakia at the start of meetings, te reo used on the ward, whānau involved in decisions. You are not expected to arrive fluent — you are expected to try. The national chapter Te ao Māori at work covers pronunciation, the words you will hear and marae etiquette.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Southland: working as a clinician
chunks.x: What to ask at interview What is the catchment for my service, and how much rural, outreach or island work is involved? What is the on-call or rostered-hours pattern, and how is it paid under the relevant collective agreement? What gets referred to Dunedin or Christchurch in my specialty, and what is my role in stabilising and transferring? What orientation, supervision and cultural induction is there for clinicians new to New Zealand? What professional development and study support exists, given the distance from a tertiary centre? Is there relocation support, and what help is there finding housing and schools? Sophie Sophie’s insight Nobody asks me about Southland, and it is the region where I have seen people build the most life the fastest. A base hospital, a house bought outright within a few years, and Fiordland two hours away. The weather is the cost — everything else is in your favour. Sophie Careem Founder, Ethicare Resourcing

chunks.t: Healthcare in Southland: working as a clinician
chunks.x: Registration with your professional body, and the visa that goes with it, are national processes and identical wherever in New Zealand you land. They are explained once, properly, in Eligibility & registration and Immigration & visas . How the health system is funded and structured — ACC, primary care, what things cost, how it differs from the NHS or a private system — lives in How the health system works . Ethicare Live roles & professions What we’re recruiting for now, by profession and by region. Nearby Dunedin The tertiary centre and medical school this region refers to, two and a quarter hours east. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Southland: ten places compared
chunks.x: Invercargill is a city of wide streets and generous sections where every suburb is ten minutes from the hospital. That removes the usual trade-off entirely, so this chapter is about character and about how far out of the city you want to be. Three ways to live at the bottom of the country Every city suburb sits within about ten minutes of the hospital, so the real choice runs on character and distance from town rather than the morning drive. The city grid Room to breathe on big flat sections, from villa streets near Queens Park to the value-heavy southern edges — New Zealand’s cheapest city housing, minutes from work. The bush fringe Otatara’s tree-wrapped blocks between city and estuary — land, trees and birdsong, ten minutes out. The coast towns Bluff on its hill half an hour south, Riverton at its river mouth forty minutes west — small-town character bought with a modest daily drive. Whatever you pick, a family home on a single clinical salary is achievable here in a way it is almost nowhere else in the country.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Southland: ten places compared
chunks.x: Waikiwi & Grasmere Established northern suburbs, well regarded and well served by schools. A common landing spot for relocating clinical families, and close to the hospital. Windsor & Georgetown Solid, central, family housing on the eastern side. Good value even by local standards, and walkable to schools and shops. Avenal & Gladstone Older character housing near Queens Park, the city’s large and lovely botanic park. Villas and bungalows, mature trees. Rosedale & Newfield Affordable, straightforward suburbs on the southern and eastern edges. The best value in an already cheap city. The city centre Compact, being steadily redeveloped, with apartments appearing. Practical if you want to walk everywhere and don’t need a garden. Otatara Semi-rural lifestyle blocks in native bush between the city and the estuary, ten minutes out. Where people go for land and trees. Photography needed — Invercargill housing Wide streets, generous sections, established suburbs

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Southland: ten places compared
chunks.x: Bluff Thirty minutes south, on a hill above the strait. A working port town with real character, the oysters, and the ferry to Rakiura. Cheap, windy and much loved by those who choose it. Riverton / Aparima Forty minutes west, a small seaside town at a river mouth — arguably the prettiest spot in the region and increasingly popular. Beach, boats and a close community. Winton Half an hour north on the plains. A tidy farming service town with a school and a straightforward commute. Gore An hour north-east on the Mataura. The region’s second town, with its own services, schooling and a strong identity — brown trout, country music and farming.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Southland: ten places compared
chunks.x: Te Anau Two hours north-west, on the lake at the gateway to Fiordland National Park. A small town with a rural health service, a school, and the most spectacular setting in the country. Its own decision, not an Invercargill commute. Rakiura / Stewart Island An hour by ferry from Bluff. Four hundred people, eighty-five per cent national park, kiwi in the evening. A remote-community posting for a very particular clinician. Three things to check before you sign Insulation, heating and ventilation. This is the cool, damp end of the country. The good news: houses are cheap enough that you can afford one already done properly. Ask for the Healthy Homes compliance statement. Whether to rent at all. Unusually for this collection, buying quickly is possible here. Many clinicians rent for six months to learn the city and then purchase — see Cost of living . The school zone, at the exact address.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Southland: ten places compared
chunks.x: Choice is good for a city this size, and popular schools are zoned by address — see Schools & education . How renting works — the application pack, bond, tenancy rights and the Healthy Homes standards — is national and covered once in Renting in New Zealand . Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Getting around Southland: driving, flying and the Rakiura ferry
chunks.x: Getting around inside Southland is the easiest of any region in this collection. Getting out of it is the hardest. Check both before you commit.

chunks.t: Getting around Southland: driving, flying and the Rakiura ferry
chunks.x: Ten minutes across Invercargill, at any hour. The city was laid out on a generous grid with wide streets, and the traffic never arrived to fill them. Parking is free and abundant, including at the hospital. There is no rush hour to speak of. If you are arriving from a large city, this is the change you will feel every single day. Clinicians tell us the reclaimed time is the thing they would least want to give back.

chunks.t: Getting around Southland: driving, flying and the Rakiura ferry
chunks.x: The plains Straight, quiet, well-sealed roads through farmland. Winton half an hour, Gore an hour, and almost no traffic on any of it. The coast road West to Riverton and the Catlins east — the Southern Scenic Route. Slower, winding and worth taking for its own sake. The Fiordland road Two hours north-west to Te Anau, then the Milford road beyond it — one of the great drives anywhere, and subject to avalanche closures in winter. Winter conditions Frost and fog rather than deep snow at sea level. Black ice on the plains at dawn is the real hazard, and the Milford road is the one to check properly. Wildlife on the road a factor at dawn and dusk on rural roads. Slow down. Do you need a car? Yes. There is a city bus network in Invercargill and it is useful, but the region assumes a vehicle and most households run two.

chunks.t: Getting around Southland: driving, flying and the Rakiura ferry
chunks.x: From Bluff, thirty minutes south of the city, a passenger ferry crosses Foveaux Strait to Oban on Stewart Island in about an hour. There are also light aircraft from Invercargill Airport, which take twenty minutes and are often the better option in poor weather. Worth knowing: Foveaux Strait has a reputation, and it earns it. The crossing can be rough. If you plan to work or travel to the island regularly, the flight is what most people end up doing.

chunks.t: Getting around Southland: driving, flying and the Rakiura ferry
chunks.x: Invercargill Airport Ten minutes from the city, with regular flights to Christchurch and Auckland, and light aircraft to Rakiura. Queenstown, two hours The nearest airport with direct trans-Tasman flights. A number of Southlanders drive up for international travel, and it is a straightforward run. Long-haul Via Christchurch or Auckland, or a drive to Queenstown. This is the longest travel day of any region in this guide, and it is fair to weigh that. Getting home Budget a full day at each end. If you’ll be travelling to Europe or Africa several times a year, factor it in properly.

chunks.t: Getting around Southland: driving, flying and the Rakiura ferry
chunks.x: Journey Typical time Across Invercargill 10 min City → airport 10 min City → Oreti Beach 15 min City → Bluff 30 min City → Winton 30 min City → Riverton 40 min City → Gore 1 hr City → Te Anau 2 hr City → Queenstown 2 hr City → Dunedin 2 hr 15 City → Milford Sound ~4 hr City → Christchurch 6 hr, or 1 hr 15 flying Bluff → Oban, Rakiura 1 hr by ferry, 20 min by air Times on dry roads. Add for frost and fog in winter, and always check the Milford road before setting out. Converting your licence, buying a car, and what a warrant of fitness and registration involve are national matters, explained once in Driving & licences . Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Weekends in Southland: Fiordland, Rakiura and the south coast
chunks.x: This is the answer to every reservation in this guide. Two hours from your front door is one of the great wildernesses on earth. An hour by sea is an island that is almost entirely national park. And the coast between them is emptier than anywhere else you will live. The wilderness, from your front door Driving times from Invercargill, to scale against each other. The marked row is the answer to every reservation in this guide: World Heritage wilderness begins two hours from home. Oreti Beach Firm open sand for kilometres, and cars are allowed on it ~15 min Bluff & Stirling Point Land’s end: the harbour hill walk and the famous local catch ~30 min Riverton & the western coast A small seaside town where the coast road turns west ~40 min Te Anau & the edge of Fiordland Where the road ends and the World Heritage area starts ~2 hours Milford Sound The drive is the event — at its best in heavy rain ~4 hours Rakiura / Stewart Island sits off this chart entirely — a short ferry crossing or a lighter flight, and close enough that it needs no annual leave.

chunks.t: Weekends in Southland: Fiordland, Rakiura and the south coast
chunks.x: 1.2 million hectares of World Heritage wilderness, beginning about two hours north-west of the city. Glacier-carved sounds, rainforest, waterfalls and some of the highest rainfall on the planet. Most New Zealanders visit once. You would live at the edge of it. Milford Sound About four hours from the city on one of the great drives anywhere. Go on a wet day — that is when the waterfalls are extraordinary and the buses are fewer. Doubtful Sound Larger, quieter and harder to reach, via Lake Manapouri. Overnight trips are worth doing once and then again. The Milford Track Booked out a year ahead by people flying from the other side of the world. You would be two hours from the start. The Kepler & Routeburn Two more Great Walks within easy reach of Te Anau, and a lifetime of shorter tracks around them. Te Anau & Manapouri Lakeside towns that make a good weekend base, and a glowworm cave under the lake. Takahē and kākāpō country Some of the rarest birds on earth live in and off this coast. Conservation here is a live, visible thing.

chunks.t: Weekends in Southland: Fiordland, Rakiura and the south coast
chunks.x: An hour by ferry from Bluff, or twenty minutes by light aircraft. Four hundred people, eighty-five per cent national park, and one of the best places in the world to see kiwi in the wild — walking on a beach at dusk. There is the Rakiura Track for three days, day walks from Oban, Ulva Island’s bird sanctuary, and a night sky with almost no light pollution in it. Southlanders treat it as a long weekend rather than an expedition. That is a remarkable thing to be able to say about a place like this.

chunks.t: Weekends in Southland: Fiordland, Rakiura and the south coast
chunks.x: Oreti Beach Fifteen minutes from the city — a vast grey sweep of sand you can drive on, and where Burt Munro tested his motorcycle. Bracing rather than tropical, and often empty. Bluff & Stirling Point The signpost at the bottom of the country, the hill walk above the port, and the oysters. Thirty minutes south. Riverton & the western coast Forty minutes west. A river-mouth town, beaches, and the start of the road towards Fiordland’s southern edge. The Catlins East along the Southern Scenic Route — waterfalls, a petrified forest, penguins, sea lions and Nugget Point. One of the best day trips in New Zealand. The rivers The Mataura and Oreti are internationally known brown-trout water. Gore does not let you forget it. The aurora australis On clear, active nights, from the southern horizon. There are local groups who watch for it, and it is one of the privileges of living this far south.

chunks.t: Weekends in Southland: Fiordland, Rakiura and the south coast
chunks.x: Queenstown — 2 hr Four ski fields, the lakes and the restaurants, without paying to live there. Central Otago — 2 hr 30 The wine, the rail trail and the autumn. See the Central Otago guide . Dunedin — 2 hr 15 The nearest city, for galleries, gigs, the peninsula’s albatross and penguin colonies, and a change of pace. The Mackenzie & Aoraki — 5 hr Mount Cook, Lake Tekapo and the dark-sky reserve, for a longer weekend.

chunks.t: Weekends in Southland: Fiordland, Rakiura and the south coast
chunks.x: Tourism Southland NZ The region’s official visitor site: the coast, the towns, events and the scenic route. Fiordland Fiordland & Te Anau Te Anau, Manapouri, Milford and Doubtful Sound — what to do and when to go. Outdoors Department of Conservation Great Walks, huts, bookings and alerts for Fiordland and Rakiura. Council Invercargill City Council Local services, pools, libraries, parks and community programmes. That’s the guide Nine chapters on Southland. Everything national — visas, registration, tax, renting, driving, schools, te ao Māori — lives in Moving to New Zealand . This is the region people overlook and then quietly recommend to everyone. When you’re ready to look at roles, see what’s open now . Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Moving to Southland: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Nau mai, haere mai ki Murihiku. Southland is the bottom of the country — a broad green plain running down to a wild coast, with Fiordland at one end, Rakiura across the strait, and the most affordable city in New Zealand in the middle of it.

chunks.t: Moving to Southland: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: The last place people look, and one of the best
chunks.x: Southland is the southernmost region in New Zealand, and it is bigger and more varied than most people realise. Invercargill sits near the south coast with around fifty-seven thousand people and the region’s base hospital. Gore is an hour north-east through farming country. Te Anau is two hours north-west, on the edge of Fiordland National Park. And Rakiura — Stewart Island — lies an hour by ferry beyond Bluff, almost entirely national park. The clinical picture here is strong, and this is the part that surprises people. Southland has a base hospital serving the whole region, with a rural network reaching into Fiordland and the western districts. It is real hospital medicine, in a city where a family home costs less than anywhere else in the country. What it asks of you is a tolerance for weather and distance. This is cool temperate, maritime, often grey and frequently windy.

chunks.t: Moving to Southland: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: The last place people look, and one of the best
chunks.x: Dunedin is two and a quarter hours away, Queenstown two, Christchurch six. If those two things do not put you off, Southland offers a combination — a base hospital, affordable housing, and one of the great wildernesses on earth an hour up the road — that almost nowhere else can. Who wrote this Ethicare is a healthcare recruitment company. This guide is free to read, asks nothing of you, and does not give visa advice. Southland is the region we get asked about least and recommend more often than our enquiry numbers suggest. Where we think it’s the wrong answer, we say so.

chunks.t: Moving to Southland: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: ~103,000 People across the whole region, in an area larger than Wales. ~57,000 In Invercargill, the southernmost city in New Zealand and one of the southernmost in the world. 1 base hospital In Invercargill, serving Southland, Fiordland and Rakiura, run by Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora, with rural services across the region. ~2 hr 15 To Dunedin, where the region’s tertiary care and the medical school sit. Queenstown is around two hours. Cheapest City housing in New Zealand. Not "affordable relative to income" — the lowest actual prices of any city in the country. ~10 min A typical commute across Invercargill. Traffic is not a concept that applies here. ~9.45pm Sunset in late December. At 46 degrees south the summer evenings are extraordinarily long, and the winter mornings correspondingly dark. 1.2m hectares Of Fiordland National Park, a World Heritage wilderness beginning about two hours from the city. Aurora australis Visible from here on a clear, active night. One of the few inhabited places in the world where that is an ordinary occurrence.

chunks.t: Moving to Southland: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: The weather is the price of admission Cool, changeable and windy, with more grey days than the north and fewer hot ones. Nobody here pretends otherwise. What you get for it is green country, no drought, and nobody else on the trails. The summer light is astonishing Light until nearly ten at night in December and January. You will eat outside at nine, and you will do things after work that you could not do anywhere further north. There is a real accent The Southland burr — a rolled "r" inherited from Scottish settlers, and the only distinct regional accent in New Zealand. You’ll hear it within a day and grow fond of it. Housing costs almost nothing, comparatively The single most consequential fact in this guide. A large family home here costs a fraction of an apartment in Queenstown, two hours up the road. Cost of living spells it out.

chunks.t: Moving to Southland: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: Locals defend the place fiercely Invercargill has spent decades being the butt of other regions’ jokes, and Southlanders have long since stopped caring. The community pride here is real and it is welcoming. Fiordland changes what a weekend is Milford, Doubtful Sound, the Kepler and Routeburn tracks. Most New Zealanders visit once. You would live two hours away. A note on names Murihiku — "the last joint of the tail" — is Southland’s name in te reo Māori, and this is the rohe of Ngāi Tahu. Rakiura is Stewart Island; Waihōpai is the river Invercargill sits on. The southern coast has been travelled and harvested for centuries, and tītī — muttonbirding — remains a living customary practice on the islands off Rakiura. You’re not expected to arrive fluent. You are expected to try. Te ao Māori at work covers pronunciation and the words you’ll hear on the ward.

chunks.t: Moving to Southland: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Nine chapters, all of them about Southland specifically. Anything true of New Zealand generally — visas, registration, tax, renting law, driving licences, schools — lives once in Moving to New Zealand . If you read nothing else, read Why Southland for the full case — and what we’d ask you to weigh, and Cost of living , because the numbers here are unlike anywhere else in the country. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Why Southland: the case for the deep south
chunks.x: Southland gets fewer enquiries than any region in this collection and produces more contented clinicians than most. The gap between those two facts is what this chapter is about.

chunks.t: Why Southland: the case for the deep south
chunks.x: Clinical pay in New Zealand is set nationally. You earn the same in Invercargill as in Auckland or Queenstown. What changes is what it costs to live — and here it costs less than anywhere else in the country. That is not a small difference. Invercargill has the lowest house prices of any New Zealand city, by a clear margin. A large four-bedroom family home on a proper section, ten minutes from the hospital, costs less than a modest apartment in Queenstown two hours north. On a single clinical salary you can buy here almost immediately, and on two you can do it comfortably and still travel. Set against that: it is a small city a long way from the rest of the country, and the weather is the coolest and greyest in New Zealand. Those are real costs, and they are the reason the housing is cheap. The question is simply whether you would rather pay in money or in latitude.

chunks.t: Why Southland: the case for the deep south
chunks.x: Monday to Friday Ten minutes to work, and free parking. Invercargill’s streets were laid out with an optimism about traffic that never materialised, which is entirely to your benefit. After work, summer Light until nearly ten. A beach at Oreti, a round of golf, a bike ride, or the estuary. The long evenings are the region’s secret pleasure. After work, winter Dark early and often wet. This is when the indoor life matters — and Invercargill has an unusually good stock of pools, gyms, a velodrome and community sport for its size. Saturday Bluff for oysters and the walk out to Stirling Point, Riverton for the coast, or the Catlins east along the southern scenic route. Sunday Te Anau and the edge of Fiordland, two hours up the road. Or the ferry to Rakiura, where you can hear kiwi in the evening. A long weekend Milford or Doubtful Sound, the Kepler Track, Queenstown, Dunedin or the Catlins. It is an extraordinary base for a certain kind of weekend.

chunks.t: Why Southland: the case for the deep south
chunks.h: The six things people ask us
chunks.x: Is there enough clinical work? Yes — and this is the point people miss. Southland has a base hospital covering a whole region, which means acute medicine and surgery, an emergency department, maternity, paediatrics, imaging, intensive care and a broad outpatient service. It is proper hospital medicine with a wide catchment, not a rural outpost. Healthcare here sets out what is and is not done in the region. Is the weather really that bad? It is the coolest and one of the wettest regions in New Zealand. Summers are mild rather than hot, winters are cool and damp rather than severe, and the wind is constant. What people find is that the long summer light and the green landscape compensate more than they expected — and that the clothing solves most of it. Can I buy a house? Yes, quickly, and that is the strongest argument for this region.

chunks.t: Why Southland: the case for the deep south
chunks.h: The six things people ask us
chunks.x: Invercargill is the most affordable city in New Zealand and it is not close. Most clinicians we place here buy within their first year or two rather than renting indefinitely. Is it isolated? Geographically, yes. Dunedin is two and a quarter hours, Queenstown two, Christchurch six or an hour flying. Socially it is less isolated than the map suggests — the health workforce here has recruited internationally for decades, there is a polytechnic bringing students in, and Southlanders are notably welcoming to newcomers. Is it a good place with children? Very. Space, safety, sport, short commutes, a full range of schooling from primary to secondary, and enough left over at the end of the month to do things. The main caveats are the winter darkness and the distance to some specialist paediatric services, which mean Dunedin. What is there to do? More than the reputation allows.

chunks.t: Why Southland: the case for the deep south
chunks.h: The six things people ask us
chunks.x: A strong community sport and motorsport culture, good pools and indoor facilities, a distinct food identity, and — the answer — Fiordland, Rakiura and the Catlins on your doorstep. If your idea of a weekend involves mountains, water or birds, few places on earth beat this.

chunks.t: Why Southland: the case for the deep south
chunks.x: You want warmth and sun This is the wrong end of the country, plainly. If sunshine hours matter most to you, look at Hawke’s Bay, the Bay of Plenty or Nelson. Your specialty needs tertiary volume Complex and highly specialised work goes to Dunedin or Christchurch. Southland is a base hospital, not a tertiary centre. You want a city that feels like a city Invercargill is a functional, friendly small city. It is not Wellington or Christchurch, and if urban life is central to your happiness, weigh that carefully. You need easy international travel Long-haul means Christchurch, Auckland or a drive to Queenstown. It is the longest travel day of any region in this guide. You’d find the winter dark hard At 46 degrees south, midwinter mornings and afternoons are dark. Some people love the seasonality; others find it wearing, and it is worth knowing which you are.

chunks.t: Why Southland: the case for the deep south
chunks.x: Where we’d steer you instead Want the far south with more city and a tertiary hospital? Dunedin , two and a quarter hours east. Want the mountains and lakes, and can absorb the cost? Central Otago — though read its cost chapter first. Want the South Island with real clinical depth and a bigger city? Christchurch . In our experience Southland gets fewer enquiries than any region we cover and produces more contented clinicians than most — the maths works, the hospital is steady, and Fiordland does the rest. Bring proper clothing and low expectations of the weather; everything else over-delivers. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Cost of living in Sydney: the full arithmetic
chunks.x: This is the chapter that matters most in Sydney, so we will not soften it. This is the least affordable housing market in Australia and one of the least affordable in the world. What follows is the arithmetic, and the strategies that work.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Sydney: the full arithmetic
chunks.x: We used to print a weekly rent and a monthly budget table here. We have taken them out. A figure that was true when a page was written is misleading a year later, and a candidate who plans a move around a stale number is worse off than one who plans around none. What does not go stale is the shape of a month, and the judgement about which lines will surprise you. For today’s actual numbers use the calculators at the foot of the page, and use them to compare Sydney against the city you are leaving. That is the only comparison that decides anything.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Sydney: the full arithmetic
chunks.x: Highest Housing costs of any Australian city 30–40% Of take-home pay on rent is common here West Where the same salary buys a house, not a flat The structural truth does not move: your housing decision determines your Sydney experience more than your salary does, and the east-to-west gradient is the single biggest lever you have.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Sydney: the full arithmetic
chunks.x: Where a month goes The proportions, for one person on a mid-range budget. Proportions move slowly; prices move every quarter. Rent is sixty per cent of the month — the highest share of any destination in this collection, and the reason this chapter exists. Rent 61% Groceries 15% Entertainment 8% Transport (Opal or fuel + tolls) 7% Power & water 7% Internet 2% The line that decides it Rent · 61% Every other line is ordinary; the rent line is the whole problem. That is also why it is the one worth strategising — the section below is about moving that segment, not the small ones.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Sydney: the full arithmetic
chunks.x: Look west, seriously A family house thirty minutes from a large teaching hospital in the west costs a fraction of a flat near an eastern campus. This is the single biggest financial decision available to you here. Share for the first year Sharing well into your thirties is completely normal in Sydney. It buys you a year to learn the city before committing to a suburb — and most people move after that year anyway. Use the transport network A suburb on a train, metro or ferry line with no car at all can save more than a rent discount in a car-dependent suburb. Run both numbers before choosing. Ask about accommodation help Some employers offer relocation support or subsidised accommodation, particularly outside the inner city. It is asked for far less often than it should be.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Sydney: the full arithmetic
chunks.x: The free city is world class here: a hundred beaches, dozens of free ocean pools, the coastal walks, the harbour foreshore parks, the botanic gardens and national parks at three edges of the city. A Sydney weekend can cost nothing at all and still be the best weekend available in Australia. Public transport is good enough to make a car optional in much of the inner city, which is thousands a year. On the income side, public-health and not-for-profit roles here can salary-package part of your pay before tax — ask payroll on day one, because in this city it matters more than anywhere. How packaging, tax and superannuation work is national and lives in Pay & conditions . The bottom line Do the arithmetic before you accept the job, not after you arrive. Work out what you can pay in rent, then look only at suburbs within that number and within a sane commute of your campus.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Sydney: the full arithmetic
chunks.x: If the two do not overlap, that is not a failure of planning — it is Sydney telling you something, and Brisbane or Melbourne may give you the same career for a great deal less. Get today’s numbers, and compare them to home These are live and updated continuously. Put the city you are leaving in the other box. Numbeo cost-of-living calculator — the most complete comparison tool, and the one most clinicians already use. Crowd-sourced, so treat it as a ballpark. Expatistan — the same idea with a cleaner side-by-side. Worth running as a sanity check when Numbeo looks off. Australian Bureau of Statistics — official and slower, and the one to trust on the direction of travel. If what you find differs from what we say here, tell us and we will correct it. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Sydney
chunks.x: Sydney’s best food is not on the harbour. It is in the suburbs where people live — the Vietnamese south-west, the Lebanese west, the Chinese north shore, the Greek and Italian inner west — and eating your way around them is the fastest way to understand the city.

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Sydney
chunks.x: Cabramatta, in the south-west, is one of the great Vietnamese food precincts anywhere outside Vietnam. Lakemba and Auburn cover Lebanese, Turkish and Afghan cooking, and come alive during Ramadan when the night markets run late. Chatswood and Eastwood on the north shore hold outstanding Chinese, Korean and Japanese food. The inner west layers Greek, Italian, Vietnamese and Portuguese along a few kilometres of Marrickville and Leichhardt. Closer to the centre, Surry Hills and Potts Point carry the restaurant scene proper, and the CBD hides good Japanese and Korean food in basements.
