For everyday shopping: Woolworths and Coles everywhere, ALDI for the cheap basket, and excellent independent grocers and butchers in every one of the neighbourhoods above. Coffee is a standard Sydney takes coffee seriously without Melbourne’s theology.

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Sydney
chunks.x: Find your local in week one — the good ones have queues and no branding. The markets Carriageworks on Saturday for the serious cooks, Marrickville for value and variety, Paddington for the browse. Flemington for wholesale prices if you cook a lot. Brunch is an institution Weekend brunch here is a social ritual, and Sydney arguably invented the modern version of it. Expect a queue and no bookings. Beach food is its own thing Fish and chips at the ocean pool, a coffee after a swim, a barbecue in a foreshore park — free gas, first come first served.

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Sydney
chunks.x: With around four in ten residents born overseas, Sydney is the easiest Australian city in which to find whatever you grew up eating. Halal butchers across the west and south-west, kosher shops and bakeries in the eastern suburbs around Bondi, South Asian groceries in Harris Park and Wentworthville, African and Middle Eastern stores across the west, and Asian supermarkets in essentially every suburb. Very little needs ordering online. The practical upside for newcomers is community rather than just ingredients: those shops sit alongside the associations, places of worship and weekend gatherings that turn a new city into a life. If you are arriving alone, that is the fastest route in.

chunks.t: Food, coffee & the everyday in Sydney
chunks.x: Sydney lives outdoors and early. Swims before work, coastal walks at dawn, park runs, and outdoor tables whenever the weather allows — which is most of the year. Summer adds the beach, outdoor cinema and long evenings; winter barely closes anything, though the water gets brisk. The city’s calendar runs on Vivid’s winter light festival, the New Year fireworks on the harbour, and a sporting schedule that fills most weekends. The everyday, in one list Learn one food suburb properly — Cabramatta, Lakemba, Chatswood or Marrickville. Serious shop: Carriageworks or Marrickville markets. Cheapest: ALDI and Flemington. Find your local coffee place in week one, and the nearest ocean pool in week two. Say schooner. Book nothing for brunch. Accept the queue. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.x: Before the practical chapters, orientation. Sydney has no single centre — the harbour and the national parks split it into distinct cities that happen to share a name, a train network and a housing crisis. Knowing which one you are moving to matters more here than anywhere else in Australia.

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.x: Where Sydney sits, with the straight-line distance to Newcastle and Wollongong

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.x: From the CBD out to the beaches: Surry Hills, Paddington, Bondi, Coogee, Randwick. Terraces, ocean pools, the coastal walk, and the highest prices in the country. Several major hospital campuses sit in this arc, which is what makes the eastern suburbs so competitive for clinical staff.

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.x: Across the bridge: North Sydney, Chatswood, the leafy upper north shore, and the northern beaches running up to Palm Beach. Family territory, excellent schools, big trees, and a strong hospital presence. The beaches peninsula is beautiful and badly connected — a clear trade.

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.x: Newtown, Marrickville, Leichhardt, Balmain: Victorian housing, the best food in the city, a young and diverse population, and slightly more attainable prices. Well served by trains and light rail, and close to the central hospital cluster.

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.x: Parramatta — Sydney’s second CBD — and the vast western and south-western suburbs beyond it, where most of the city’s population growth is happening. This is where housing is affordable, where the fastest-growing hospitals are, and where the summer runs several degrees hotter than the coast. It is also where a great many clinical careers are built.

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.x: Temperate and mild by Australian standards, with humid summers and gentle winters that rarely need more than a jacket. Summer brings heat and humidity, storms, and in bad seasons bushfire smoke; the western suburbs run consistently hotter than the coastal strip. Autumn is the city’s best season — warm water, clear air, fewer crowds — and winter is mild enough for the coastal walks to stay busy. Summer Dec – Feb 19–27° Humid · storms · fire season Autumn Mar – May 15–23° The best of the year Winter Jun – Aug 9–18° Mild, bright, a jacket Spring Sep – Nov 14–23° Jacarandas · warming up Two practical notes. If you are looking west, check how a home handles heat — insulation, orientation and air conditioning matter far more twenty kilometres inland than they do at Bondi. And in fire season, smoke can close windows across the whole basin for days; people with asthma should plan for it.

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.x: Sydney Airport sits unusually close to the city — about twenty minutes by train from the centre — and is Australia’s busiest international gateway, with a second airport opening in the west. The Melbourne route is one of the world’s busiest air corridors. By road, the Blue Mountains and the Central Coast are an hour, Wollongong an hour and a quarter down a spectacular coast road, and the Hunter Valley about two.

chunks.t: Sydney at a glance: the four Sydneys, the climate and the clock
chunks.h: Words you’ll hear in week one
chunks.x: Warrane The Gadigal name for Sydney Cove — the harbour’s original name Opal The tap-on card for trains, buses, ferries and light rail The Coathanger The Harbour Bridge, affectionately Ocean pool A tidal saltwater pool cut into the rocks — there are dozens, and they are free The North Shore Everything across the bridge — a state of mind as much as a place Westie Once an insult for western-suburbs residents, now worn with pride Schooner The standard beer size — smaller than a pint, and the correct order Chockablock What the traffic is, most of the time, everywhere Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Healthcare in Sydney: the largest system in Australia
chunks.x: Registration is national; hiring here is district by district. Sydney holds the deepest concentration of clinical work in Australia, and it is spread across a metropolitan area large enough that choosing your district effectively chooses your life. This chapter explains the shape without naming employers.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Sydney: the largest system in Australia
chunks.x: New South Wales runs its public system through local health districts — several of which cover metropolitan Sydney, divided broadly into the city and east, the north, the inner and south-west, and the greater west. Each district employs in its own right, runs its own recruitment, and covers a defined geography with a principal referral hospital and a network of sites around it. There are also statewide specialty networks, including children’s health and forensic mental health. Alongside the public districts sits the largest private hospital sector in the country, a substantial private imaging and pathology market, and major medical research institutes attached to the main teaching campuses. Quaternary depth The widest range of highly specialised services in Australia, including units that take referrals from other states and from the Pacific.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Sydney: the largest system in Australia
chunks.x: Districts, not one employer Each metropolitan district hires separately. Where you apply determines your commute, your case mix and your colleagues for years. The west is where growth is Western and south-western Sydney carry the fastest population growth in the state, sustained hospital investment, and the most consistent recruitment. One national register Ahpra registration works everywhere in Australia. The process, English evidence and assessment live once in Eligibility & registration . Four Sydneys, four employers Each district hires separately, so the district you apply to sets your commute, your case mix and your colleagues for years. This is the single most consequential decision in a Sydney move — and most people make it by accident. The city and east The oldest teaching campuses and the most sought-after posts, with the housing cost and the competition to match.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Sydney: the largest system in Australia
chunks.x: A superb place to work and the hardest place to arrive into cold. The north Large teaching hospitals across the harbour, a settled catchment and a strong research presence. The commute across the bridge is what decides whether it works for you. The inner and south-west Busy, complex and diverse, with major teaching hospitals and steady recruitment. A great many of the best Sydney careers are built here rather than east of the city. The greater west The fastest population growth in the state, sustained hospital investment and the most consistent recruitment — with housing thirty minutes from those campuses at a fraction of the eastern equivalent. This is where we point most people first. Statewide specialty networks — children’s health and forensic mental health among them — sit alongside the districts and recruit separately again. Registration itself is national: Eligibility & registration .

chunks.t: Healthcare in Sydney: the largest system in Australia
chunks.h: What that means for a career
chunks.x: If you want to work at the very top of a narrow field, Sydney has more of those posts than anywhere else in the country — and more people competing for them. That is the trade-off of the biggest system: the ceiling is higher and the queue is longer. Fellowships, research appointments and highly specialised units are all more plentiful here, and all harder to win. The most useful advice we give candidates is to look west. The western and south-western districts run large, busy teaching hospitals with high complexity, they are where the state is investing, and they recruit consistently — while housing thirty minutes from those campuses costs a fraction of the eastern equivalent. A great many excellent Sydney careers are built out there. One structural note: metropolitan Sydney is not classed as regional for skilled migration, which changes the visa arithmetic against much of regional New South Wales — see Visas & the move and the NSW guide . “ The highest ceiling in the country, and the longest queue. Both things are true. The one-line version

chunks.t: Healthcare in Sydney: the largest system in Australia
chunks.x: Pay follows NSW awards and enterprise agreements — we deliberately quote no figures in this guide, and will walk you through the current agreement for your profession instead. What you can pin down at interview: Salary packaging — public-health roles can package part of your pay pre-tax; ask how much and how to start it on day one Which district and which campus — and whether you may be rostered across several sites The roster reality — shift patterns, penalties, on-call frequency and how gaps get covered Whether accommodation assistance or relocation support exists, which matters more here than anywhere CPD — funded time and money, and what conference travel is covered Research and teaching time, if that is part of why you came Parking, and the commute at your actual shift times — inner-city parking is scarce and expensive Professional indemnity — what the employer covers and what stays

chunks.t: Healthcare in Sydney: the largest system in Australia
chunks.x: yours Two things to do early Start registration as soon as Sydney is on your shortlist — paperwork, not ambition, is what moves start dates. And decide your district before you look at a single rental listing: in this city the campus sets the commute, and the commute sets everything else. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Sydney: east, north, inner west and the greater west
chunks.x: In Sydney this is the decision. The gap between an eastern-suburbs life and a western one is wider — in money, in commute, in what your weekend looks like — than in any other Australian city. Here is the map as we’d draw it over coffee, including the part most guides skip. On the map The east Surry Hills Darlinghurst Paddington Randwick Coogee Bronte Bondi North shore & beaches Cremorne Neutral Bay Mosman Chatswood Killara Northern beaches The inner west Newtown Erskineville Marrickville Dulwich Hill Leichhardt The greater west Parramatta Parks & nature Beaches Landmarks Shaded areas are the suburbs named in this chapter. Arrows point to places beyond the map edge, with the straight-line distance from the city centre. Suburb boundaries © Geoscape Australia, CC BY 4.0 · Natural Earth

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Sydney: east, north, inner west and the greater west
chunks.x: Surry Hills, Darlinghurst and Paddington sit next to the central hospital cluster: terraces, restaurants, and a walk-to-work life for the small number who can afford it. Out toward the coast, Randwick, Coogee, Bronte and Bondi put ocean pools and the coastal walk at the end of the street, with major campuses close by. This is the most competitive rental market in the country, and sharing well into your thirties is normal here rather than a failure.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Sydney: east, north, inner west and the greater west
chunks.x: Across the bridge, the lower north shore — Cremorne, Neutral Bay, Mosman — gives harbour views, ferries and family life at eastern-suburb prices. The upper north shore around Chatswood and Killara is leafier, quieter and school-driven, with a large and long-established Chinese-Australian community and excellent food. The northern beaches are beautiful and isolated: no train line, one road in and out, and a commute that tests people. The eastern beaches — the most expensive commute in Australia The greater west — where the housing maths works

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Sydney: east, north, inner west and the greater west
chunks.x: Newtown, Erskineville, Marrickville, Dulwich Hill and Leichhardt: the best value inside ten kilometres, Victorian and Federation housing, and the strongest food culture in the city — Greek, Italian, Vietnamese and Lebanese layered over each other. Well served by trains and light rail, and close to the central hospital cluster. For clinicians without eastern-suburbs money, this is usually the answer.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Sydney: east, north, inner west and the greater west
chunks.x: This is the part most relocation guides skip, and it deserves the opposite. Parramatta is Sydney’s second CBD, with its own commercial centre, university presence and major hospital campus. Around it, the western and south-western suburbs hold the fastest population growth in the state, the biggest hospital investment, and family houses at a fraction of coastal prices — often thirty minutes from a large teaching hospital rather than ninety. The trade-offs: summers run several degrees hotter than the coast, the beach is an expedition rather than a walk, and the cultural centre of gravity is different — more suburban, more family-oriented, far more multicultural. For a great many clinicians, particularly those with children, the west is not the compromise. It is the sensible choice, and we say so plainly.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Sydney: east, north, inner west and the greater west
chunks.x: Least Affordable housing market in Australia 4 wks Typical bond, lodged with the state authority Share Normal well into your thirties near the coast If you want… Consider Because Walk to the central campuses Surry Hills, Darlinghurst No commute at all — at a price Ocean pools before a shift Coogee, Bronte, Randwick The eastern beaches, campuses close Harbour and a ferry Cremorne, Neutral Bay, Balmain The best commute in the country Value inside 10 km Newtown, Marrickville, Dulwich Hill Inner west — food, trains, terraces Schools and space Chatswood, the upper north shore Leafy, established, family-shaped A family house that adds up Parramatta and the greater west Big hospitals, real houses, sane prices Renting itself — applications, bonds, rights, the documents that win a competitive inspection — works the same across Australia and lives once in Living in Australia .

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Sydney: east, north, inner west and the greater west
chunks.x: Sydney-specific: go to inspections with every document ready to submit on the spot, and expect to apply for several properties before one lands. That is normal here and not a reflection on you. Before you sign a lease What is the commute to your actual campus at your actual shift times — door to door? If you are looking west: how does the house handle 40-degree days? Insulation and orientation matter. Is there a train, light rail or ferry within walking distance? Bus-only suburbs feel much further out. Is it in the school catchment you need? Zones are checked by address here. Would a short lease first be wiser? Almost everyone re-chooses after their first year. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Getting around Sydney: trains, ferries, metro and the traffic
chunks.x: Sydney’s public transport is better than visitors expect and its traffic is worse. The rail network is extensive, the ferries are a pleasure, and the driverless metro is steadily changing the city. The rule here: live near a station, or accept the commute.

chunks.t: Getting around Sydney: trains, ferries, metro and the traffic
chunks.x: Opal One tap-on card — or a contactless bank card — across trains, metro, buses, ferries and light rail, with daily and weekly caps and cheaper off-peak travel. Trains An extensive suburban network reaching most of the metro area, plus intercity lines to the Blue Mountains, the Central Coast and Wollongong. The backbone. Metro Driverless, frequent and expanding across the city — already reshaping which suburbs count as well connected. Ferries Ordinary public transport, on the same card, across the harbour and up the Parramatta River. The best commute in Australia, and not a tourist novelty. Car-free life is practical near a train, metro or ferry line — which covers much of the east, the inner west and the lower north shore. It is far harder in bus-only suburbs and on the northern beaches, where one road carries everything.

chunks.t: Getting around Sydney: trains, ferries, metro and the traffic
chunks.x: Australians drive on the left. Sydney is the hardest Australian capital to drive in: a road network shaped by water rather than planning, heavy congestion, and an extensive toll network across the motorways and harbour crossings, so a toll account is essential rather than optional. Licence transfer and buying a car work the same across the country and live in Living in Australia . Two local notes. Hospital parking in the inner city is scarce and expensive — ask about staff parking at interview rather than assuming. And check your commute at the times you will travel: a route that takes twenty-five minutes at 10am can take an hour at 8am. Ferries are on the same card as the trains — and comfortably the best of the network.

chunks.t: Getting around Sydney: trains, ferries, metro and the traffic
chunks.x: From the CBD to… Roughly How Surry Hills / Darlinghurst 10–15 min Walk or light rail The eastern beaches 25–40 min Bus or light rail Lower north shore 15–25 min Ferry or train Inner west 15–25 min Train or light rail Parramatta ~30 min Train or river ferry Northern beaches 45–75 min Bus or drive — no train Sydney Airport ~20 min Train Blue Mountains / Central Coast ~1 hr Intercity train or drive The takeaway Choose your home by its station, not its postcode. In Sydney the difference between a well-connected suburb and a bus-only one is an hour a day, every day — and that hour costs more over a year than the rent difference that tempted you. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Weekends in Sydney: harbour, beaches and the Blue Mountains
chunks.x: Sydney’s weekends are the compensation, and they are extraordinary. A hundred beaches, national parks pressing in from three sides, a harbour you can swim in, and a World Heritage escarpment an hour from the suburbs. Most of it is free.

chunks.t: Weekends in Sydney: harbour, beaches and the Blue Mountains
chunks.x: Bondi at sunrise, before a day shift East: Bondi, Tamarama, Bronte, Coogee — linked by the coastal walk that everyone does at least monthly, with ocean pools cut into the rocks along the way. North: Manly, Freshwater, Curl Curl and up the peninsula to Palm Beach, quieter and better for surfing. South: Cronulla and the beaches inside the Royal National Park, where the crowds thin out entirely. The ocean pools deserve their own mention — dozens of them, tidal, free, and used year-round by people of every age. They are the most democratic thing about this city.

chunks.t: Weekends in Sydney: harbour, beaches and the Blue Mountains
chunks.x: Take the ferry to Manly at least once a month; it costs the same as a bus and is one of the great urban journeys anywhere. Beyond that: Cockatoo Island’s industrial heritage, the harbour beaches at Balmoral and Nielsen Park where the water is flat and warm, the Hermitage foreshore walk, and Sydney Harbour National Park’s tracks around the headlands. The New Year fireworks are worth doing once, from a park with a picnic.

chunks.t: Weekends in Sydney: harbour, beaches and the Blue Mountains
chunks.x: The Blue Mountains begin an hour west: a World Heritage sandstone escarpment with the Three Sisters, canyons, waterfalls and hundreds of kilometres of walking track, plus mountain villages that are ten degrees cooler than the city in February. South, the Royal National Park — the world’s second-oldest — has the coast track, cliff-top walks and beaches you have to walk into. North, Ku-ring-gai Chase holds Aboriginal rock engravings and bushland running down to the water. National parks on three sides The compensation for everything else in this guide: three ways out of the city, and a World Heritage escarpment or a coast track at the end of each. Most of it is free. North, up the peninsula Quieter beaches and better surfing the further you go — and the ferry, which costs the same as a bus and is one of the great urban journeys anywhere.

chunks.t: Weekends in Sydney: harbour, beaches and the Blue Mountains
chunks.x: The city Manly · by ferry Curl Curl & Freshwater Ku-ring-gai Chase West, into the mountains A sandstone escarpment with canyons, waterfalls and hundreds of kilometres of track — and villages ten degrees cooler than the city in February. The city Blue Mountains · ~1 hr The Three Sisters & the canyons South, down the coast The world’s second-oldest national park, then the Sea Cliff Bridge, then white sand and the quiet towns beyond. The city Royal National Park Sea Cliff Bridge Jervis Bay The east is the fourth direction and needs no rail: the Bondi-to-Coogee coastal walk, and dozens of tidal ocean pools that are free and used year-round by people of every age.

chunks.t: Weekends in Sydney: harbour, beaches and the Blue Mountains
chunks.x: The Hunter Valley Two hours north — Australia’s oldest wine region, and the classic Sydney weekend away. The south coast Down past Wollongong on the Sea Cliff Bridge to Jervis Bay’s white sand and the quiet coastal towns beyond. The Central Coast An hour north by train — beaches, lakes and a much slower pace, popular for a weekend shack.

chunks.t: Weekends in Sydney: harbour, beaches and the Blue Mountains
chunks.x: The Bondi-to-Coogee coastal walk, with a swim at each ocean pool The Manly ferry, then the Manly-to-Spit walk back around the harbour The Blue Mountains: the Three Sisters, then a canyon walk away from the lookouts The Royal National Park coast track, or just the beaches you have to walk into Ku-ring-gai Chase for the rock engravings and the water views A Hunter Valley weekend, cellar doors and a long lunch The south coast: the Sea Cliff Bridge, then Jervis Bay’s white sand Cockatoo Island and the harbour’s industrial history Balmoral or Nielsen Park for flat, warm harbour swimming Vivid in winter, walking the harbour foreshore after dark That’s the guide Nine chapters on Sydney. Statewide and regional topics live in the New South Wales guide , and everything national in Moving to Australia . When you’re ready to talk about roles here, send us your CV . Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Moving to Sydney: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Sydney is the one Australian city that needs no introduction and the one that most needs a clear guide. The largest health system in the country, a spectacular setting, and housing costs that will shape every other decision you make. This guide is about making that trade with your eyes open.

chunks.t: Moving to Sydney: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: The Harbour Bridge after dark Around five and a half million people live around a drowned river valley — which is why Sydney has no single centre but dozens, and why a journey of four kilometres can take forty minutes. The harbour, the beaches and the national parks that press in from three sides are not scenery here; they are the reason people put up with the rest. For clinicians the draw is scale. New South Wales runs the country’s largest public health system, and the greater Sydney share of it carries the deepest bench of tertiary and quaternary services, the biggest teaching hospitals, and specialist units that take national referrals. If your field is narrow, or you want to work at the very top of it, the density here is unmatched. The cost is money.

chunks.t: Moving to Sydney: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Sydney is one of the least affordable cities in the world for housing, and the gap between an inner-suburb life and an outer-suburb one is wider than in any other Australian city. Everything in this guide is written with that fact in the room. Who wrote this Ethicare is a healthcare recruitment company. This guide is free to read, asks nothing of you, and does not give visa advice. Sydney is the city candidates most often name first and research least. We will tell you plainly when the sums do not work, and which other city gives you the same career for a great deal less.

chunks.t: Moving to Sydney: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: ~5.5M People in Greater Sydney — the largest city in Australia, and the largest health system with it. ~100 Beaches inside the metropolitan area, from Palm Beach in the north to Cronulla in the south. ~70 km From the eastern beaches to the western edge of the metro area. This is a very large city. Deepest Bench of tertiary and quaternary services in Australia, spread across several local health districts. Least Affordable housing in the country, and among the least affordable in the world. Plan around it. 1 hr To the Blue Mountains, a World Heritage escarpment that starts at the edge of the suburbs. UTC+10 With daylight saving — long summer evenings on the harbour, and mild winters by any standard. ~40% Of residents were born overseas. Whatever you left behind, there is a community here already. 2 Airports, once the western one opens fully — and the busiest domestic route in the country to Melbourne.

chunks.t: Moving to Sydney: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: Rent decides everything Where you live sets your commute, your savings and your weekends. Most newcomers rent smaller and further out than they expected, and adjust after a year. The harbour is transport Ferries are ordinary commuting on the same card as the trains, and the best twenty minutes of anyone’s working day. Distance is measured in time Nobody says kilometres here. Four kilometres across the harbour can be forty minutes; twenty by ferry can be pleasant. The beach is a routine Ocean pools, dawn swims, the coastal walks. People do this before work, year-round, and it is the compensation for the rent. Summer has teeth Humid heat, and in bad years bushfire smoke that closes windows across the city. It is the part the postcards leave out.

chunks.t: Moving to Sydney: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: There is no one Sydney The east, the north shore, the inner west and the greater west are different cities with different prices, cultures and hospitals. A note on Country Sydney stands on the lands of the Gadigal and other clans of the Eora Nation, and Warrane is the name for the harbour’s cove where the colony began. This is where the colonial history of Australia starts, and the city carries that weight. Acknowledgement of Country opens meetings, and health services work in partnership with Aboriginal community-controlled organisations. Take the cultural induction seriously.

chunks.t: Moving to Sydney: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Nine chapters, all about Sydney specifically. Topics true across the state — regional New South Wales, the state health structure — sit in the New South Wales guide . Anything true of Australia generally — Medicare, visas, Ahpra registration, tax, superannuation, schools — lives once in Moving to Australia . If you read nothing else, read Why Sydney for the full case — and what we’d ask you to weigh, and Cost of living , because in this city the money question comes before the suburb question. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Why Sydney: the case for the harbour city
chunks.x: Sydney needs no selling, so this chapter does the useful job instead: what the city gives a working clinician, what it takes back in rent and commuting — and when we’d point you interstate.

chunks.t: Why Sydney: the case for the harbour city
chunks.x: Scale, and the setting. New South Wales runs the largest public health system in the country, and Sydney holds the deepest concentration of it — major teaching hospitals across several districts, quaternary units that take national referrals, and research institutes attached to them. For sub-specialty work, fellowships and academic pathways, the density of opportunity here is unmatched in Australia. Then the city itself, which at its best is extraordinary: a working harbour you commute across, a hundred beaches, ocean pools, coastal walks, and a mild climate that makes all of it usable most of the year. Pay follows NSW awards and enterprise agreements — we quote no figures here and will walk you through the current agreement instead. Largest Public health system in Australia ~100 Beaches inside the metro area 1 hr To World Heritage wilderness

chunks.t: Why Sydney: the case for the harbour city
chunks.x: A ferry commute across the harbour, which never quite becomes ordinary. A tertiary list with the equipment and the team to match. A swim at an ocean pool before a late start, or the Bondi-to-Coogee walk after one. Friday night somewhere in the inner west that would be a destination restaurant in a smaller city. Saturday at the beach with half the city; Sunday in the Blue Mountains or the Royal National Park, an hour away and completely quiet. The counterweight: a proportion of that week is spent travelling, and a significant proportion of your income goes on housing. People who love Sydney accept both. People who resent them are usually happier elsewhere. The ordinary evening version of the harbour — which is most of them Sophie’s insight Sydney is the city everyone names first, and the one where I most often ask people to do the arithmetic before they commit.

chunks.t: Why Sydney: the case for the harbour city
chunks.x: If your career needs the biggest system in the country, it is worth it — nowhere else in Australia has that depth. But if what you want is a tertiary job, a house and a short commute, Brisbane or Adelaide will give you all three, and Sydney will give you two at most. Sophie Careem Founder & CEO, Ethicare Resourcing

chunks.t: Why Sydney: the case for the harbour city
chunks.x: The housing maths The least affordable city in the country. Buying near an inner-city hospital is out of reach for most clinical salaries, and renting takes a large share of take-home pay. The commute A city of 70 kilometres across with congestion to match. Affordable housing and inner-city work rarely coexist, and the difference is measured in hours a week. Competition The biggest system attracts the most applicants. Training posts and sought-after roles are competitive in a way smaller systems are not. Summer extremes Humid heat, and bushfire smoke in bad seasons. The western suburbs regularly run several degrees hotter than the coast. It can be transactional A big, busy, expensive city where people work long hours. Building a social life takes more deliberate effort than in smaller places.

chunks.t: Why Sydney: the case for the harbour city
chunks.x: Where we’d steer you instead If you want tertiary work with housing that still adds up, read Brisbane — the closest thing to Sydney’s career with a livable price. If you want the deepest system but not the cost, Melbourne is the direct comparison — comparable depth, meaningfully cheaper. If regional New South Wales appeals, the NSW guide covers the coastal cities and inland centres, many with strong incentives. In our experience Sydney suits clinicians who want the ceiling as high as it goes — the sub-specialty depth, the research links, the sheer scale. We’re equally plain about the housing maths with everyone; the people who love Sydney decided the city was worth planning around. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Cost of living in Tasmania: cheaper than the mainland, audited
chunks.x: Tasmania costs less than the mainland capitals and more than the postcard suggests. In practice: day-to-day life is gentle on the wallet, Hobart’s rental market is tight, and the two lines newcomers underestimate are heating and the car.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Tasmania: cheaper than the mainland, audited
chunks.x: We used to print a weekly rent and a monthly budget table here. We have taken them out. A figure that was true when a page was written is misleading a year later, and a candidate who plans a move around a stale number is worse off than one who plans around none. What does not go stale is the relationship between places — which suburb, ring or region you choose — and the judgement about which costs catch people out. For today’s actual numbers use the calculators at the foot of the page, and use them to compare it against the city you are leaving. That is the only comparison that decides anything.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Tasmania: cheaper than the mainland, audited
chunks.x: The structural truth holds: like-for-like housing runs well below Sydney and Melbourne, and it is housing that decides whether a salary feels big.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Tasmania: cheaper than the mainland, audited
chunks.x: The costs the postcard hides Day-to-day life here is gentle on the wallet. These three lines are the ones newcomers underestimate, and none of them shows up in a rent comparison. Heating Winter is cold and much of the housing stock is old. A home with a good heat pump can halve the season’s cost — make heating a search criterion, and budget for your first July. The car you’ll definitely own Public transport is light, so a reliable car, registration and insurance belong in the arrival budget, not the month-two surprise. The Spirit brings one over cheaply compared with buying twice. The island premium Everything crosses Bass Strait, so groceries, fuel and trades run slightly dearer than mainland equivalents — and family visits are flights or ferries. Two or three mainland trips a year is the likely budget line.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Tasmania: cheaper than the mainland, audited
chunks.x: Housing is the big one: the gap against Sydney or Melbourne funds the rest of the island life. The short commutes give back time and fuel; school costs are unusually kind here for visa-holder families (Tasmania largely charges a modest levy rather than tuition — the detail lives in Schools & education ); and the free entertainment is world-class, because the national parks are the point of living here. On the income side, public-health roles can salary-package part of your pay before tax — ask payroll on day one, because many international staff set it up months too late. How packaging, tax and superannuation work is national and lives in Pay & conditions . The bottom line Plan the bridge: temporary accommodation, a bond of about four weeks’ rent, the car, the winter kit and the ferry crossing.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Tasmania: cheaper than the mainland, audited
chunks.x: It adds up to less than an east-coast move — and the people who price it before they fly are the ones who arrive calm. Get today’s numbers, and compare them to home These are live and updated continuously. Put the city you are leaving in the other box. Numbeo cost-of-living calculator — the most complete comparison tool, and the one most clinicians already use. Crowd-sourced, so treat it as a ballpark. Expatistan — the same idea with a cleaner side-by-side. Worth running as a sanity check when Numbeo looks off. Australian Bureau of Statistics — official and slower, and the one to trust on the direction of travel. If what you find differs from what we say here, tell us and we will correct it. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Food, produce & the everyday in Tasmania
chunks.x: Tasmania grows what the mainland’s best restaurants serve — the seafood, the cheese, the berries, the whisky — and much of it is sold a few kilometres from where it was made. The everyday food culture here runs on markets, farm gates and a supermarket you’ve never heard of.

chunks.t: Food, produce & the everyday in Tasmania
chunks.h: The markets and the weekly shop
chunks.x: Salamanca Market fills Hobart’s sandstone waterfront every Saturday — part produce market, part makers’ fair, part social institution where you’ll meet half the hospital. The Sunday Farm Gate Market is the cooks’ market, growers only. Launceston’s Harvest Market does the same job in the north each Saturday, and every coast town keeps its own. For the weekly shop: Woolworths and Coles run full-range stores in the cities, ALDI covers the cheapest basket, IGA holds the towns — and the local pride is Hill Street Grocer, the Tasmanian institution that turned the corner shop into something worth crossing town for. In the smaller coast and valley towns, the independent grocer is the town’s living room. Bring your bags Single-use plastic bags are banned; locals keep a boot full of reusables and a cooler bag for the market run.

chunks.t: Food, produce & the everyday in Tasmania
chunks.h: The markets and the weekly shop
chunks.x: The farm-gate habit Cherries in January, apples in April, oysters year-round — buying at the gate is how the island shops, and half the fun of a Sunday drive. The scallop pie Curried scallops in pastry: the state’s bakery signature. Every town claims the best one. Order it once, for citizenship. The whisky is not a gimmick Tasmanian single malts win world awards, and the distillery cellar door is the island’s answer to the brewery tour.

chunks.t: Food, produce & the everyday in Tasmania
chunks.x: Here is the straight answer: the specialist range is smaller than the mainland’s. Hobart and Launceston have a modest spread of Asian and continental grocers and some halal outlets, the big supermarkets carry a growing world-food range — and dedicated kosher and harder-to-find ingredients are often an online order. Most families work out a rhythm within a month: local for fresh, online for the specific, and a list for anyone visiting from Melbourne. The Migrant Resource Centres in Hobart and Launceston are the fastest shortcut to your community’s grocers, cooks and gatherings — worth a visit in week one, whatever your reason.

chunks.t: Food, produce & the everyday in Tasmania
chunks.x: Hobart eats far above its size: the waterfront seafood institutions, North Hobart’s restaurant strip, and a bar scene that MONA dragged into international company. Launceston holds its own with the Tamar’s cellar doors twenty minutes away. Prices sit below Sydney; quality, on the produce’s home ground, often doesn’t. The calendar does the rest. Dark Mofo’s winter feast fills a wharf shed with fire and long tables each June; the Taste of Summer runs across New Year as the Sydney–Hobart yachts arrive; and Launceston’s Festivale fills a park each February. Eating here is seasonal because the island is. The everyday, in one list Saturday: Salamanca in the south, Harvest in the north. Sunday: the Farm Gate, growers only. Cheapest basket: ALDI; the local pride: Hill Street Grocer; the towns: IGA and the independent. Specialist ingredients: Hobart and Launceston grocers first, online for the rest — the Migrant Resource Centre knows the shortcuts. Bags in the boot, a cooler for the market, and a scallop pie at least once. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Tasmania at a glance: geography, seasons & getting on and off
chunks.x: Before the practical chapters, orientation. Tasmania is compact — Ireland-sized, two and a half hours end to end — but it divides, for a newcomer’s purposes, into three quite different places sharing one cool-temperate climate and a ferry line to the mainland.

chunks.t: Tasmania at a glance: geography, seasons & getting on and off
chunks.x: Where Hobart sits, with the straight-line distance to Launceston and Devonport

chunks.t: Tasmania at a glance: geography, seasons & getting on and off
chunks.x: Hobart and its surrounds hold nearly half the state: the harbour city itself, the beach suburbs of Kingston and Blackmans Bay, and the Huon Valley’s orchards and forests half an hour out. This is where the principal referral hospital, the widest job market and most of the island’s cultural life sit — MONA, Salamanca, the festival calendar. If you take a southern post, the mountain and the Tasman Peninsula’s sea cliffs are your local geography.

chunks.t: Tasmania at a glance: geography, seasons & getting on and off
chunks.x: Launceston is the elegant second city — heritage streets, the Cataract Gorge running wild through the middle of town, and the kanamaluka / Tamar Valley’s vineyards all around. It carries the north’s major teaching hospital, noticeably gentler housing costs, and a quietly strong food-and-wine scene. The east coast — Freycinet, the Bay of Fires — is its weekend playground.

chunks.t: Tasmania at a glance: geography, seasons & getting on and off
chunks.x: Devonport, where the Spirit of Tasmania docks, and Burnie, the working port with the coast’s referral hospital, anchor a string of friendly towns along Bass Strait. Behind them the island turns wild: Cradle Mountain ninety minutes inland, and beyond it takayna / the Tarkine, one of the largest temperate rainforests on earth. Health care out here runs on breadth, community and weather-watching.

chunks.t: Tasmania at a glance: geography, seasons & getting on and off
chunks.x: Cool temperate, with four real seasons — closer to England or the South Island of New Zealand than to mainland Australia. Summers are mild and long-lit, with evenings that stay cool; winters are cold, crisp and often blue-skied, with snow settling on kunanyi and the highlands. The weather changes fast in any month: layers and a good jacket are year-round equipment, and the UV is fierce despite the cool air. Summer Dec – Feb 17–23° Mild · light till late Autumn Mar – May 12–18° Still, gold, clear Winter Jun – Aug 4–12° Cold · snow on the tops Spring Sep – Nov 11–17° Fresh, blustery, green Two practical notes, both about winter. Ask how any home is heated before you sign — a heat pump and decent curtains change the season entirely. And if you’ll drive the mountain or highland roads, learn the black-ice habits early; locals will teach you cheerfully.

chunks.t: Tasmania at a glance: geography, seasons & getting on and off
chunks.h: Getting on and off the island
chunks.x: Two clocks matter here: Tasmania runs on the same time as Melbourne and Sydney (AEST, daylight saving included), and Melbourne itself is about 75 minutes’ flight from either Hobart or Launceston, with direct flights on to Sydney, Brisbane and beyond. The Spirit of Tasmania sails overnight between Devonport and Geelong — the practical way to bring a car and your belongings across Bass Strait, and many families’ preferred way to arrive. On the island itself, the road network does the work: Hobart to Launceston is two and a half hours, the east coast about two from either city, and Cradle Mountain ninety minutes from the north-west towns. Getting around has the detail.

chunks.t: Tasmania at a glance: geography, seasons & getting on and off
chunks.h: Words you’ll hear in week one
chunks.x: nipaluna Hobart, in palawa kani — dual naming is official and widely used kunanyi Mount Wellington — “the mountain”, and the city’s weather forecast in one glance takayna The Tarkine — the vast temperate rainforest of the north-west The Spirit The Spirit of Tasmania ferry — how cars, furniture and grandparents cross Bass Strait The mainland Everywhere else in Australia. Said with affection, mostly Salamanca Hobart’s sandstone waterfront row — and the Saturday market that fills it The shack The Tasmanian holiday house — modest, beloved, usually by water Scallop pie The island’s signature bakery order — curried, contested, compulsory once Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Healthcare in Tasmania: how the island system works for clinicians
chunks.x: Registration is national; hiring here is statewide. Tasmania is the one Australian state without a maze of health networks — it runs a single public service — and that shapes careers on the island more than any other fact. This chapter explains how, without naming employers, because our job is to be useful before it is promotional.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Tasmania: how the island system works for clinicians
chunks.h: How the island system is organised
chunks.x: The public system runs as one statewide service under the health department: four principal hospitals — the state referral centre in the capital, a major teaching hospital in the north, and a regional referral centre on the north-west coast working alongside a nearby community hospital — plus district hospitals, community health sites and a state ambulance service. Alongside it sit private and not-for-profit hospitals, mainly in Hobart and Launceston, and Aboriginal community-controlled organisations. One service, one state A single statewide employer for the public system — moving between the south, north and north-west is an internal move, not a new health network. The capital carries the depth The principal referral hospital holds the state’s specialist services — including cardiothoracic surgery, neurosurgery and burns — and the widest range of roles.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Tasmania: how the island system works for clinicians
chunks.h: How the island system is organised
chunks.x: The north stands on its own A teaching hospital serves Launceston and the north-east — a full career base, not a satellite. One national register Ahpra registration works everywhere in Australia. The process, English evidence and assessment pathways live once in Eligibility & registration .

chunks.t: Healthcare in Tasmania: how the island system works for clinicians
chunks.h: What a small system means for a career
chunks.x: Breadth, mostly. With four principal hospitals covering everything from tertiary referral to district care, clinicians here see a wider case mix and carry more responsibility earlier than big-city equivalents — generalist skills are prized, and the far-flung sites run on them. The flipside: some narrow sub-specialties are referred to Melbourne, and a very specific career ladder may need a bigger system. Why Tasmania weighs that trade properly. The social texture matters too. In a system this size you are known — by name, quickly — and the service tends to look after the people it goes to the trouble of recruiting from overseas: relocation support is common, and rural and coastal posts frequently carry incentives. It is also worth saying plainly: the whole of Tasmania is classed as regional for skilled migration, which can open extra visa pathways and points.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Tasmania: how the island system works for clinicians
chunks.h: What a small system means for a career
chunks.x: The detail lives in Visas & the move . Four principal hospitals, one employer Tasmania is the one Australian state without a maze of health networks. That single fact is why a career here can cross the island without ever crossing an employer. The capital The state referral centre, holding the specialist services — cardiothoracic surgery, neurosurgery and burns among them — and the widest range of roles on the island, with the medical school beside it. The north A teaching hospital serving Launceston and the north-east. A full career base rather than a satellite, and a common route in for clinicians arriving from overseas. The north-west coast A regional referral centre working alongside a nearby community hospital. The widest scope of the three, the likeliest incentives, and the lowest housing costs in the state.

chunks.t: Healthcare in Tasmania: how the island system works for clinicians
chunks.h: What a small system means for a career
chunks.x: The district network District hospitals and community health sites across the island, running on exactly the generalist skills this system prizes — and where a great deal of the most satisfying work happens. Because it is one statewide service, moving between these is an internal move, not a new health network — and the seniority and relationships you build travel with you across the island. “ One register, one statewide service, four hospitals. Small is the feature, not the bug. The one-line version

chunks.t: Healthcare in Tasmania: how the island system works for clinicians
chunks.x: Pay follows Tasmanian enterprise agreements — we deliberately quote no figures in this guide, and will always walk you through the current agreement for your profession instead. What you can pin down at interview: Salary packaging — public-health roles can package part of your pay pre-tax; ask how much and how to start it on day one The roster reality — shift patterns, penalties, on-call frequency, and how gaps are covered in a small team Scope and supervision — what you’ll carry, and the support around it, especially in your first year CPD — funded time and money, and whether mainland conference travel is covered (it matters more from an island) Public, private or both — what rights of private practice exist in your profession here For north-west and district posts: the incentive package — relocation, housing help, retention payments Parking and commute at your shift times — short every

chunks.t: Healthcare in Tasmania: how the island system works for clinicians
chunks.x: where, but confirm the site Professional indemnity — what the employer covers and what remains yours to hold Two things to do early Start registration the moment the island is on your shortlist — in a small system, start dates move at the speed of your paperwork. And once you land, sort ambulance cover: it isn’t automatic in Tasmania (free ambulance applies only in some circumstances), and adding it to health insurance is cheap insurance against a very expensive ride. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Tasmania: Hobart’s villages to the north-west coast
chunks.x: On an island where nothing is far from anything, this decision is less about commute than about which Tasmania you want: the harbour city, the beach south, the valley, the elegant north or the working coast. Here is the map as we’d draw it over coffee.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Tasmania: Hobart’s villages to the north-west coast
chunks.x: Battery Point and Sandy Bay hold the postcard — Georgian cottages, the yacht clubs, the university — at the postcard’s prices. West Hobart and New Town trade a little polish for weatherboard character and mountain views; North Hobart adds the island’s best eating strip. Across the bridge, the eastern shore — Bellerive, Lindisfarne — gives water views, morning sun and better value, ten minutes from town. All of it is close to the central hospitals; in Hobart the commute is rarely the deciding factor.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Tasmania: Hobart’s villages to the north-west coast
chunks.h: The beach south and the Huon
chunks.x: Kingston and Blackmans Bay are the family-beach suburbs, twenty minutes south of the wards with surf-lifesaving clubs and newer housing. Keep driving and the Huon Valley opens out — Huonville, Franklin, Cygnet — orchards, artists and river mist, thirty to forty-five minutes from Hobart and beloved of clinicians who want acreage and a wood fire. The trade is the drive, and in winter you’ll make it in the dark both ways. The Tasman Bridge — the eastern shore’s ten-minute link

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Tasmania: Hobart’s villages to the north-west coast
chunks.x: The second city is the island’s quiet bargain: handsome heritage streets, the Cataract Gorge running wild through the middle of town, the Tamar’s vineyards twenty minutes out — and housing that costs noticeably less than Hobart’s. It carries the north’s major teaching hospital and a self-sufficient cultural life. Families settle in Newstead, Trevallyn and East Launceston; the river towns of the Tamar suit those who want vines out the window.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Tasmania: Hobart’s villages to the north-west coast
chunks.x: Devonport (~30,000) is the practical ferry-port base; Burnie (~20,000) the working port with the coast’s referral hospital and a growing arts scene; between and beyond them run friendly towns with Bass Strait at the bottom of the street and Cradle Mountain ninety minutes behind. Housing is among the most affordable in the country, incentives are real, and the community will absorb you fast. Say the hard thing early: specialist services, schooling choices and retail are thinner here, and Hobart is three-plus hours away. The clinicians who thrive on the coast wanted breadth and belonging — not a smaller Hobart.

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Tasmania: Hobart’s villages to the north-west coast
chunks.x: ~A$550 /wk Indicative Hobart house rent (3-bed median) Less In the north, less again on the coast 4 wks Typical bond, lodged with the Rental Deposit Authority If you want… Consider Because The widest job market Hobart’s inner villages The referral centre and most roles Water views on a budget The eastern shore Ten minutes over the bridge, morning sun Beach family life Kingston & Blackmans Bay Surf clubs, newer homes, 20 min south Acreage and orchards The Huon Valley River-valley life, 30–45 min out Heritage value & vines Launceston & the Tamar The quiet bargain with its own hospital Affordability & breadth Devonport & Burnie Coast-town prices, real incentives Renting itself — applications, bonds, rights — works the same across Australia and lives once in Living in Australia .

chunks.t: Where clinicians live in Tasmania: Hobart’s villages to the north-west coast
chunks.x: Two Tasmanian habits worth copying: arrive with references, proof of income and your offer letter as clean PDFs, because Hobart’s tight market rewards the instant, complete application; and ask how every home is heated before you fall for it. Before you sign a lease How is it heated — heat pump, wood, or hope? This is the question in Tasmania. Is the property inside the school catchment you need? Boundaries run street by street. What’s the commute at your shift times — including the bridge, if you’re eastern shore? Would a short-term rental first be wiser? Most people re-choose their suburb once they know the island. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Getting around Tasmania: a car island with short, spectacular drives
chunks.x: Tasmania’s transport truth fits in a sentence: it is a car island with the shortest commutes in the country. The buses are light, there are no passenger trains, and the ferry across Bass Strait is how a household arrives. Plan around those three facts and the island is easy.

chunks.t: Getting around Tasmania: a car island with short, spectacular drives
chunks.x: Metro buses Hobart, Launceston and Burnie run bus networks on the tap-on Greencard. Fine for main corridors and the commute if you live on one; light on evenings and weekends. No trains, no trams Passenger rail ended decades ago. The bus, the bike and the car are the whole menu — choose your suburb accordingly. Small-city cycling Hobart’s intercity cycleway runs flat along the Derwent to the northern suburbs — one of the pleasanter hospital commutes going. Ferries, small and large Hobart’s Derwent ferry links the eastern shore to the waterfront; Bruny’s car ferry runs from Kettering; and the Spirit crosses the Strait. Car-free life is practical in inner Hobart and inner Launceston if you pick your street. Everywhere else — the Huon, the beach south at shift hours, the coast towns — plan on driving from day one.

chunks.t: Getting around Tasmania: a car island with short, spectacular drives
chunks.x: Australians drive on the left, and Tasmania is a gentle place to learn a new country’s roads: light traffic, short distances, and scenery that makes every errand a minor holiday. You can usually drive on a valid overseas licence for a period, then transfer to a Tasmanian licence once resident — the rules, and buying a car, live in Living in Australia . Three local skills. Winter mornings bring black ice on the mountain, highland and valley roads — slow early, brake gently, and take the locals’ advice on chains for the high country. Wildlife moves at dawn and dusk, so country drives at those hours ask for real attention. And the west’s roads are winding and remote: fuel up, download offline maps, and tell someone your plans.

chunks.t: Getting around Tasmania: a car island with short, spectacular drives
chunks.x: From… To… Roughly Hobart Launceston 2.5 hrs Hobart Port Arthur / Tasman Peninsula 1.5 hrs Hobart Freycinet & Wineglass Bay 2.5 hrs Hobart Kingston / the beach south 20 min Launceston The Bay of Fires 2 hrs Devonport Cradle Mountain 1.5 hrs Hobart / Launceston Melbourne, by air ~75 min Devonport Geelong, on the Spirit Overnight or a long day The Spirit of Tasmania deserves its own line: it carries your car, your furniture and the family dog across Bass Strait, and for most relocating households it is the move itself. Book the crossing early in summer. The takeaway Budget for a reliable car before you budget for anything else, pick your suburb for heating and school catchment rather than commute — the commute will be short regardless — and let the Spirit do the heavy lifting on arrival day. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Weekends in Tasmania: wilderness, coast & the seasons
chunks.x: Forty per cent of this island is national park and reserve, and none of it is far away. This chapter is what people do with that — season by season, because in Tasmania the seasons are not weather. They are the calendar. The year, as Tasmanians keep it The island rearranges itself four times a year, and nowhere else in this collection is the gap between February and June this wide. What each quarter does to your plans: Summer Dec – Feb Daylight until nine at night and every track open. Book the east coast months ahead — accommodation there is scarcest and dearest now, and the shacks are all in use. Autumn Mar – May The most settled walking weather of the year, cold nights, and the fagus turning gold in the highlands — Australia’s only native deciduous tree, and a short window. Winter Jun – Aug Short days, snow to low levels and highland roads that want chains or close outright.

chunks.t: Weekends in Tasmania: wilderness, coast & the seasons
chunks.x: Cheapest months to travel, and Ben Lomond’s runs open in a good July. Spring Sep – Nov The windiest and least predictable quarter — four seasons in a day is a literal forecast. Alpine tracks reopen, wildflowers start, and rates stay low until December. Come for a winter interview if you can. Anyone can love Tasmania in February; the question worth answering before you move is how you feel about July. What happens in each season is below.

chunks.t: Weekends in Tasmania: wilderness, coast & the seasons
chunks.x: Cradle Mountain is the postcard for a reason: dolerite spires over a glacial lake, wombats on the boardwalks, and the Overland Track running six days south through the World Heritage wilderness. Ninety minutes from the north-west towns, four hours from Hobart — close enough that locals go for the day and feel slightly guilty about it. Beyond it, takayna / the Tarkine spreads one of the largest temperate rainforests on earth toward a coast that takes the Roaring Forties head-on.

chunks.t: Weekends in Tasmania: wilderness, coast & the seasons
chunks.x: The island’s holiday coast: Freycinet’s pink granite and the climb to the Wineglass Bay lookout, the Bay of Fires’ orange-lichened boulders on white sand, and Maria Island’s car-free wildlife sanctuary a ferry ride out. It is two hours from either city, which is why the Tasmanian shack — the modest family holiday house — clusters here. Summer books out; autumn has the coast to itself.

chunks.t: Weekends in Tasmania: wilderness, coast & the seasons
chunks.x: The everyday wilderness is the island’s quiet luxury. From Hobart: kunanyi’s summit and foothill tracks, Bruny Island’s oysters and sea cliffs via the Kettering ferry, Mount Field’s waterfalls an hour out, and the Tasman Peninsula’s Three Capes cliffs — with Port Arthur’s sobering, essential history — ninety minutes away. From Launceston: the Cataract Gorge is literally in town, the Tamar’s cellar doors twenty minutes out, and Ben Lomond’s ski runs an hour up the hill in a good July.

chunks.t: Weekends in Tasmania: wilderness, coast & the seasons
chunks.x: Winter · Dark Mofo June belongs to MONA’s midwinter festival — fire, art, the nude solstice swim and the Winter Feast. Tasmania doesn’t endure the dark; it throws it a party. Summer · the finish line The Sydney–Hobart fleet arrives between Christmas and New Year as the Taste of Summer fills the docks — the island’s big, bright fortnight. All year · MONA The Museum of Old and New Art — provocative, subterranean, reached by ferry — single-handedly changed how the mainland sees Hobart. Locals get discounted entry and strong opinions.

chunks.t: Weekends in Tasmania: wilderness, coast & the seasons
chunks.x: Cradle Mountain and the Dove Lake circuit, wombats included Freycinet: the Wineglass Bay lookout, then oysters at the water’s edge The Bay of Fires, walked slowly, thermos in hand Bruny Island via the Kettering ferry — cheese, oysters, the Neck at dusk kunanyi’s summit by road, then down the Organ Pipes track Port Arthur and the Tasman Peninsula’s sea cliffs Mount Field: Russell Falls and the tall-tree forests, an hour from town A Tamar Valley cellar-door crawl from Launceston Maria Island’s car-free loop — wildlife at walking pace Dark Mofo’s Winter Feast, booked the week tickets open That’s the guide Nine chapters on Tasmania. Everything national — Medicare, visas, registration, tax, super, schools — lives once in Moving to Australia . When you’re ready to talk about roles on the island, send us your CV . Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Moving to Tasmania: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Tasmania is the deliberate choice. Nobody drifts to an island 240 kilometres off the south coast — you choose it, for the wilderness at the end of the street, the cleanest air on record, and a health system small enough to know your name. This guide is for deciding whether to choose it.

chunks.t: Moving to Tasmania: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: An island that trades scale for life
chunks.x: About 570,000 people share an island the size of Ireland, and nearly half of them live around Hobart — a working harbour city folded between the sea and kunanyi / Mount Wellington, whose summit stands snow-dusted above the office blocks fifteen minutes from town. Launceston anchors the north amid the Tamar wine country; Devonport and Burnie hold the north-west coast where the ferry docks. The state runs a single public health service — four principal hospitals rather than a metropolis full — and that smallness cuts both ways. Careers here are broad rather than narrow, colleagues become neighbours, and the system tends to look after the people it goes to the trouble of recruiting. The trade is the smallest job market in the country, and winters that are cold in a housing stock that wasn’t always built for them.

chunks.t: Moving to Tasmania: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: An island that trades scale for life
chunks.x: What you get back is proximity: Cradle Mountain, Wineglass Bay, the Bay of Fires and a fleet of farm gates, distilleries and cellar doors all sit within a couple of hours of wherever you live. In Tasmania the weekend is not a plan. It is a default. Who wrote this Ethicare is a healthcare recruitment company. This guide is free to read, asks nothing of you, and does not give visa advice. Tasmania is the move people romanticise most and research least. This guide takes the winter, the market size and the island logistics as seriously as the scenery — because the clinicians who thrive here knew exactly what they were choosing.

chunks.t: Moving to Tasmania: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: ~570K People on an island the size of Ireland — Australia’s only island state, across Bass Strait from Melbourne. ~250K In Greater Hobart — the harbour capital and the widest job market on the island. ~90K In Launceston, the elegant second city at the head of the Tamar, two and a half hours north. 4 Principal public hospitals in a single statewide service — the capital, the north, and the north-west coast. ~40% Of the island is national park and reserve, including a World Heritage wilderness a fifth the size of the state. 1,271 m kunanyi / Mount Wellington, rising straight out of Hobart — snow on top, city at its feet, fifteen minutes apart. Cleanest Air on earth, measured at Cape Grim on the north-west tip — the world’s baseline air-quality station. 2.5 hrs Hobart to Launceston by road. Almost nothing on the island is more than four hours from anything else. UTC+10 Same clock as Melbourne and Sydney, daylight saving included — island life, mainland time.

chunks.t: Moving to Tasmania: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: The cold lives indoors Winter is cold, and older weatherboard homes are draughty. Ask how a house is heated before you sign anything, and budget for warm bedding in month one. The UV doesn’t match the air Cool air, fierce sun. The UV here burns fast even when you need a jumper — sun protection is a year-round habit, not a summer one. You’ll want a car Public transport is light. Distances are short and the drives are lovely, but plan on driving from the start — the ferry from Geelong is the easy way to bring one over. It’s a two-degrees island Everyone knows everyone, faster than you expect. You’ll have a community in a month — and a reputation just as quickly. Winter is embraced, not endured Tasmania leans into the dark: Dark Mofo fills June with fire, art and feasting, and the log-fire pub is a genre of its own. The wilderness is serious Mobile coverage drops out fast beyond the towns.

chunks.t: Moving to Tasmania: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.h: Six things you only learn once you’re here
chunks.x: Download offline maps, tell someone your plans, and treat the weather warnings as instructions. A note on Country Hobart stands on the Country of the muwinina people — nipaluna — and today’s Tasmanian Aboriginal community, the palawa/pakana, carries one of the oldest living cultures on earth. Dual names are official and warmly used: nipaluna (Hobart), kunanyi (Mount Wellington), kanamaluka (the Tamar), takayna (the Tarkine). Acknowledgement of Country opens meetings, and health services work in partnership with Aboriginal community-controlled organisations. Learn the names early — using them well is noticed and appreciated.

chunks.t: Moving to Tasmania: a guide for healthcare professionals
chunks.x: Nine chapters, all of them about Tasmania specifically. Anything true of Australia generally — Medicare, visas, Ahpra registration, tax, superannuation, schools — lives once in Moving to Australia . If you read nothing else, read Why Tasmania for the full case — and what we’d ask you to weigh, and Where clinicians live — because Hobart, the north and the coast are three different lives. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Why Tasmania: the case for the island
chunks.x: The island offers what no mainland state can: wilderness at the end of the street, seasons that mean something, and work that’s visible in its community. Here is what Tasmania gives a working clinician, what a week here plausibly looks like — and who we’d steer back to the mainland.

chunks.t: Why Tasmania: the case for the island
chunks.x: Start with the working life. A single statewide service and four principal hospitals mean careers here run broad rather than narrow: you see more, carry more, and are known by name in a way the big-city systems can’t manage. Smaller systems tend to look after the people they recruit — relocation help, warm welcomes, rosters negotiated with a human — because every arrival matters. Pay follows state enterprise agreements in the national range; we quote no figures here and will always walk you through the current agreement instead. Then the life around the work. Housing costs less than the mainland capitals. Commutes are short everywhere. And the island’s real currency is proximity: the mountain fifteen minutes from the wards, the east coast two hours, the wilderness at the end of the street. The whole of Tasmania is classed as regional for skilled migration, which can open extra visa pathways and points. 15 min Hobart’s wards to the mountain road ~40% Of the island is park and reserve 100% Of Tasmania counts as regional for migration

chunks.t: Why Tasmania: the case for the island
chunks.x: A week here can plausibly hold all of this. A shift that starts without traffic, because nowhere in Hobart is far from anywhere else. An after-work walk on kunanyi’s foothill tracks, or a swim at Kingston Beach in the long summer light. Salamanca Market on Saturday morning — produce, makers and half the people you know — then a drive up the Coal River for a cellar-door lunch. Sunday on the Tasman Peninsula under sea cliffs, home by dark. In winter the same week bends rather than breaks: snow on the mountain over breakfast, a log fire in a pub that has kept one burning for a century, and June given over to Dark Mofo’s fires and feasts. People here don’t wait out the seasons. They use them.

chunks.t: Why Tasmania: the case for the island
chunks.x: Four real seasons — autumn is the connoisseur’s pick Russell Falls — World Heritage forest, an hour from Hobart Sophie’s insight What I love about Tasmania is how deliberately people make time for life — a walk up kunanyi, a market on Saturday, a weekend in the wilderness. And in a smaller, close-knit system, you’re valued and looked after in a way the big cities can’t match. My advice: choose the island on purpose. The clinicians who come for the life it offers — seasons included — are among the happiest placements I have anywhere. Sophie Careem Founder & CEO, Ethicare Resourcing

chunks.t: Why Tasmania: the case for the island
chunks.h: Who we’d steer back to the mainland
chunks.x: The market is the country’s smallest One principal referral centre, four main hospitals. A narrow sub-specialty, a very specific career ladder or a two-clinician household may simply need a bigger system. Winter is cold, and so are the houses Cold, dark-by-five winters in a housing stock that can be draughty. If low light flattens you, take that seriously — June here is embraced, but it is still June. Everything crosses the Strait Goods, holidays and family visits all mean a flight or a ferry. If your people are in Sydney or overseas, every reunion is a fare — budget it, emotionally too. It’s quiet Hobart is a small city with a superb food scene, not a metropolis. If big-city churn recharges you, Melbourne is the answer — and it’s 75 minutes away. Hobart’s rentals are tight A small market with strong demand: good homes go fast.

chunks.t: Why Tasmania: the case for the island
chunks.h: Who we’d steer back to the mainland
chunks.x: Arrive with your paperwork ready, and consider the north, where the same money goes further. Where we’d steer you instead If you need scale — sub-specialty depth, two careers, big-system progression — start with Victoria or New South Wales . If the dream is warmth rather than wilderness, read Queensland — Tasmania’s winter is the opposite promise. If you want lifestyle-for-money in a bigger city, South Australia is the closest mainland cousin. In our experience Tasmania suits clinicians who want their work to be visible in a community and their weekends to look like a documentary. The bench is smaller and the flights are real — the people who settle here counted that cost and decided the island was the point. Prefer it on paper? Request the printed guide →

chunks.t: Cost of living in Victoria: the numbers
chunks.x: Victoria’s pitch is a discount, so this chapter prices it. Melbourne runs meaningfully below Sydney on housing while matching it on most everything else — and the regional cities cut the housing line in half again.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Victoria: the numbers
chunks.x: We used to print a weekly rent and a monthly budget table here. We have taken them out. A figure that was true when a page was written is misleading a year later, and a candidate who plans a move around a stale number is worse off than one who plans around none. What does not go stale is the relationship between places — which suburb, ring or region you choose — and the judgement about which costs catch people out. For today’s actual numbers use the calculators at the foot of the page, and use them to compare it against the city you are leaving. That is the only comparison that decides anything.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Victoria: the numbers
chunks.x: Clinical pay is set by state awards and is broadly comparable across the eastern capitals; we don’t print figures until we’ve verified them against the current instruments. What changes between cities is the outgoing side, and one line dominates it: rent or mortgage. The working comparison: inner Melbourne costs like a serious world city; middle-ring Melbourne costs like Sydney’s discount rack; Geelong, Ballarat and Bendigo cost like a different country. The rest of the budget — groceries, transport, utilities — moves far less between them. The Victorian twist on utilities: winter heating is a real line here, the reverse of the northern states’ air-conditioning summers. Old, draughty period homes are the culprits; newer builds and anything renovated hold heat and money better.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Victoria: the numbers
chunks.x: Inner Melbourne — north and south Fitzroy to St Kilda: apartment and terrace territory at the top of the state’s range, still a visible step below equivalent Sydney. Bayside & the school-zone belt Brighton, the south-east spine — the premium is the zone and the beach; houses priced accordingly. The middle north and west Preston, Coburg, Footscray, Yarraville — the value inside ten kilometres, and where most relocating couples land. The growth corridors Point Cook, Werribee, Craigieburn, Clyde — the most house for the money in the metro area; commute and summer heat are the trade. Geelong & the surf coast A clear discount on Melbourne, with the coast attached. Torquay carries a lifestyle premium; Geelong proper does not. Ballarat, Bendigo & the regions Family houses at prices that end the conversation — routinely half the metropolitan equivalent, on commuter rail.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Victoria: the numbers
chunks.x: Three rings, three different countries Monthly rent for the same room or small one-bedroom, at true relative scale. This is the discount Victoria advertises, priced. Inner Melbourne Costs like a serious world city Baseline The middle ring Costs like Sydney’s discount rack ~0.8× Geelong, Ballarat, Bendigo Costs like a different country ~0.6× Melbourne runs meaningfully below Sydney on housing while matching it on most everything else. The regional cities cut the housing line in half again — Geelong with the coast attached, and without Torquay’s lifestyle premium. Indicative prices that change over time. Compare the top and bottom rent lines against the NSW guide’s — that spread is Victoria’s whole argument.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Victoria: the numbers
chunks.x: Winter heating The Victorian speciality. A draughty terrace can double its energy bill in July; ask about heating and insulation before signing anything. School fees on a temporary visa Victoria generally charges nothing: dependants of 482 holders enrol as local students, though school levies and materials still apply. The rule, the exemptions and the other states sit in the master’s School fees on a visa . Health cover for your visa Many visas require private cover, separate from Medicare — national detail, covered in Immigration & visas . The eating-out gravity Melbourne’s food scene is priced for two incomes and zero restraint. It is how budgets quietly fail here, and it is worth a named line in yours.

chunks.t: Cost of living in Victoria: the numbers
chunks.x: Compare cities Numbeo · cost of living Melbourne and Geelong prices against your current city. Plan your budget Moneysmart budget planner The Australian government’s free budgeting tool. Property realestate.com.au Live rents and sales — compare inner, middle and regional early. Master guide The cost of relocating Flights, shipping, bonds and the first ninety days — budgeted once, properly. Sanity check Expatistan A cleaner side-by-side of two cities. Worth running when Numbeo looks off. Official data ABS price indexes Slower than the comparison sites, and the one to trust on the direction of travel. The summary Melbourne gives you a serious city at a real discount on Sydney — but it is a discount, not a bargain.
