chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: At a glance Accredited, not registered Sonography is not a protected title under the National Scheme, so there is no Ahpra board. The route is ASMIRT → ASAR. ASMIRT first, then ASAR ASMIRT issues a Certificate of Recognition in Ultrasound; that certificate supports your ASAR accreditation. Starting the second before the first is complete wastes time. Tied to Medicare An Accredited Medical Sonographer can perform scans that attract Medicare rebates. That is why employers need it — whatever your experience. No exam to fall back on If ASMIRT finds your qualification short, the ask is further evidence, more clinical experience or further education — unlike radiography, there is no standard exam to sit.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Shorter than the Ahpra guides, because the route is simpler than it sounds. Read it once, then return to each section as you reach it. The checklist at the end remembers what you have ticked, on this device. Why sonography is different Step one: ASMIRT assesses your qualification Step two: ASAR accredits you Visas, and how the two connect English and identity Applying, and what happens next Where people get stuck Questions we are asked most The whole journey on one page The checklist — 22 items, tickable Section 01

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Sonographers do not follow the Ahpra registration pathway. Ahpra, through the Medical Radiation Practice Board, registers diagnostic radiography, radiation therapy and nuclear medicine — not sonography. Instead, two organisations share the job. ASMIRT assesses your overseas qualification and experience and, if satisfied, issues a Certificate of Recognition in Ultrasound. ASAR then accredits you as a practitioner, and that accreditation is what lets you scan under Medicare. Public departments and private practices need an accredited sonographer for exactly that reason, so accreditation is not a formality on top of the job — it is the job. ASMIRT qualification assessment → Certificate of Recognition in Ultrasound → ASAR accreditation → Accredited Medical Sonographer — scan under Medicare The order matters. ASMIRT first, then ASAR. ASAR will not accredit you without the ASMIRT certificate, whichever visa you are on — so a well-evidenced ASMIRT application is where almost all of the time you can save sits. Section 02

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Step one: ASMIRT assesses your qualification
chunks.x: The Australian Society of Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy is the gateway. It assesses your qualification against the Australian standard as it stood when you qualified, and reaches one of three outcomes. Outcome 1

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Your qualification and experience meet the standard. The Certificate of Recognition in Ultrasound is issued and you move to ASAR. Outcome 2

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Recognition subject to further evidence or additional clinical experience first. The ask is specific; meet it and the certificate follows. Outcome 3

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: The qualification does not currently support recognition. Unlike radiography there is no standard exam to sit instead — the route back is further evidence, more clinical experience or further education.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Why The basis of the assessment — what you studied, and against which standard. Provide Your ultrasound qualification and the full academic transcript: subjects, results and the grading system. Tip Clean colour scans, certified where required, consistent file names.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Why Recency matters. Skills fade when unused, and ASAR applies its own recency rule later. Provide Evidence of recent clinical ultrasound practice — dates, settings and the modalities you scan. Mistake A CV that lists roles without making the scanning hours and modalities clear.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Why Independent confirmation of what you say you have done. Provide References confirming roles, dates and modalities, from employers or supervisors who can speak to your scanning. Tip Brief your referees on what ASMIRT wants confirmed; a warm but vague letter helps no one. Send us your details before you commit. Where and what you studied decides which outcome is likely, and we will tell you before you pay an assessment fee. The decision itself is ASMIRT’s. Section 03

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Your ASMIRT recognition supports your accreditation with the Australian Sonographer Accreditation Registry. Alongside the certificate, ASAR expects three things. 1

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Citizenship, permanent residency or a valid Australian working visa
chunks.x: You must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen, a permanent resident, or hold a valid Australian working visa. 3

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: ASAR ties this to time away from clinical ultrasound, not to the age of your ASMIRT certificate. If you have not practised clinical ultrasound for three years or more, its Return to Clinical Practice Policy applies and must be met before you resume. The policy sets out what it asks for — read it on ASAR’s own site rather than relying on a summary. Accreditation renews annually. Fees fall due between 1 and 30 April for both Medical and Student Sonographers. ASAR’s published grounds for removal from the Registry are failing CPD requirements and not paying the annual fee, so those are the two things to diarise. Let it lapse and reactivation costs more than renewal. Section 04

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Visas, and how the two connect
chunks.x: The ASMIRT certificate does double duty. It is what ASAR needs, and for a skilled-migration visa it also supports the skills assessment the Department of Home Affairs requires. Most sonographers we place move on an employer-sponsored 482 instead, where the employer sponsors the role and you work toward accreditation alongside. Which visa suits you, and what it requires, is for Home Affairs to decide — not us, and not ASAR. Employer-sponsored 482

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: The route most of the sonographers we place take
chunks.x: The employer sponsors the role. You still need the ASMIRT certificate for ASAR, and your accreditation is renewed each year against a valid visa. Skilled migration — 189, 190, 491

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: The same ASMIRT certificate supports the skills assessment Home Affairs requires. Accreditation still follows through ASAR once you hold the visa or residency. Section 05

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Two things that do not decide the outcome but can hold it up. Certified identity documents — passport, and evidence of any name change if your name differs across documents — go in with both applications, together with certified translations of anything not in English. English-language evidence is a requirement of the ASMIRT assessment itself, not something only your visa or employer asks for. ASMIRT accepts IELTS Academic at 7.0 overall with no element below 7.0, OET at B with no element below B, PTE at 66 with no element below 66, or TOEFL iBT at 94 total. Tests must be sat at a venue — home and online tests are not accepted — and completed within the last two years. Time it so the result is still valid when it is needed. Sitting a test too early. Assembling ASMIRT evidence takes time, so an early test can expire before it is used. Confirm the requirement and the validity period first. Section 06

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Confirm the route and your visa pathway
chunks.x: ASMIRT then ASAR; employer-sponsored or skilled migration. The certificate serves both. 2

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Qualification, transcript, recent scanning practice, references, identity — clean, certified, well named. 3

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Apply to ASMIRT and pay the fee
chunks.x: Then wait for one of the three outcomes. Respond promptly and completely to any request for more. 4

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Certificate of Recognition in Ultrasound issued
chunks.x: Keep it safe; ASAR and, for some visas, Home Affairs rely on it. 5

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: With the certificate, your visa or residency evidence, and recency evidence if the certificate is over three years old. 6

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: The category overseas applicants are accredited into. Renew annually between 1 and 30 April, and keep your CPD current. 7

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Coordinate timelines with your employer. Do not resign or book anything until ASMIRT recognition is confirmed. How long it takes

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: And the order matters. A complete, well-evidenced ASMIRT application is the biggest factor within your control; starting ASAR before ASMIRT is complete saves nothing. Fees

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: The ASMIRT qualification assessment, ASAR accreditation and its annual renewal, plus any English test and document certification. Amounts are not printed here — both organisations publish and revise them. Where people get stuck

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: There is no Ahpra board for sonography. The route is ASMIRT then ASAR.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Starting ASAR before ASMIRT is complete
chunks.x: ASAR will not accredit without the certificate. Sequence, not parallel.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: A CV that does not make recent scanning hours and modalities clear — to ASMIRT now, and to ASAR later if the certificate ages past three years.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Referees who cannot speak to your scanning
chunks.x: References must confirm roles, dates and modalities, not just character.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Assuming an exam can rescue a shortfall
chunks.x: Unlike radiography there is none. A conditional outcome asks for evidence, experience or education.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: Letting the visa lapse at renewal
chunks.x: Accreditation on a working visa renews each year against a valid visa.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: The fix for all of these
chunks.x: Confirm the route, get the ASMIRT evidence right first, line accreditation up with the role and the visa, and have it read by someone else before you submit. Section 08

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: The questions we are asked most
chunks.x: Do sonographers register with Ahpra? No. Sonography is not a protected title under the National Scheme, so there is no Ahpra board for it. The route is ASMIRT recognition of your qualification, then accreditation with the Australian Sonographer Accreditation Registry. Ahpra, through the MRPBA, registers diagnostic radiography, radiation therapy and nuclear medicine. Will my overseas qualification be recognised? That depends entirely on where and what you studied. ASMIRT assesses your qualification against the Australian standard as it stood when you qualified, with three possible outcomes: unconditional recognition; conditional, meaning further evidence or additional clinical experience first; or not recognised. Unlike radiography there is no standard exam you can simply sit if it falls short. Do I need the ASMIRT assessment whichever visa I am on? Yes.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: The questions we are asked most
chunks.x: ASAR will not accredit you without it. It does double duty: for a skilled-migration visa (189, 190 or 491) the same certificate supports the skills assessment Home Affairs requires. On an employer-sponsored 482 the employer sponsors the role and you work toward accreditation alongside. Can I be accredited before I have a visa? ASAR expects you to be an Australian or New Zealand citizen, a permanent resident, or to hold a valid Australian working visa. ASAR’s published grounds for removal from the Registry are failing CPD requirements and not paying the annual fee. Renewal falls due between 1 and 30 April each year, and reactivation after a lapse costs more than renewing on time. What is the recency rule? ASAR ties this to time away from clinical ultrasound, not to the age of your ASMIRT certificate.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: The questions we are asked most
chunks.x: If you have not practised clinical ultrasound for three years or more, its Return to Clinical Practice Policy applies and must be met before you resume. The policy sets out what it asks for — read it on ASAR’s own site rather than relying on a summary. Why does accreditation matter so much? Because it is tied to Medicare. An Accredited Medical Sonographer can perform scans that attract Medicare rebates, which is what public departments and private practices need from you. Without it the role does not work, whatever your experience. How long does it take? Months rather than weeks, and the order matters: ASMIRT first, then ASAR. Starting the second before the first is complete wastes time. A complete, well-evidenced ASMIRT application is the biggest factor within your control. Can Ethicare review my application? Yes.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.h: The questions we are asked most
chunks.x: We review your qualification and experience evidence against what ASMIRT looks for, flag likely issues while they are easy to fix, and line the accreditation up with the role and the visa so they do not hold each other up. The decisions rest with ASMIRT and ASAR. Section 09

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Employer-sponsored or skilled migration; the certificate serves both. Section 04 Preparing

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Qualification, transcript, recent scanning practice, references. Section 02 Applying

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: One of three outcomes; respond fully to any request. Section 02 Milestone

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Certificate, visa or residency, recency if needed. Section 03 Decision

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Get the shape of the route clear before you spend money. Know the route: ASMIRT first, then ASAR Qualification assessment, then accreditation. Not Ahpra. Identify your visa route Employer-sponsored 482, or points-tested skilled migration (189, 190 or 491). The ASMIRT certificate serves both. Note the current fees ASMIRT assessment, ASAR accreditation and its annual renewal — check the live figures on each organisation’s site. Check your recency of practice If your ASMIRT certificate will be over three years old at accreditation, ASAR’s recency rule applies.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: The gateway. Get this moving first. Your ultrasound qualification, certified The qualifying award in medical ultrasound or sonography. Full academic transcript Subjects, results and the grading system. Evidence of recent clinical scanning practice Recency matters — dates, modalities and settings. Professional references confirming roles, dates and modalities From employers or supervisors who can speak to your scanning. Understand the three possible outcomes Unconditional recognition; conditional — further evidence or clinical experience first; or not recognised. Certificate of Recognition in Ultrasound issued Keep it safe. ASAR and, for some visas, Home Affairs both rely on it.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Confirming who you are, and your English where it is required. Certified identity documents Passport, plus evidence of any name change. English-language evidence, where required Required by ASMIRT, not just by your visa. IELTS Academic 7.0 with nothing below 7.0, or OET B throughout. At a venue, within the last two years. Certified translations of any non-English documents Supplied with the certified original.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: Your ASMIRT recognition supports the application. ASMIRT Certificate of Recognition in Ultrasound Required — ASAR will not accredit without it. Citizenship, permanent residency or a valid Australian working visa One of the three is required. Meet the recency rule if your certificate is over three years old About a year part-time or six months full-time in clinical ultrasound within the last three years — or the return-to-practice policy applies. Submit the accreditation application and fee Confirm the current figure on ASAR’s site first.

chunks.t: Sonographer accreditation: ASMIRT and ASAR
chunks.x: What follows accreditation. Accredited Medical Sonographer status confirmed You can now scan under Medicare. Renew annually, 1–30 April Keep CPD current and pay on time — those are ASAR’s published grounds for removal. Keep your CPD current Accreditation carries ongoing professional development obligations — check ASAR’s current requirements. Secure your role and confirm sponsorship Coordinate accreditation and visa timelines with your employer. Don’t make irreversible moves too early Wait until ASMIRT recognition is confirmed before you resign or book anything. Print or save as PDF What next?

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: At a glance Registration and migration are separate The Board registers you to practise. ASMIRT assesses skills for certain visas. A positive migration assessment does not grant registration, and registration does not by itself satisfy migration. Three divisions, one Board Diagnostic radiographer, radiation therapist, nuclear medicine technologist — distinct registrations. You register in the division your qualification supports. Check the fast lane first — if your division has one Qualifications accredited by the UK’s HCPC (2010–2030) or Ireland’s CORU (2013–2030) are treated as substantially equivalent, generally with no portfolio assessment and no exam. This route is for diagnostic radiographers and radiation therapists only . The Board states it is unavailable for nuclear medicine technologists. Registration is national; radiation licensing is not Each state or territory licenses the use of radiation separately. You will usually need both, and employers normally guide you through the local one.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: If you remember one thing, make it Section 01. Everything else follows from getting those two processes in the right order. The checklist at the end remembers what you have ticked, on this device. Two separate processes The Board, and what it does Is my qualification recognised? chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: These are two separate assessments, run by different bodies for different reasons, and the outcomes can differ. 1 · Lets you practise

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: Professional registration — Ahpra and the MRPBA
chunks.x: The Board assesses whether you meet the registration standards required to practise. Without MRPBA registration you cannot legally work in Australia as a medical radiation practitioner — whatever your visa says. It considers your formal qualifications only. 2 · For certain visas

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: Migration skills assessment — ASMIRT or ANZSNM
chunks.x: Required for some skilled-migration visa pathways, and which body assesses you depends on your division : ASMIRT for diagnostic radiographers and radiation therapists, ANZSNM for nuclear medicine technologists. Its purpose is immigration, not registration. It can weigh your work experience as well as your qualifications — which is why the two outcomes can differ. The key point. A positive migration skills assessment does not grant registration, and registration does not by itself satisfy migration requirements. Some people are approved for skilled migration and still have to meet the Board’s registration requirements. Section 02

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: The MRPBA sits within the National Registration and Accreditation Scheme, administered by Ahpra. You must be registered to use the title and to work in the role.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Diagnostic radiographer, radiation therapist and nuclear medicine technologist — distinct registrations with distinct education pathways. You register in the division your qualification supports.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: Registration is national. Radiation licensing is not.
chunks.x: MRPBA registration applies Australia-wide. Using radiation is licensed separately by each state or territory, so you will usually also need a radiation-use licence where you work. Employers normally guide you through the local one. Is my qualification recognised? → Submit to Ahpra / MRPBA → Assessment — exam if required → Registration granted → State radiation licence → Practise Section 03

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: If the Board already recognises your qualification, that is the quickest route. Otherwise it assesses your portfolio and reaches one of three outcomes. The fast lane — comparable regulators. If your qualification was accredited by a regulator the Board recognises as comparable for your division, within its published date ranges, it is treated as substantially equivalent and you are qualified for general registration — generally without a portfolio assessment or the National exam. This currently includes qualifications approved by the UK’s HCPC and Ireland’s CORU within the Board’s date ranges, plus a list of specific recognised qualifications by institution and award year. The match has to be exact — division, institution, award title and year. Check your own position on the Board’s “Is my qualification recognised?” page before assuming either way.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: Substantially equivalent, or based on similar competencies
chunks.x: Meets the full set of criteria. The most direct route toward general registration. s.53(c) National Law

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Meets the threshold criteria but not full equivalence. Registration is still possible, typically with an additional step such as the National examination. Threshold not met

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: The minimum threshold criteria are not met, so the qualification does not currently support registration in the division. Recognition is always subject to the Board’s assessment of your individual evidence, and the recognised lists and date ranges are reviewed periodically — confirm your position against the Board’s current page. Section 04

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Your qualification was recognised by a registration or licensing body for the profession where you trained, and you met any pre-registration assessment there — or, where there is no such body, it enabled you to practise. 2

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Your programme was externally accredited against published education standards, including contemporary evidence-based practice and work-integrated clinical learning. 3

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: AQF level 7 — an Australian bachelor’s degree — is the bar for a substantially equivalent outcome. A qualification one level lower, or AQF 5 from a comparable regulator jurisdiction, can still be assessed as relevant to the profession . So AQF 7 is the fast-lane threshold, not the minimum to be considered at all.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: The core topics the Board looks for
chunks.x: Across all divisions: anatomy, physiology and pathology; principles of patient care; clear communication; medical radiation physics; safe radiation practice; CT imaging; and the safe use of medicines including contrast media. Then the division’s own. Diagnostic radiographer

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: The examinations the Board expects a diagnostic radiography or medical imaging degree to have covered. Radiation therapist

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Radiation therapy planning, treatment delivery and treatment verification. Nuclear medicine technologist

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Radiopharmaceuticals and SPECT and PET imaging. In our experience. It is easy to assume registration is just paperwork. It isn’t — it is a real assessment of whether your training meets the Australian standard. The part you control most is the part that matters most: complete, well-organised documents, sent early. Section 05

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: It exists to confirm that practitioners whose qualifications are not assessed as substantially equivalent still meet the Australian standard before registration. Not everyone sits it. Applicants already recognised as substantially equivalent — including those accredited by a comparable regulator within the date ranges — generally are not required to. Where a qualification is assessed as “relevant to the profession” rather than fully equivalent, you must pass the National exam for medical radiation practice before you can apply for registration. It is not optional for that outcome. What is uncertain is which outcome you receive, not whether the exam follows one.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Where required it is a written, knowledge-based assessment: a component common across the divisions, a component specific to yours, and Australian-context material — radiation safety legislation, the professional capabilities, culturally safe practice — alongside clinical knowledge you will already recognise. Confirm the current format. Structure, components and pass requirements are set by the Board and reviewed periodically. Check its National exam pages before you prepare — no format is reproduced here for exactly that reason. Section 06

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: All applicants must satisfy the MRPBA’s English Language Skills Registration Standard. It sets out the recognised ways to demonstrate English — an approved test result, or one of several exemption pathways, for example where your education was conducted and assessed in English in a recognised country. No scores or exemption criteria are reproduced here, deliberately. The Board reviews the standard periodically and the accepted tests and pathways change — the minimum scores did in April 2026. Read the current standard before you book any test, and if you need one, time it so the result is still valid when your application reaches the Board. Section 07

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: A clean, complete pack is the biggest factor within your control on timing: certified copies, not copies of certified copies, and clean high-resolution scans. Passport and proof of identity Certified, with evidence of any name change. Degree certificate Your qualifying award in diagnostic radiography or medical imaging, radiation therapy, or nuclear medicine technology. Academic transcript Full record of subjects, results and the grading system. Clinical placement evidence Evidence of supervised clinical training, where required. Registration history Your professional registration and licensure record. Certificate of Good Standing From each authority you are registered with, and current at submission. Employment history and CV Roles, dates and responsibilities, up to date, with no unexplained gaps. English language evidence If required under the registration standard. Translations Certified, supplied together with the certified original of any non-English document. Section 08

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Most people we support relocate under an employer-sponsored visa. On that pathway MRPBA registration is the priority, because it is what allows you to practise. Your employer sponsors the role; the Board registers the practitioner. Both have to happen, and they are separate workstreams. An ASMIRT migration skills assessment is not generally required simply to obtain registration on a 482. ASMIRT’s assessment is a migration step tied to particular visa pathways — most often the points-tested skilled-migration visas, 189, 190 and 491. That is not a blanket “ASMIRT is never required.” Additional migration assessments may be needed if you later pursue permanent skilled migration or a different visa. Confirm what applies to you with your employer and the Department of Home Affairs — that is their call, not ours, and not the Board’s. Before you apply

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Check recognition — is your qualification already on the Board’s lists? Understand your pathway — recognised, portfolio assessment, and whether the exam is likely. Gather your documents. Decide your visa route — employer-sponsored 482 or skilled migration, which decides whether ASMIRT applies. Then talk to us: we confirm the pathway, help secure the role and sponsorship, and review your evidence before you submit. Section 09

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: On a 482 it generally is not, for registration — but it can be for other visa pathways. Confirm yours.

chunks.x: Whether the National exam applies depends on your assessment outcome. Do not assume either way.

chunks.x: Check the current registration standard before booking, and time it so it stays valid.

chunks.h: The fix for all of these
chunks.x: Understand the two processes, get your qualification assessed early, prepare complete documents, and confirm your visa route with your employer. Section 11

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: The questions we are asked most
chunks.x: Do I need an ASMIRT assessment to register? Not generally. The MRPBA assesses your qualification for registration; ASMIRT conducts skills assessments for migration purposes tied to certain visa pathways. On an employer-sponsored 482 an ASMIRT assessment is not generally required just to register, but it may be needed for other migration routes. So who assesses my qualification? For registration, the MRPBA does, through Ahpra. That assessment determines your pathway and whether you need to sit the National exam. Will I have to sit the National examination? It depends on your qualification and the outcome of the Board’s assessment. Some applicants are required to; others are not. Your assessment confirms it — do not assume either way. What English evidence do I need? You must satisfy the Board’s English Language Skills Registration Standard.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: The questions we are asked most
chunks.x: The accepted tests and exemption pathways are set in that standard and reviewed periodically, so confirm the current requirements before booking anything. How long does registration take? It varies with the completeness of your application, document verification and your circumstances. A complete, well-evidenced submission is the best way to keep things moving. Is registration the same as a radiation licence? No. MRPBA registration is national and lets you practise; using radiation is licensed separately by each state or territory. You may need both, and your employer will usually help with the local licence. Can I start applying for jobs before I am registered? You can start the conversation early, and many employers support you through the process.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: The questions we are asked most
chunks.x: But a lot of Australian employers expect registration to be in place, or well under way, before they finalise a role — so get the MRPBA application moving first. We line the two up so they do not hold each other up. Can Ethicare help with all of this? Yes. We help secure the role and sponsorship, and guide the preparation and timing of your registration, flagging issues while they are still easy to fix. The registration decision always rests with the Board. Section 12

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Getting this clear saves time and money. Know that registration and migration are separate MRPBA registration lets you practise; an ASMIRT assessment is a migration step. Confirm MRPBA registration is your priority It is the thing that allows you to work in Australia. Identify your visa route Employer-sponsored 482, or points-tested skilled migration (189, 190 or 491). Check whether an ASMIRT assessment applies to you Generally not required for registration on a 482 — confirm with your employer or adviser.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: 02 Check whether your qualification is already recognised
chunks.x: The fast lane. Establish this early, because it decides how much of the rest applies. Confirm your division Diagnostic radiographer, radiation therapist or nuclear medicine technologist — the one your qualification supports. Use the Board’s “Is my qualification recognised?” page It may already recognise your qualification, which changes everything below. Check the comparable-regulator lists UK HCPC (2010–2030) and Ireland CORU (2013–2030). Diagnostic radiography and radiation therapy only — this route is not available to nuclear medicine technologists. Check the recognised-qualifications list It must match exactly on division, institution, award title and year. Note whether a portfolio assessment is needed Required if your qualification is not already recognised.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: What the Board weighs if it assesses your portfolio. Professional registration evidence Recognised by a registration or licensing body where you trained. Quality assurance and accreditation evidence An externally accredited programme, assessed against published standards. Check your educational level against both bars AQF level 7 is the threshold for a substantially equivalent outcome. One level lower, or AQF 5 from a comparable regulator jurisdiction, can still be assessed as relevant to the profession. Core topics covered, including your division’s own Projection radiography and fluoroscopy; or treatment planning, delivery and verification; or radiopharmaceuticals, SPECT and PET.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Only if it applies to you under the registration standard. Read the English Language Skills Registration Standard Confirm the currently accepted tests and exemptions on the standard itself. Provide an approved test result, if no exemption applies Meet the minimum in every component, not just overall. Check your results are still valid at submission Time the test so it cannot expire before you apply.

chunks.t: MRPBA registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: It depends on your assessment outcome — not everyone sits it. Confirm whether the exam applies to you Comparable-regulator and recognised-qualification applicants are generally exempt. Check the current format on the Board’s exam pages A component common to all divisions and one specific to yours; structure and pass requirements are set by the Board. Prepare for the Australian-context content Radiation safety legislation, the professional capabilities, and cultural safety.

Degree certificate and full academic transcript Showing subjects, results and the grading system. Clinical placement evidence Evidence of supervised clinical training, where required. Registration history and Certificate of Good Standing From each authority you are registered with, and current at submission. Employment history and up-to-date CV Roles, dates and responsibilities, with no unexplained gaps. Certified translations of non-English documents Supplied together with the certified original.

chunks.x: Submitting the registration application itself. Complete the overseas-qualified application Select your division. Pay the application and registration fee Non-refundable — confirm the current figures on the Board’s fees page. Submit a complete, well-organised pack Certified copies, clear scans, consistent file naming. Respond promptly to any Board queries Incomplete applications are the most common cause of delay.

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: At a glance The College advises, the Board decides RANZCR assesses how comparable your training is to an Australian radiologist’s. The Medical Board makes the registration decision on that advice. Most people take the specialist pathway A RANZCR comparability assessment, then a period of supervised practice in Australia, then full specialist registration. Trained in Canada? Check the fast track Since 1 July 2026 the Canadian Royal College specialist certificate in diagnostic radiology is on the Board’s Expedited Specialist pathway. It is the only radiology qualification on that list at present. Registration is not the same as Medicare Section 19AB decides where an overseas trained doctor can bill Medicare for ten years. Check the role’s location before you accept it.

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: If you remember one thing, make it Section 01: which route is yours. Everything else follows from it. The checklist at the end remembers what you have ticked, on this device. Which route is yours The RANZCR assessment The three outcomes The Expedited Specialist pathway Your registration along the way English language Your supporting documents Medicare and where you can work The visa Where people get stuck Questions we are asked most The whole journey The checklist Section 01 · The one that matters most

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: There are three ways in for a radiologist who trained overseas. Which one applies depends on where you trained and what you already hold, not on the job you are offered. Most people

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: RANZCR assesses your training and experience and finds you substantially comparable, partially comparable or not comparable. You then practise under supervision in Australia before the Board grants full specialist registration. This is the route for radiologists trained in the UK, Ireland, South Africa and most other countries. Canadian-trained

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: If you hold the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada specialist certificate in diagnostic radiology, for training that began on or after 1 July 2002, you can apply to the Board directly, without a college comparability assessment. Section 04 explains how it works. Already a Fellow

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: RANZCR is a joint college for Australia and New Zealand. If you are already a Fellow, you hold the Australian specialist qualification and apply to the Board for specialist registration in the usual way. Recruited for a regional shortage role? If an employer offers you a post the College accepts as an area of need, RANZCR can assess you for that position and for comparability at the same time. That assessment includes an interview, clinical case scenarios and film reading. It is a way into a specific role, not a different end point: the aim is still full specialist registration. Section 02

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: The College compares your training and experience with those of a radiologist trained in Australia, from your paperwork first, then in an interview. 1

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Your primary medical degree and your specialist qualification are verified directly with the institutions that awarded them. This is done through the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG), using its MyIntealth service. Start early: it depends on universities and colleges replying. 2

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: Open an Australian Medical Council portfolio
chunks.x: The AMC portfolio holds your verified documents and links your application across the Board and the College. 3

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: You send the College its specialist recognition application form with your supporting documents. Once the application is complete, the College invoices you for the assessment. 4

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Two Fellows of the College, both trained assessors, interview you online. It is a structured conversation about your training, your experience and the work you do now. 5

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: The College decides how comparable you are and tells the Board. That finding decides what you need to do in Australia before full specialist registration. Verify qualifications → AMC portfolio → RANZCR application → Interview → Outcome → Supervised practice → Specialist registration Section 03

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Up to 12 months of peer review in a RANZCR-accredited training site, practising as a consultant with oversight. When the College confirms you have met its requirements, you apply for full specialist registration. Partially comparable

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Up to 24 months of upskilling before you sit the College’s Part or Phase 2 examinations. It is a longer road, and worth planning around: the role you take needs to support it. Not comparable

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: The College refers you back to the Medical Board, which can tell you about other options for medical registration. The specialist pathway is not the route on the evidence provided. Before you resign or sell anything. Wait for your outcome. A partially comparable finding changes your timeline, your role and sometimes your pay, and it is much easier to plan around before you have committed to a date. Section 04

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: The Medical Board opened this pathway in October 2024 for specialists whose qualifications it has already judged substantially equivalent to Australia’s. Diagnostic radiology joined it on 1 July 2026. The qualification on the list for radiology is the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada specialist certificate in diagnostic radiology , for an accredited Canadian residency that began on or after 1 July 2002. At present it is the only radiology qualification on the list. If you trained in the UK, Ireland or elsewhere, the RANZCR specialist pathway in Sections 02 and 03 is your route. On the expedited pathway you apply to the Board directly, without a college comparability assessment. You are then supervised for six months by an Australian-registered specialist, complete an orientation to the Australian health system and do the Board’s mandatory cultural safety education.

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Because the supervision happens in a job, you need a role lined up. Everything else is the same as for any other doctor: the English language, criminal history and recency of practice standards all apply. The list grows. The Board adds specialties and qualifications as the Australian Medical Council assesses them. If yours is not on the list today, check again before you apply. Section 05

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: On the specialist pathway you do not start on full specialist registration. You hold an interim registration while you complete what the College asks of you. 1

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: If you are substantially or partially comparable, you need a role, and the Board approves both the position and the supervision arrangements for it. 2

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: The Board grants provisional or limited registration for your period of supervised practice. The Board describes this as lasting between three and 24 months, depending on what the College requires. 3

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: When the College confirms you have met its requirements, you apply to the Board for specialist registration in diagnostic radiology. Section 06

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: Every doctor registering in Australia has to meet Ahpra’s English language skills standard, and the expedited pathway is no exception. There are two broad ways to meet it. If you completed your education in English in one of the countries Ahpra recognises, you may not need to sit a test; that list was widened in 2025, so check it even if you were told otherwise before. South Africa was removed from it at the same time, so if you trained there, check the transition arrangements before you assume you are exempt. Otherwise you sit one of the accepted tests and reach the scores the standard sets. We do not print the scores here because Ahpra revises them. Read the current standard before you book a test, and time the test so your result is still valid when you apply. Section 07

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.x: A clean, complete pack is the biggest thing within your control on timing. Certified copies, clear high-resolution scans, consistent names and every page included. Passport and proof of identity Certified, with evidence of any change of name. Primary medical degree Verified at source through the ECFMG, with your transcript. Specialist qualification Your radiology fellowship or certificate and, where your country issues one, your certificate of completion of training. Also verified at source. Training record Your specialist training programme, rotations and assessments, in enough detail for the College to compare it. Experience since training A structured CV showing your consultant posts, modalities, subspecialty work and reporting volumes, with no unexplained gaps.

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist

chunks.t: Radiologist registration guide and checklist
chunks.h: Medicare, and where you can work
chunks.x: Registration lets you practise. Whether you can bill Medicare, and where, is a separate question decided by section 19AB of the Health Insurance Act. Section 19AB applies to every doctor who qualified overseas. For ten years from your first medical registration in Australia, you can generally only access Medicare benefits in areas classed as having a shortage. For specialists other than GPs, those areas are called Districts of Workforce Shortage, and each specialty has its own map. Diagnostic radiology is assessed separately from other specialties, so a town that is a shortage area for one specialty may not be for radiology. The ten years can be shortened by working in more remote areas, and work in a public hospital that does not bill Medicare is not restricted. This matters most in private practice, where your reports are billed to Medicare.

chunks.h: Medicare, and where you can work
chunks.x: Before you accept a role, ask the employer to confirm the location’s status for diagnostic radiology, or search the Health Workforce Locator by specialty yourself. Once you are registered, you apply to Services Australia for a Medicare provider number. One more licence to know about: each state and territory regulates the use of radiation separately, and doctors who operate radiation equipment, for example in fluoroscopy or interventional work, generally need a licence under the local rules. Your employer will usually tell you what applies where you are going. Section 09

The Department of Home Affairs sets the visa rules and publishes them in full. Visa agents can be expensive and are not always necessary; many people apply themselves with their employer’s help. If your situation is complicated, a registered migration agent can advise you, and Home Affairs explains how to check that an agent is registered. Before you apply

chunks.x: I trained in the UK. Can I use the expedited pathway? Not at present. For diagnostic radiology, the only qualification on the Board’s expedited list is the Canadian Royal College specialist certificate. UK-trained radiologists go through the RANZCR specialist pathway. The Board adds qualifications over time, so it is worth checking the list again before you apply. Who decides whether I am comparable? RANZCR assesses you and advises the Medical Board, which makes the registration decision. Can I work while I complete supervised practice? Yes. Supervised practice happens in a real role, on provisional or limited registration, with supervision the Board has approved. That is why the role and the registration need to be lined up together. What does partially comparable mean for me? The College asks for up to 24 months of upskilling before you sit its Part or Phase 2 examinations.

chunks.h: Registration is what lets you practise, and it’s very doable
chunks.x: Reviewed July 2026 · checked against the current published guidance of the relevant Australian national board or accrediting authority Australia runs one national scheme, so registration is recognised in every state and territory. For most medical-imaging professions that means Ahpra and the MRPBA. The one thing to hold onto: registration lets you practise; a visa lets you live and work here. They’re separate, run by different bodies, and getting them in the right order is most of the battle. We’ll come to visas in Stage 07; this stage is about the right to practise.

chunks.t: Can I work in Australia? Registration
chunks.h: “Can I work there?” is four questions, and registration is one of them
chunks.x: Ahpra and your National Board decide whether you can practise. Whether you can live and work in Australia at all is decided elsewhere, and each part has its own owner. This page is the first. Registration — the right to practise. This page, then your profession . The visa — the right to live and work here, decided by the Department of Home Affairs, not the board, and for most clinicians sponsored by an employer. A skills assessment for migration is a third, separate thing. Immigration & visas owns all of that. English, health and character — asked by the board and by Home Affairs in slightly different forms. English requirements . Time and money — months rather than weeks, with fees at each stage. How long it takes ; what it costs sits in Make the numbers work .

There’s a second thing worth knowing early: for the professions that use radiation, national registration is separate from a state radiation use licence . Registration is Australia-wide; the licence to operate radiation equipment is issued by each state or territory, and your employer usually helps you arrange it. The distinction that trips people up

Our job is to tell you, which pathway is yours, help secure the role and sponsorship, and flag issues while they’re still easy to fix. chunks.t: Can I work in Australia? Registration
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Is my registration valid in every state? Yes. Australia’s registration is national, so once you’re registered (or accredited, for sonographers) it’s recognised in every state and territory. The exception is the radiation use licence, which is issued by each state separately for the professions that operate radiation equipment. Do I need to sit an exam? It depends on your profession and how your qualification is assessed. Applicants recognised through a comparable regulator (such as the UK’s HCPC or Ireland’s CORU, for radiographers and radiation therapists) are generally exempt; others may sit the national MRP examination. Your profession page explains what’s likely for you. Can I start applying for jobs before I’m registered? You can, and many employers will support you through the process.

chunks.t: Can I work in Australia? Registration
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: That said, Australian employers generally expect your registration to be in place or well underway, so it’s wise to get your application moving first. We help line the role, the registration and the visa up so they don’t hold each other up. How long does it take? It varies with the completeness of your application, document verification and your circumstances. The single biggest lever is a complete, well-evidenced submission, and starting the slowest items (certificates of good standing, document verification) early. Do I need a skills assessment as well? Only if your visa route requires one. On an employer-sponsored route it generally isn’t needed just to register. For points-tested skilled visas it is, and it’s done by a separate authority: ASMIRT for radiographers and radiation therapists, ANZSNM for nuclear medicine. Two different processes, often confused.

chunks.t: Can I work in Australia? Registration
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: What if I’ve had a break from practice? It’s common and it’s manageable. Boards apply a recency of practice standard, so a significant break usually means more evidence about what you’ve been doing, and occasionally a period of supervised practice. Tell us early and we’ll be straight with you about what it’s likely to mean. Will my overseas CPD count? Generally yes, and it’s worth having your records in order. Keep evidence of what you’ve completed and when. Once registered you’ll meet Australian CPD requirements going forward, which most clinicians find familiar rather than onerous. What does it cost? There’s an application fee and then annual renewal, plus the costs around it: document verification, certificates of good standing, any English test, and a state radiation licence where one applies.

chunks.t: Can I work in Australia? Registration
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: None of it is unaffordable, but it adds up, so budget for the whole set rather than the headline fee. Do you charge me for any of this? No. Our support is free to you, employers pay us. The boards, assessment authorities and test providers charge their own fees, and we’ll tell you which are coming before they arrive. Next · Stage 06

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Reviewed July 2026 · general guidance only. Rules on visas, licences, pets and tax differ by state and change over time, check the official sources linked below for your own circumstances. This is the step where people either feel organised or overwhelmed, and the difference is almost never how capable they are. It’s whether the long-lead items. Pets, freight, school places, a rental, were started early enough that they weren’t all happening in the last fortnight. Every region is a little different on housing, schools and the cost of getting set up, which is why we’ll point you to a relocation guide for your state as those are published. This step is the national overview that sits behind them. Order of operations

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Registration and visa are already running. Alongside them: begin the pet import process if you’re bringing an animal, it is the longest lead time of anything on this list and cannot be rushed. Get quotes for freight. Order official copies of documents you’ll need: birth and marriage certificates, qualifications, children’s school reports and immunisation records, driving licences and history, references. If you rent, check your notice period. If you own, start the conversation with an agent about selling or letting. 6–8 wk

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Open an Australian bank account, many banks allow this from overseas. Book short-term accommodation for landing (four to six weeks is a sensible window). Start contacting schools about places and enrolment. Book freight if you’re shipping. Confirm what health cover you need in place on arrival. Tell utilities, insurers, banks and your GP at home what’s happening, and get copies of your medical and dental records for everyone in the family. 2–4 wk

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Book flights once your visa is granted, not before. Confirm your first day with your employer and what they need from you. Cancel or transfer subscriptions, memberships and insurance. Arrange mail redirection. Sort a plan for money in the first month: cleared funds in your Australian account before you land is the goal. Final wk

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: Hand luggage matters more than you think
chunks.x: Passports and visa evidence, all original certificates, medical summaries and prescriptions, your children’s immunisation records, employer contact details, accommodation details, and enough medication for the transition. Everything else can be replaced; these can’t easily be. Week 1

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Local SIM, activate the bank account, apply for a Tax File Number, enrol in Medicare if you’re eligible, register the family with a GP, and start the rental search in person. Also: find your nearest emergency department and check how ambulance works in your state. Then stop and go and look at something beautiful, you’ve earned it. Get the admin moving

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: A few accounts and numbers make everything else possible, and several can be started before you land. Banking

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Many Australian banks let you open an account from overseas weeks before you arrive, then activate it with your passport once you’re here. Your salary and rent then have somewhere to land from day one. Tax

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Apply for a TFN once you arrive. It’s needed for pay and tax. Without it you’re taxed at the top rate and have to claim the difference back, so it’s a first-week job, not a first-month one. Super

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Employers pay compulsory superannuation on top of your wage. Retirement savings that are yours. You’ll nominate a fund or be assigned one when you start. It is real money, so it is worth knowing how it works.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: Three things people wish they’d known
chunks.x: Moving money costs more than you expect. High-street bank transfer rates are rarely the best available, and on the sums involved in a relocation the difference is meaningful. Compare a specialist transfer service, and split the transfer rather than moving everything on one day’s exchange rate. Your credit history doesn’t travel. However established you are at home, you arrive with no Australian credit file. That affects phone contracts, car finance and sometimes rental applications. It builds quickly, but the first few months can feel oddly like being twenty-two again. Mind the gap before your first pay. Between landing costs and your first Australian pay cycle there can be four to six weeks of outgoings with nothing coming in. That gap, plus a rental bond and several weeks’ rent up front, is the single most common cause of relocation stress we see. Plan the buffer properly and almost everything else is manageable. Health cover from the start

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: How you access healthcare depends on your visa and your passport, so it’s worth sorting before you need a GP, not after.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Australia’s public scheme. Citizens and permanent residents enrol. Many temporary visa holders qualify through one of Australia’s eleven reciprocal health care agreements, enrolment happens after you arrive, with passports, visa evidence and an Australian address.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Many temporary work visas require you to hold and maintain adequate cover for the whole stay. Medicare-eligible families often take cover anyway, for shorter elective waits and extras toward dental and optical. Check the waiting periods before you choose a policy.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Bring a written summary of everyone’s medical and dental history and current prescriptions, plus immunisation records for the children (schools ask). Check your medicines against the PBS before you travel, brand names differ. The full picture. Eligibility, bulk billing, the PBS, ambulance by state and what Medicare doesn’t cover, is in Understanding healthcare in Australia . It’s worth twenty minutes before you accept an offer. Where you’ll land

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Book short-term accommodation for four to six weeks and house-hunt on the ground. Photographs flatter, commutes deceive, and a suburb that looks right on a map can feel wrong in person. Almost nobody regrets renting first; plenty regret signing early. Applying

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Rental markets in the major cities are tight, and viewings can be brief and busy. Have a folder ready: identification, your employment contract or offer letter, references from previous landlords or agents, and bank statements. Applying the same day you view is normal. Money up front

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Expect to pay a bond (held, and returned at the end if all is well) plus rent in advance. Rent here is usually quoted and paid weekly or fortnightly rather than monthly, which catches people out when they budget. Ask exactly what’s due before you sign. The no-rental-history problem. With no Australian tenancy record and no local credit file, good applicants can still be passed over. Two things help more than anything: a letter from your employer confirming the role and salary, and written references from previous landlords or agents with contactable details. Have both before you land. Furnished or not. Most long-term rentals are unfurnished, and often without white goods. If your freight is weeks behind you, plan for a period of camping in your own home, or budget for second-hand basics, a very well-served market here. For the children

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: For public schools, where you live usually determines where children go, so the suburb decision and the school decision are the same decision. 1

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Public schools generally enrol from a defined local catchment. Confirm the zone before you commit to a lease, not after, and confirm it with the school or the state education department rather than a property listing. 2

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Independent and faith-based schools enrol on their own terms, often with waiting lists and fees. If that’s your preference, start the conversation months out. 3

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: Fees can apply on temporary visas
chunks.x: Public schooling is generally free for citizens and permanent residents. Some states charge fees for children of temporary visa holders, and the rules differ state by state. Check yours specifically, it can be a significant annual figure. 4

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: The school year runs late January to December
chunks.x: Four terms, with the long summer holiday over Christmas and January. If your children are mid-year in the northern hemisphere, they may join part-way through a year, or be placed by age rather than by year completed. Schools handle this constantly and handle it well. 5

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Immunisation records, recent school reports, any assessments or learning-support documentation, and birth certificates. Having these ready shortens enrolment from weeks to days. 6

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Long day care and preschool places in popular areas have waiting lists, and subsidy eligibility depends on your visa. If you need childcare to start work, treat it as a long-lead item like the pet, not a first-week task. More detail on year levels, choosing between systems and how the school day feels is in Education & schools in Australia . The physical move

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Sea freight to Australia is measured in weeks at sea plus port and customs time at both ends — plan for a long gap between your things leaving and your things arriving. Air freight a small “first month” box if the budget allows. Get several quotes and ask specifically what customs, quarantine inspection and delivery are included.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Strict, and enforced. Wooden items, cane and bamboo, garden tools, footwear with soil, seeds, food and plant material all attract attention and can be treated or destroyed at your cost. Clean everything thoroughly, declare and don’t try to bring food. This is not a formality.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: Pets: start now, and get help
chunks.x: Bringing a cat or dog involves permits, vaccinations, blood tests with waiting periods, an approved route and post-arrival quarantine. It runs to many months and is expensive. It’s entirely doable and thousands of families do it, but it must be the first thing you start, and most people use a specialist agent. What’s worth shipping. Almost everyone over-ships on the first move. Furniture rarely justifies the freight; the sentimental, the irreplaceable and the good quality do. Electrical goods are worth checking against Australian plugs and voltage before you pay to move them. What to sell or store. Storing at home for a year sounds prudent and often turns into storing for five. If you’re unsure whether the move is permanent, store the small and sentimental and sell the bulky, it’s cheaper to buy a sofa twice than to store one for three years. Getting around

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Driving licences are handled by each state and territory, not nationally — so the answer to “can I drive on my licence?” depends on where you land. Your licence

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Most overseas licences can be used for a period after you arrive, and many can be converted without a full test. Timeframes and requirements vary by state, and some licences need a translation. Check your state’s transport authority early. The grace period is shorter than people assume. Buying a car

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Public transport is good in the inner cities and thin beyond them. Most families end up with a car, sometimes two. With no local credit history, finance can be harder at first, many newcomers buy modestly for cash and upgrade in year two. Distance

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: It’s bigger than the map suggests
chunks.x: Australia is vast, and a drive that looks like an afternoon can be a full day. It shapes weekends, commutes and how often you’ll see friends in another city. Worth factoring into where you choose to live. Landing well

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: What the first few weeks look like
chunks.x: Expect the early days to go on the practical foundations: activating your bank account, applying for your Tax File Number, local SIM cards, enrolling in Medicare, registering with a GP, enrolling the children, starting the rental search, and finding your way around a neighbourhood where you don’t yet know which supermarket is the good one. Two notes. First, the admin bunches : much of it can only be done once you’re here, so week one feels front-loaded. Second, the emotional shape of it surprises people . The first fortnight is often adrenaline; weeks four to eight are frequently the hardest, when the novelty thins and you’re tired and the people who know you well are asleep when you’re awake. That’s not a sign the decision was wrong. It’s the ordinary middle, and it lifts.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: What the first few weeks look like
chunks.x: Local SIM & bank activation Tax File Number Medicare & myGov Register with a GP School enrolment Licence check Ambulance cover Rental applications You won’t be doing this alone. We stay in touch through arrival and those first weeks, and once you’re settling in, Stage 08 is about building the life that lasts. Told straight

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Costs differ enormously between a capital city and a regional town, so we do not print figures. The list itself is remarkably consistent. Before you go: document certification and official copies, English testing if required, registration and assessment fees, visa application charges for the whole family, health and police checks, pet import, freight, and the flights themselves. Landing: short-term accommodation for four to six weeks, rental bond plus rent in advance, basic furniture and white goods, a car, local SIMs and internet connection, school uniforms and supplies, and any state school fees that apply to temporary visa holders. Ongoing, and easy to forget: health cover if your visa requires it, ambulance cover in some states, dental for the family, car insurance and registration, and the flights home you’ll want to take more often than you planned.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Ask your employer directly what relocation support is offered. Some roles include a contribution to flights, freight or initial accommodation, and some don’t, but it is a fair, normal question and it is far better asked before you accept than after. We’ll help you ask it well. Told straight

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: Don’t book flights before the visa is granted
chunks.x: Not the application, the grant. Changeable fares cost a little more and save a great deal of grief. 2

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: Don’t resign until both are real
chunks.x: Offer and visa. We say this on the interview page too, and we mean it just as much here. 3

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: The first-pay gap is the budget risk
chunks.x: Landing costs, bond and rent in advance all land before your first Australian pay does. Build the buffer. 5

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Licences, ambulance, school fees for temporary visa holders. Advice from a friend in another state may not apply to you. 6

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: We’re not tax or migration advisers
chunks.x: On pensions, savings transfers and tax residency, we’ll tell you what to ask; the answers need a licensed financial adviser. On visas, the Department of Home Affairs publishes the rules in full. Official sources

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Immigration & biosecurity Department of Home Affairs Biosecurity · what you can bring Importing cats & dogs Start the pet process here, months ahead. Declare everything on arrival. Honesty costs nothing.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: The set-up essentials ATO · Tax File Number & super Services Australia · Medicare Moneysmart · independent money guidance Moneysmart is the government’s own financial guidance service, no product to sell you.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.x: Schools, tenancies & licences Schooling & education overview Ahpra · your registration Ethicare · state destination guides Tenancy rights, driving licences and school fees are state matters. Your state’s own government site is the authority. Sophie’s insight The move feels overwhelming when it’s one giant cloud of tasks; it gets manageable the moment you break it into lists with dates. Bank and health cover early, short-term accommodation for landing, schools and long-term housing once you’re here. We’ve walked many families through this exact sequence. Lean on us for the order of operations, and the practical side stops being the scary part. If I could make one change to how people plan, it would be the money buffer. Almost every difficult first month I’ve seen came down to the same thing. Bond, rent in advance and setting up a home all landing before the first Australian pay did. Get that right and the rest is admin. Sophie CEO & Founder, Ethicare Resourcing Common questions

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Should I buy or rent when I arrive? Almost everyone rents first, and we’d encourage it. It lets you learn an area, settle the children and start work before committing to a suburb or a mortgage. Arrange short-term accommodation for four to six weeks, then take your time. Very few people regret renting first; plenty regret buying in month two. How far ahead should I start all this? Three to six months for the slow items, pets above all, then freight quotes, official document copies and school conversations. Six to eight weeks for banking, accommodation and confirming health cover. Flights only once the visa is granted. If you’re bringing an animal or need childcare to start work, start those first. Can I drive on my current licence? Usually for a period after you arrive, and many overseas licences convert without a full test.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: The grace period and the requirements vary by state and territory, and some licences need a certified translation. Check your destination’s transport authority early. People routinely assume they have longer than they do. Bring your licence history or an official driving record if you can get one. How much should I budget to get set up? It varies enormously. Landing in Sydney or Melbourne costs meaningfully more than a regional centre, so we won’t print a figure that would mislead you. Plan against the list instead: short-term accommodation, rental bond plus rent in advance, basic furniture, a car, connections and school costs, all before your first Australian pay arrives. That gap is the risk. And ask your employer what relocation support is offered. Can I bring my pet? Yes, and many families do, but it’s the longest and most expensive item on this page.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Permits, vaccinations, blood tests with mandatory waiting periods, an approved route and post-arrival quarantine add up to many months. Start it first, use the Department of Agriculture’s own guidance as your source, and consider a specialist agent. Do not leave it until the visa is granted. What can’t I bring into Australia? Biosecurity here is strict and enforced. Food, seeds, plant material, soil on shoes or garden tools, wooden and cane items all attract inspection and may be treated or destroyed at your cost. Clean everything, declare everything, and check the biosecurity site before you pack. Declaring something is never penalised; failing to declare it is. Will my children get a free school place? Public schooling is generally free for citizens and permanent residents.

chunks.t: Preparing to move to Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Several states charge fees for children of temporary visa holders, and the amounts differ by state, so check yours specifically before you budget. Public places are usually tied to your address, so confirm the enrolment zone before signing a lease. Bring immunisation records, recent reports and birth certificates. Should I ship my furniture? Usually less of it than you think. Sea freight is slow and costly, and most rentals are unfurnished, so you’ll be buying basics anyway. Ship the irreplaceable, the sentimental and the high quality; sell the bulky. Check electricals against Australian plugs and voltage first. And if freight will land weeks after you do, plan for that gap. What about my pension or savings back home? That needs proper financial advice rather than guesswork. Rules on transfers, tax residency and timing differ by country and can be expensive to get wrong. We can suggest the questions to ask and when to ask them; a qualified adviser in both jurisdictions should handle the specifics. Moneysmart is a good independent starting point. Next · Stage 08

chunks.x: The hopeful final step, settling into working life, building community and creating a life that lasts well beyond the first few months. Continue to Stage 08 Helpful alongside this step
