chunks.x: From the order of the admin to the questions worth asking, we’ve helped many families land well. Tell us where you’re heading and we’ll help you build a workable plan. Plan your move Register with Ethicare Ethicare Resourcing · your guide to a life and career in Australia.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: There is no national tenancy law in Australia
chunks.x: Renting is regulated by each state and territory, not by the Commonwealth, and everything else on this page follows from it. Eight jurisdictions, eight separate Residential Tenancies Acts, eight different bond authorities and eight different sets of rules on how often rent can rise, what minimum standards a property must meet, how much notice ends a tenancy and whether you can keep a pet. Someone who rented in Melbourne and then moves to Brisbane is learning a new system, not a regional variation of the same one. So the useful question is never “how does renting work in Australia”. It is “how does renting work in the state I am moving to”. The table below points you at the right authority for each one — they are the primary source, they are free, and they are more current than any guide including this one.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: There is no national tenancy law in Australia
chunks.x: What is consistent across the country is the shape of the process: you find a property listed online, you attend a short inspection, you apply afterwards in competition with other applicants, and the successful applicant pays a bond that is lodged with a government body rather than held by the agent. That shape, and the one part of it that is harder for an arriving clinician than for a local, is what follows. The primary source

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Your state’s rulebook, and who holds your bond
chunks.x: Bookmark the row for your destination before you start looking. Every one of these authorities publishes plain-English tenant guides, standard lease terms and a free dispute service. State or territory Tenancy authority & bond holder Worth knowing New South Wales NSW Fair Trading Bonds held via Rental Bonds Online Bond is lodged online and released only when both parties agree or the tribunal decides. Victoria Consumer Affairs Victoria Bonds held by the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority Victoria has an explicit set of minimum standards a rental must meet before it is let. Queensland Residential Tenancies Authority The RTA holds bonds directly The RTA runs a free dispute resolution service before anything reaches a tribunal.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Your state’s rulebook, and who holds your bond
chunks.x: Western Australia Consumer Protection WA Bonds lodged with the Bond Administrator Worth reading early if you are moving to a resources region, where the market moves fast. South Australia Consumer and Business Services CBS holds bonds Bond amounts are tiered by the weekly rent, so check which tier your property falls into. Tasmania Consumer, Building and Occupational Services Rental Deposit Authority holds bonds A small, tight rental market. Start looking earlier than you would elsewhere. Australian Capital Territory Access Canberra Bonds lodged with the ACT Revenue Office The ACT has some of the strongest tenant protections in the country. Northern Territory Consumer Affairs NT Bond arrangements set under NT tenancy law Many Top End roles come with subsidised or provided housing, ask before you search. Authorities and their web addresses occasionally change. If a link here does not resolve, search the authority name plus “renting” and tell us, and we will correct the page. The difficulty

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: The real obstacle is not money. It is that you have no history here.
chunks.x: Australian agents rank the applications they receive and put a shortlist to the owner, who chooses. A local applicant arrives with things you do not have: a rental ledger showing two years of payments on time, references from an Australian agent, and a local credit file. You are not being judged as unsuitable. You are being judged as unknown, and an owner choosing between a known quantity and an unknown one will usually take the known one unless you have given them a reason not to. The good news, and it is good: a signed healthcare employment contract is one of the strongest documents in that pile. Clinical employment reads as stable, well-paid and unlikely to evaporate. Many arriving clinicians are, on paper, a better financial prospect than the local applicant with the rental ledger. The task is to make that legible. In our experience

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: The applications that succeed are the ones that answer the questions nobody asked out loud
chunks.x: An agent looking at an overseas application has three unspoken worries: can this person pay, will they still be in the country in a year, and can I verify any of this. A pack that answers all three before being asked tends to move to the top of the pile. The single most effective thing we see is a short covering note. Three or four sentences, no more, that says what you do, who you are employed by, when you start and that you are happy to provide anything else. It costs nothing and it is startlingly rare. What to prepare

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: Have all of this ready as PDFs before you view anything. Applications are usually submitted through an online platform within hours of an inspection, and the ones that go in complete and first do best.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: Photo identification . Passport, and your driving licence if you have it. Most platforms score you on points of ID. Proof of income . Your signed employment contract or offer letter is the key document. Recent payslips from your current post help. Proof of funds . A bank statement showing you can cover bond, rent in advance and the first weeks. Rental references . From your current landlord or agent, wherever in the world that is. Translated if not in English. Personal or professional references . A colleague or manager is fine, and easy to arrange before you leave. Visa evidence . Your grant notice or application status, which tells the owner how long you can stay.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: The covering note. Three sentences: what you do, where you will be working, when you arrive. Nothing more. Offering to pay more rent in advance rather than more bond. Bond is capped by law; rent in advance usually is not, and it reassures without breaking any rule. Being contactable in Australian hours during the week you apply, even if that is inconvenient from your time zone. Applying to fewer properties, properly. Six complete applications beat twenty rushed ones. A local guarantor if you happen to have one, useful, but never necessary, and never worth delaying for. Honesty about pets. Rules vary by state and hiding an animal is the fastest way to lose a tenancy. The money, as rules

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Bond and what you pay up front
chunks.x: We publish no rent or bond amounts, because they move every quarter. The rules behind the numbers are what last.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Bond is expressed in weeks, not dollars
chunks.x: It is a multiple of the weekly rent, and it is capped by your state or territory’s tenancy law. Four weeks is the common maximum for an unfurnished home, with some jurisdictions allowing more where the property is furnished or the rent is above a threshold. Because it is a multiple, it tracks the market automatically, which is exactly why quoting an amount here would be pointless.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: You will also pay rent in advance
chunks.x: Typically two weeks, sometimes more, paid at signing on top of the bond. Together these are the largest single outlay of the whole move for most people, and the one worth having liquid and ready before you land.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: A government authority holds your bond, not the agent
chunks.x: This protection matters. In every state and territory the bond is lodged with the relevant authority from the table above, and neither you nor the owner can release it unilaterally at the end of the tenancy. You should receive written confirmation of the lodgement. If you do not, ask for it.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: Australian rent is quoted per week and most commonly paid fortnightly or monthly by direct debit. If you are used to thinking in monthly rent, multiply the weekly figure by 52 and divide by 12 rather than by four. The difference over a year is most of an extra month.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Letting fees are not charged to tenants
chunks.x: Unlike some countries, you should not be asked to pay a fee to the agent for the privilege of applying or being granted a tenancy. If you are, that is a warning sign worth checking against your state authority. For what a month looks like in a particular city, which lines are large, which are small, and which catch people out, each of our destination guides has a cost-of-living chapter written for that place, with live calculators so you can compare against the city you are leaving. A practical surprise

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: A fridge. The single most common surprise. Unfurnished means no fridge, and you will want one on day one. A washing machine , and a dryer, though in much of Australia a line in the sun does the job for most of the year. A dishwasher in older stock, though newer builds and apartments usually have one fitted. Furniture of any kind, including beds, in the ordinary sense of unfurnished.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: Built-in wardrobes in most bedrooms. Freestanding wardrobes are far less common here than in Europe. Oven, cooktop and rangehood , fitted as standard. Window coverings , blinds or curtains, which matters more than it sounds given the summer sun. Air conditioning or a reverse-cycle heat pump in most of the country, and increasingly treated as essential rather than a luxury. Ceiling fans , often in every room in the warmer states. The practical answer is to buy second-hand for the first year. Australia has a large, entirely unsnobbish second-hand market for whitegoods and furniture, and buying a used fridge and washing machine in your first week is completely normal behaviour rather than a sign of struggling. Replace them properly once you know which suburb you want to stay in. How it goes

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Open homes, and how quickly this moves
chunks.x: Most properties are shown at an open home . A fixed slot, often fifteen minutes on a Saturday morning, where anyone who has registered turns up at once. You will be one of several groups walking through the same rooms. You register online beforehand, you are asked to sign in on arrival, and the agent is there to answer questions rather than to sell you anything. You do not negotiate at the inspection and you do not make an offer there. You go away, submit an application through whichever online platform that agency uses, and wait. Decisions frequently come within a day or two in a busy market, and properties are commonly leased within a week of first being listed. Two practical consequences. First, have your documents assembled before you attend anything, because the gap between viewing and applying is hours, not days.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Open homes, and how quickly this moves
chunks.x: Second, if you are arriving into a tight market, expect to be unsuccessful a few times before you are successful. That is the normal experience of a good applicant in a competitive market, not a signal that something is wrong with your application. If you cannot attend in person, most agencies will accept an application from someone who has viewed by video or had a friend attend on their behalf. It is not ideal, and the next section explains why we would still rather you waited. Once you are in

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: Australian tenancy law is reasonably protective, and enforced through free, accessible tribunals rather than the courts. The detail varies by state. Condition report

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: You will be given a condition report to check and return within a few days of moving in. Complete it properly and take date-stamped photographs of every room, every mark and every appliance. This document is what protects your bond at the other end, and it is the single most-skipped step in the process. Repairs

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Urgent and non-urgent are different in law
chunks.x: Every jurisdiction distinguishes urgent repairs. No hot water, a burst pipe, an unsafe electrical fault, from ordinary maintenance, with faster obligations and a route to arrange the work yourself if the owner does not act. Report in writing, always, even after phoning. Rent increases

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Limited in frequency, and notice is required
chunks.x: Rent cannot be raised whenever the owner likes. Every state limits how often an increase can occur during a periodic tenancy and requires written notice, and several have tightened those rules recently. Your state authority publishes the current position. Entry

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: Inspections, repairs and viewings all require notice, in a form and period set by your state. Routine inspections happen. Commonly a couple of times a year, and are entirely normal rather than a sign of suspicion. Ending a tenancy

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.x: Fixed-term leases are the norm, typically six or twelve months, after which most roll into a periodic tenancy. Breaking a lease early is possible but usually carries a cost. Ask what it would be before you sign, particularly if your role has a probationary period. Disputes

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Free tribunals, and they are used
chunks.x: Every state has a tenancy tribunal that is accessible, low-cost and used routinely by ordinary tenants. You do not need a lawyer. Most disputes about bond are resolved this way, and going there is not an escalation to be embarrassed about. Our advice

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: We would not sign a lease before you land
chunks.x: A twelve-month lease signed from photographs commits you to a suburb you have never stood in. Photographs do not carry the sound of the road at seven in the morning, which way the living room faces in February, whether the walk to the station is pleasant or grim, or how the commute to your actual hospital feels on a wet Monday. Those are the things that decide whether you like where you live, and none of them survive a listing. What we suggest instead: book four to six weeks of temporary accommodation near where you will be working, arrive, and spend the first fortnight looking properly while you settle into the job. It feels less organised. It consistently produces better decisions, and it costs less than breaking a lease. In our experience

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Every clinician we have placed who regretted their first home had signed it remotely
chunks.x: Not one of them chose badly through carelessness. They chose from the information available, which was photographs and a map, and the information available was not enough. The families who settle fastest are usually the ones who arrived with somewhere to sleep for a month and no lease, which sounds like the riskier plan and is not. If your employer offers temporary accommodation as part of the package, take it, and if they have not mentioned it, it is a reasonable thing to ask for. Protect yourself

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Scams, and how to spot them
chunks.x: Overseas applicants are targeted because the scam depends on you being unable to visit the property. Treat any of these as a stop sign A request for bond or rent before a lease is signed. No legitimate agent asks for money to hold a property you have not been granted. An agent who will not do a live video walkthrough. If they cannot show you the property in real time, on request, there may not be a property. Payment by anything other than bank transfer to a business account , gift cards, cryptocurrency, a personal account, a money transfer service. Never. A bond that is not being lodged with the state authority. Ask which authority and request the lodgement confirmation. A real agent produces it without hesitation. Pressure and a deadline. “Three other applicants are waiting, I need the deposit today” is the core of the scam.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: Scams, and how to spot them
chunks.x: Real competition exists; real agents do not take deposits to end it. A price noticeably below the market for the suburb, especially with photographs that appear elsewhere online. Reverse-image search the listing photos. An agency you cannot verify. Licensed agents are searchable on your state authority’s register. Check the licence, not the website. If something feels wrong, send it to us before you send anyone money. We would much rather read a listing for you than help afterwards, and it takes us a few minutes. Common questions

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Can I rent with no Australian rental history? Yes, and most arriving clinicians do. Remember that agents rank applications rather than accepting or rejecting them, so the aim is to remove every reason to rank you lower: a complete pack, your employment contract, references translated where needed, proof of funds, and a three-sentence covering note. A signed healthcare contract is a strength. How much bond will I need? Bond is set as a number of weeks’ rent rather than a fixed sum, and it is capped by your state or territory’s law. Four weeks is the common maximum for an unfurnished home. You will usually pay rent in advance on top. Because it is a multiple of rent it moves with the market, so check it against the actual property rather than any published figure. Who holds my bond? A government authority in every state and territory, never the agent or the owner.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Neither party can release it alone at the end of the tenancy. If an agent asks to hold it themselves, or wants it before a lease is signed, stop and check with the authority in the table above. Does unfurnished mean completely empty? Not quite, but it usually means no fridge and no washing machine, which is the part that surprises people. You should expect built-in wardrobes, an oven and cooktop, window coverings and very often air conditioning. Buy whitegoods second-hand for the first year; it is completely normal here. Should I sign a lease before I arrive? We would advise against it. Book four to six weeks of temporary accommodation, arrive, view in person and sign then. Every clinician we have placed who regretted their first home had signed it remotely, not through carelessness, but because photographs cannot tell you about the road noise or the commute.

chunks.t: Renting in Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Can I keep a pet? It depends on the state, and the rules have been changing in tenants’ favour in several of them. Some jurisdictions now require an owner to have a valid reason to refuse. Never hide an animal. Declare it in the application, because a disclosed pet occasionally costs you a property while an undisclosed one can cost you the tenancy. Getting the animal into the country is a separate matter, covered in moving with pets . Is it better to buy instead? Not in your first year, in our view, whatever the numbers say. Renting for twelve months teaches you which suburb you want, and that knowledge is worth more than a year of capital growth. There may also be foreign-investment approval requirements and additional stamp duty depending on your visa status, worth proper advice rather than a paragraph here. Read a little deeper

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.h: Nobody earns the minimum, but everyone should know it
chunks.x: Australia answers what you will earn in two parts, and most salary guides only show you one. The first part is public and precise. A national modern award sets a legal minimum for your profession, the same in every state, published by the Fair Work Ombudsman and updated each July. Anyone can read it. The second part is where real offers live: state enterprise agreements and private-market rates that sit above that floor , often well above it. So the award is not a forecast of your salary. It is the number below which an offer cannot legally go, which makes it the most useful reference point you have when you are new to a country and cannot yet tell a good offer from a poor one. Read it as a floor, not a target. If an offer is anywhere near the award minimum for your level, that tells you something. Knowing the floor is what lets you ask the right question about everything above it. How the system is built

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.h: The two layers of Australian pay
chunks.x: Australia has no single national pay scale. It has a national safety net with state and private layers on top, and which one applies depends on who employs you. Layer one · the floor

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: A single federal instrument per profession group, setting minimum rates, penalties, allowances and conditions. It applies everywhere in Australia and is reviewed every July by the Fair Work Commission. For most allied health and medical-imaging roles this is the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020. Layer two · the public system

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Public hospitals and health services are covered by enterprise agreements negotiated in each state and territory, usually with the relevant union. These sit above the award and are where most public-sector clinicians are paid. Because they are negotiated separately, the same job pays differently in different states. Layer three · the private market

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Australia has one of the world’s largest private healthcare and imaging markets. Private employers must meet the award floor but are otherwise free to build their own packages, and for in-demand skills those packages compete hard. Why this matters to you It means "what does a radiographer earn in Australia" has no single answer, and anyone who gives you one figure is guessing. The answerable questions are: what is the floor for my level, which agreement or contract would cover this specific role, and what does that role pay. We answer those three for every role we discuss. The published minimum

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.h: The national floor, in real numbers
chunks.x: Rates change every July, check the current Fair Work pay guide or the Pay and Conditions Tool before relying on any figure. Read this the right way These are minimums for the private sector, at the first pay point, before anything is added. A public-hospital offer under a state enterprise agreement will normally sit above them, and a private offer for a skill in short supply can sit well above them. We publish the floor because it is verifiable and stable enough to be useful. We do not publish "typical" or "average" salaries, because the version of that number depends on your state, your employer, your pay point and your roster, and a made-up average helps nobody make a decision this big. Landing on the right rung

chunks.x: Complexity of work, supervision of others and specialist scope move you up levels rather than pay points. Senior, lead and advanced-practice roles sit higher on the scale. D

chunks.x: You typically move up a pay point each year of service, so pay grows steadily without renegotiating. Pay points should be reviewed annually. It is worth checking yours has moved.

chunks.x: Four weeks of paid annual leave is the national minimum, plus personal and carer’s leave, public holidays and long service leave. Shift workers are often entitled to a fifth week.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Covers allied health professionals in the private sector: radiographers, sonographers, radiation therapists, nuclear medicine technologists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, dietitians, podiatrists, audiologists and medical scientists. Health professional Levels 1–4, each with pay points. This is the award the rates above come from. Doctors

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Medical practitioners were removed from MA000027 coverage by Fair Work Commission determination from 1 July 2021. Consultant and specialist pay is set by state enterprise agreements, private practice arrangements or individual contracts, nowhere near an award minimum, and always confirmed role by role. And if you are heading for a public hospital Then the award is only your safety net. Your actual pay, hours, leave and progression come from the enterprise agreement covering that state or territory’s public health service. Those agreements are public documents, and we will tell you which one applies and what it says for your classification before you consider a role. Coverage is worth confirming rather than assuming, Fair Work’s Pay and Conditions Tool will tell you which instrument applies to a given role. What lands in your account

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Australian salaries are quoted before tax, and often separately from superannuation, so check which you are being shown. Income tax is deducted from each pay by your employer under PAYG withholding . You will need a tax file number soon after arriving. Giving it to your employer promptly means you are taxed at the correct rate rather than the top one. There is also a Medicare levy , a percentage of taxable income that helps fund the public health system, and higher earners without private hospital cover can pay an additional surcharge. On top of your salary, your employer pays superannuation at 12% of ordinary earnings into a retirement fund. It is not deducted from your pay and it is not optional. When you compare an Australian offer with what you earn now, count it, it is real money, even though you cannot spend it yet.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Watch for the difference between a salary quoted as base and one quoted as "package including super": the same role can look several thousand dollars apart depending on which convention the advert used. There is no separate National Insurance-style contribution as in the UK, and GST is already included in displayed prices. Our living & thriving guide walks through setting up the everyday money side, bank account, tax file number and choosing a super fund, step by step. A note on advice Tax rates, thresholds and Medicare levy rules depend on your circumstances and visa, and they change. Always confirm the current position with the Australian Taxation Office or a registered tax agent. Ethicare are recruitment specialists, not financial advisers, but we are glad to introduce you to advisers we trust. Earning, against living

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Housing is the cost that surprises newcomers most, and it varies enormously. A regional city can stretch the same salary far further than a capital. Because pay is set state by state rather than nationally, both halves of the equation move when you move.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Workforce shortages are sharpest outside the big cities, so regional and remote roles frequently carry incentives, accommodation support or higher rates, alongside lower living costs and, for many, a better daily life.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.x: Shorter commutes, the outdoors on your doorstep and a cultural respect for time off mean many clinicians feel better off here even where the headline figure is comparable to home. Our destination guides help you weigh this up properly.

chunks.h: Knowing your exact rate, before you decide
chunks.x: For any role we discuss, we will tell you which instrument sets the pay , award, enterprise agreement or contract, confirm the current rate against that document , tell you the level and pay point you would be placed on and why, and walk through the full package : base, penalties, shift loadings, superannuation and leave. Where pay is individually negotiated, we will say so plainly and tell you what the market is doing. A move this big deserves clear numbers, straight answers and the time to think them over. Sophie’s insight Money is rarely the first reason people move, but it has to add up, and it is the thing clinicians feel most awkward asking about. I would rather you ask us everything. Australia is harder to read than New Zealand, because there is no single national scale to point at, and I think that is exactly why so many salary guides end up quoting one number and hoping.

chunks.h: Knowing your exact rate, before you decide
chunks.x: We show you the floor, tell you which agreement governs the role in front of you, and then talk about what sits above it. You will know your real take-home, against the cost of living where you are headed, long before you have to decide anything. Sophie CEO & Founder, Ethicare Resourcing Common questions

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about pay
chunks.x: Is the award rate what I’ll be paid? Almost certainly not, it is the legal minimum, not the going rate. Public-hospital pay comes from the enterprise agreement for that state or territory and normally sits above the award. Private employers must meet the award floor but compete above it, sometimes well above it for skills in short supply. Use the award to sanity-check an offer, not to predict one. Why does the same job pay differently in different states? Because public-sector pay is negotiated state by state rather than nationally. Each state and territory health service has its own enterprise agreement with its own scales, progression and allowances. It is one of the biggest differences from New Zealand or the NHS, and it means the state you choose is a financial decision as well as a lifestyle one. Will my overseas experience count towards my pay point? Generally yes.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about pay
chunks.x: Relevant experience earned abroad normally counts towards your pay point within a classification level. The key is documenting it clearly and completely, because being placed at too low a pay point is one of the most common underpayments under this award, and once it is set, it is easy to leave uncorrected for years. We will help you present your history so nothing is overlooked. Can I negotiate my salary in Australia? It depends which layer you are in. In the public system, base pay follows the enterprise agreement’s published scale, so the negotiation that matters is about your classification and pay point, not the rate itself. In the private sector there is real room to negotiate, on base, and often on hours, on-call arrangements, professional development and relocation support.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about pay
chunks.x: What is superannuation, and does it really count as pay? Superannuation is Australia’s compulsory retirement savings system. Your employer must pay 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund on top of your salary, it is not deducted from what you earn. It is yours, though you cannot access it until retirement, and there are specific rules about what happens to it if you later leave Australia permanently. When comparing offers, check whether a figure is base salary or a package including super. Do you publish typical or average salaries? No, we publish the verifiable floor and then confirm the figure per role. An "average" for a profession across eight states, public and private, metro and regional, is a number with no one behind it. It cannot tell you whether an offer in front of you is fair, which is the only thing you need to know.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in Australian healthcare
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about pay
chunks.x: How often do these figures change? Award minimums are reviewed every year by the Fair Work Commission and take effect from the first full pay period on or after 1 July. The rates on this page are the current 2026–27 figures, which rose 4.75% from 1 July 2026. Enterprise agreements run on their own multi-year cycles, so those change on different dates again, another reason we confirm against the live document rather than relying on a page. Keep exploring

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: Australia has an excellent public system. It isn’t automatically free.
chunks.x: Public education in Australia is not free for every family living there on a temporary visa. The rules vary between states and territories, and can also depend on the visa you hold. That makes this particularly relevant for healthcare professionals relocating on employer-sponsored temporary visas , which is how a great many internationally trained clinicians arrive. If you are relocating with two or three school-aged children, don’t compare the salaries offered in Queensland, Western Australia, Victoria or New South Wales. Check the schooling position attached to your visa in that state as well. It can change the economics of an offer substantially. The mechanism

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: Why your visa decides this, not the school
chunks.x: Each state and territory sets its own position on what dependants of temporary visa holders pay, so the same family can face a different answer in two states.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: Government schooling is free or low-cost, on the same basis as any local family. The everyday costs below still apply, but there is no tuition contribution.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: Several states and territories charge an annual tuition contribution for dependants, and several don’t. Exemptions, waivers, income tests and regional concessions all exist, and all vary.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: Eligibility is usually tied to the exact visa subclass, and sometimes to your occupation being on a skills list. Two clinicians on different subclasses can be treated differently in the same state. This is why we won’t give you a figure on this page. The number depends on your state, your subclass, your occupation and sometimes your household income, and the rules change. We’ll check the current position for your actual circumstances before you weigh an offer. Where to look

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: Each state and territory publishes its own rules. Check the position for your subclass directly, in the year you’re moving.

chunks.x: NSW Department of Education sets the temporary-resident tuition fee and its exemptions. Notably, families on eligible temporary skilled visas moving to regional NSW can currently access public schooling without the temporary-resident tuition fee, so metropolitan and regional positions differ.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: WA’s Department of Education applies a family tuition fee for holders of certain temporary skilled visas, including subclass 482, rather than a separate full fee for every child, which changes the arithmetic considerably for larger families.

chunks.x: The Victorian Department of Education sets the position for international and temporary-resident students, including which visa subclasses enrol as local students. Confirm your subclass against their current schedule.

chunks.x: Queensland’s Department of Education publishes the rules for dependants of temporary visa holders, including any waiver or application process that applies to skilled visa families.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: The South Australian Department for Education sets fees for temporary residents, with eligibility criteria that can include income testing and sibling arrangements. Check both.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: Tasmania’s Department for Education, Children and Young People publishes the position for temporary visa holders, including any levy that applies in place of tuition.

chunks.x: Two states worth flagging for anyone weighing offers: New South Wales treats regional and metropolitan moves differently , and Western Australia charges per family rather than per child for certain skilled subclasses. If you have several children, those two differences alone can be worth more than a pay difference between states. Either way

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: Public school doesn’t mean no school costs
chunks.x: Even where public education is tuition-free, budget for everyday school expenses. They arrive together in your first term. Uniforms and shoes Books and stationery Laptops or other devices School camps and excursions Sports and extracurricular activities Transport Before- and after-school care Voluntary contributions or school-specific charges None of these is large on its own. All of them landing in the same month, alongside a rental bond and furnishing a house, is a different matter, our relocation cost guide puts them in the context of everything else you’ll be paying for at once. The other sectors

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: Australia has a substantial Catholic and independent school sector, and fees vary enormously across it — more than the phrase “private school” suggests to most families arriving.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: Often considerably less expensive than families expect when they hear “private school”. Fees typically rise gradually through the year levels, and for many families this is an affordable middle path.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: An enormous range. Australia’s most prestigious independent schools charge substantial annual fees; many others sit far below that. Facilities, programs and philosophy all feed into it.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.x: Research the specific schools and their current fees in the particular area you’re considering, before accepting a role. Many have waiting lists, so enquire early rather than after you arrive. The practical part

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: Check before choosing where to live
chunks.x: Many Australian government schools have local enrolment areas or catchments, so schools influence your choice of accommodation more than most families expect. A property that looks perfect online may not place your child within the enrolment area of the school you have chosen. And by the time you’ve signed a twelve-month tenancy, that is an expensive thing to discover. Our advice is simple: look at the job, the school and the home together. Don’t secure accommodation first and start thinking about schools afterwards. And if you’re moving on a temporary visa, check the current state education rules applying to your subclass before you calculate your relocation budget at all. Comparing offers

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: One of the hidden differences between two states
chunks.x: School fees don’t appear in an employment contract but can change which offer is better for a family. Two roles with identical salaries in two different states are not equivalent offers if one state charges tuition for your children and the other doesn’t, or if one charges per child and the other per family. For a clinician moving with three school-aged children, that difference can outweigh a meaningful gap in pay. So when you’re weighing states, put the schooling position beside the salary. Our money guide works through the other costs that shift the answer the same way, and the education guide covers how Australian schooling is structured, childcare and the tertiary pathways. Common questions

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: The questions parents ask us about fees
chunks.x: We’re on a 482 visa. Will we pay for a government school? It depends entirely on the state or territory. Some charge dependants of temporary visa holders an annual tuition contribution; others don’t; and several operate exemptions, waivers, income tests or regional concessions. Check the current position with the relevant state department for your exact subclass before you plan around it. How reliable are the figures above? They are indicative, rounded down, and reviewed each year — enough to plan a relocation budget against, not a quote. The fees themselves change annually, the exemption criteria change, and eligibility often turns on your exact visa subclass and occupation, so the figure that applies to your family can be lower than the band or nothing at all. Confirm the current position with the department that sets it, and we will work through your own position with you.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: The questions parents ask us about fees
chunks.x: Does moving regionally make a difference? In some states, considerably. New South Wales currently distinguishes regional from metropolitan moves for eligible temporary skilled visa families. It’s one of several reasons regional roles can be worth more to a family than the headline salary suggests. Is it cheaper if we have several children? It can be, depending on the state. Western Australia currently applies a family tuition fee for certain temporary skilled subclasses, including 482, rather than a full fee per child. Some other states operate sibling arrangements. If you have three children, this is worth checking state by state before you shortlist locations. Will becoming a permanent resident change it? Generally yes, permanent residents and citizens access government schooling on the same basis as local families.

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: The questions parents ask us about fees
chunks.x: If you’re on a pathway to permanent residence, the timing of that can matter to your school costs, which is worth factoring in early. What about New Zealand, is it the same? No, the systems and rules are different, and New Zealand’s enrolment zones work differently again. Our New Zealand education guide covers the position there, and it’s worth comparing both if you’re still deciding between the two countries. Free, any time

chunks.t: Will I pay school fees in Australia?
chunks.h: Tell us the ages, and we’ll check the position
chunks.x: Once you’re applying for a role through us, give us your likely visa subclass, the states you’re considering and your children’s ages, and we’ll help you understand what schooling would cost in each, before it becomes a factor you discover after accepting a role. Ask Ethicare about school fees Read the education guide Ethicare Resourcing · your guide to a life and career in Australia.

chunks.x: Home Affairs, the skilled occupation lists and the forms you’ll need, gathered in one place. Open the directory I want someone to sequence it with me

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: We explain the routes and keep your file moving. The decisions stay with Home Affairs, but you won’t be guessing at the order. Ask us about your visa First, the big picture

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: Two main ways in, and how they meet registration
chunks.x: Reviewed July 2026 · checked against the Department of Home Affairs’ current published guidance. Immigration rules change, always confirm at the source Two routes cover most healthcare professionals: employer-sponsored or skilled migration. Registration and visa are separate workstreams, sequenced so neither holds the other up. A note up front: immigration is regulated, and the rules change. Nothing here is migration advice, it’s a plain-English map so you know the shape of it. For your actual application, the Department of Home Affairs publishes the current detail in full, and we point you to it. How it fits together

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Registration, the role and the visa run alongside each other. Start each early enough that none becomes the thing everyone is waiting on. Thread one

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Your right to practise comes from the national board for your profession, or from the accrediting body where your profession isn’t board-registered. It’s the longest lead time of the three, so it starts first. Thread two

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: An offer from an employer willing to sponsor is what unlocks the most direct visa routes. It also anchors the timing of everything else, including when you can fly. Thread three

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Lodged once the role and your evidence are in place. Health examinations and police certificates sit inside this thread and are the two things people most often start too late. The most common route for us

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: An Australian employer sponsors you to fill a role they can’t fill locally. For most candidates we support, this is the most direct path, and on it, a separate migration skills assessment generally isn’t required just to register. Skills in Demand (482)

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: A temporary skilled visa sponsored by your employer for an eligible occupation. It lets you live and work here while you settle, often with a pathway to permanent residence over time. Employer Nomination (186)

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: An employer-nominated permanent route for eligible roles, sometimes available from the outset, sometimes after a period on a working visa. Your adviser will confirm what fits. The appeal

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: You arrive with a job, an employer invested in your move, and often relocation support, which makes the practical side of settling considerably smoother. The points-based route

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Skilled migration lets you apply based on your occupation, age, English, qualifications and experience, without needing a specific employer first. It’s where the migration skills assessment matters most.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Subclasses such as 189 (independent), 190 (state-nominated) and 491 (regional) are scored on a points test. State and regional nomination can add points and open doors.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: These visas require a skills assessment by the gazetted authority for your profession: ASMIRT for radiographers and radiation therapists, ANZSNM for nuclear medicine, the ASMIRT ultrasound certificate for sonographers.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Many healthcare roles are outside the big cities, and regional visas and incentives can make a regional move both easier and rewarding, something worth exploring openly. A rough sort

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: You want a role confirmed before you commit to moving Your profession is one hospitals and providers are actively short of You’d rather arrive with an employer invested in your relocation You want the shortest sensible route from decision to arrival You’re moving with a partner and children and want certainty first

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: You want permanent residence from the outset, before choosing an employer You’re happy to complete a migration skills assessment for your occupation You score well on the points test on age, English and experience You’re open to a state-nominated or regional route, and the incentives that come with it Your timeline is longer and you’d rather trade speed for flexibility Both can be true. Plenty of people arrive on an employer-sponsored visa and move toward permanent residence later, either through their employer or in their own right. Starting on one route rarely closes the other. The shape of it

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: First, a clear look at your qualifications, experience and English against what your profession requires. This is Stage 03, and it saves months of wasted effort. 2

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: The longest thread begins. Document gathering, verification and assessment run in the background while the rest of your move takes shape. 3

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Interviews, offer, and confirmation that the employer will sponsor. This is the point where an abstract plan becomes a real date on a calendar. 4

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: On a sponsored route your employer’s nomination is generally lodged alongside or just ahead of your visa application. On a skilled route you submit an expression of interest and wait to be invited. 5

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Health examinations for everyone on the application, plus police certificates from each country you’ve lived in. Start these the moment you’re told to; overseas certificates can be slow. 6

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Once granted, flights, shipping, schools and housing come into focus. That’s where Preparing to move picks up, and by then the hardest part is behind you. You’re not moving alone

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: For most work and skilled visas you can include your partner and dependent children on the same application, and partners are usually able to work. The detail (who counts as a dependant, evidence of your relationship, schooling and health checks) depends on the visa and your circumstances. It’s all routine, but it rewards getting organised early: gathering documents, booking the health examinations, and being clear about everyone you’re bringing. We’ll make sure nothing important is left to the last minute, and Home Affairs confirms the specifics.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Partners included on most work and skilled visas hold work rights, often unrestricted. For a lot of couples that’s the detail that makes the move viable: two careers, not one on hold.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: Your children can go to school
chunks.x: Dependent children study here while you work. What you pay depends on your visa and the state or territory you land in, so it’s worth checking before you choose a suburb.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Access to Medicare depends on your visa, and reciprocal health care agreements cover people from a number of countries in the meantime. Most families also hold private cover, and some visas require it. The longer view

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: After a period in the role
chunks.x: Employer-nominated permanent routes are generally open to people who’ve held an eligible role for a qualifying period, and sometimes from the outset. Your employer and your adviser confirm what applies. In your own right

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: If you meet the points test you can pursue permanent residence independently of any employer, including through state nomination. Some people arrive sponsored and go this way later. Further out

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Citizenship follows a period of lawful residence, part of it as a permanent resident. It’s years away rather than months, but it’s the reason many families make the move at all. Worth saying plainly: permanence is not automatic, and eligibility rules change over time. If putting down roots is the point of the move for you, say so early. It changes which route we’d recommend exploring, and which questions your adviser should be asked first. Worth knowing

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Visa subclasses, occupation lists, income thresholds and nomination criteria are all reviewed. Whatever you read, including this page, confirm the current position with the Department of Home Affairs. 2

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: Health and police checks take time
chunks.x: Medicals for every person on the application, and police certificates from every country you’ve lived in for a meaningful period. Overseas certificates are the single most common cause of delay, and some countries need your fingerprints before they will issue one, so check each country’s process early. 3

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Application charges, medicals, certificates, skills assessments and registration fees add up across a family, and some are payable per person. They’re manageable when you budget for them and unpleasant when you don’t. 4

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: English evidence has a shelf life
chunks.x: Test results expire, and different bodies accept different tests and scores. Check what your registration and your visa each require before you book, rather than sitting the wrong test twice. 5

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Approval for one is not approval for the other. Both have to land, and they’re assessed by different organisations against different criteria. 6

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: We coordinate, we chase, we keep the threads aligned. Visa agents can be expensive and are not always necessary: if you have the time to work through the process yourself, many people do, and it can save a good deal of money. 7

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: Age limits sit on the permanent step
chunks.x: The Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) has no age limit. The Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186) , the usual permanent step after it, generally requires you to be under 45 when you apply, with some exemptions. The points-tested skilled visas have an age limit too. If you are in your forties, check the permanent visa’s age rules before you start the work visa. Practical

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: You can start this before you’ve chosen a visa, an employer or even a state. Certified copies get used more than once.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Current passports for everyone moving, with plenty of validity left Degree certificates and academic transcripts A full employment history with dates, and references you can reach Evidence of registration, past and present, in every country you’ve practised English test results, if your route requires them Police certificates from each country you’ve lived in

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.x: Marriage or relationship evidence, and children’s birth certificates A migration skills assessment from the authority for your occupation Continuing professional development records Certified translations of anything not in English A change-of-name document, if your paperwork doesn’t all match Sophie’s insight Visas are the part people fear most. Once you have a role and your registration is moving, the visa is mostly paperwork, timelines and patience. The key is the order: job, registration and visa need to line up. Ethicare is not an immigration adviser, so check your visa with the Department of Home Affairs. Sophie CEO & Founder, Ethicare Resourcing Common questions

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Which visa is right for me? It depends on your profession, whether you have an employer, your age and your plans. Most candidates we support come on an employer-sponsored visa; others suit skilled migration. We’ll talk through which fits, and Home Affairs sets out each route in full. Do I need the skills assessment and registration? Not always both. Registration is what lets you practise and is generally the priority. A migration skills assessment is needed for certain skilled visas, but on an employer-sponsored route it often isn’t required just to register. We’ll confirm what your pathway needs. Can my partner work? In most cases, yes. Partners on employer-sponsored and skilled visas are usually able to work, frequently with full rights. The specifics depend on the visa, which your adviser confirms.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: How long does a visa take? It varies by visa type, your documentation and current processing times. The biggest things within your control are starting early and submitting complete, well-evidenced applications, for the visa, the skills assessment and your registration alike. Do I need a job offer before I can apply? For employer-sponsored routes, yes, that’s the point of them. For points-tested skilled visas, no, you can apply in your own right. Which is why the first useful conversation is about what you want, not which form to fill in. Will I have to move somewhere regional? Not necessarily, though it’s worth keeping an open mind. A lot of healthcare roles sit outside the largest cities, regional routes can carry extra points and incentives, and plenty of people who arrived intending to move on ended up staying. We’ll be straight with you about what the trade-offs feel like day to day.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Can I bring our pets? Usually, yes, and it’s a proper process: vaccinations, testing, an import permit and quarantine on arrival, all with lead times measured in months. Start it as soon as your move looks real. Preparing to move covers the practical side. What if my application is refused? It’s uncommon on well-prepared applications, which is precisely why preparation matters. Where it happens there are usually options, review rights or a different route, and the decision letter explains them. We’ll help you work out what it means for your move. Do you charge candidates for any of this? No. Our support for you is free, employers pay us to find the right people. Third parties charge their own fees, registration bodies and assessment authorities, and we’ll always tell you which costs are coming before they arrive.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas for Australia
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Is there an age limit? Not for the work visa: the Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) has no age limit. The permanent step most people take after it, the Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186), generally requires you to be under 45 when you apply, with some exemptions. If you are in your forties, check the age rules on the Home Affairs subclass 186 page before you start. Next · Stage 07 continues

chunks.x: With the visa underway, attention turns to the practical move: flights, banking, Medicare, housing, schools and what those first few weeks look like. Continue to Preparing to move Helpful alongside this step

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: New Zealand Australia The money guide Where will your salary go further? Higher pay is not the same as more money Australia generally pays healthcare professionals more than New Zealand. That sounds as though it should make the financial decision straightforward. It doesn’t. Work through it → Ask Ethicare 12 sections Updated August 2026 Free The wrong question

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: A higher salary is not the same as more money
chunks.x: So if you’re weighing Australia against New Zealand, the useful question isn’t where will I earn more? It’s: where will my salary give me the life I want? This guide works through the things that decide that. Retirement contributions, housing, commuting, children, everyday costs, your profession, your career stage and the first-year costs nobody budgets for. Section 01 · The headline

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: Australia generally wins on headline salary
chunks.x: Across many healthcare professions, Australian salaries tend to be higher than the equivalent New Zealand salaries. The gap can become particularly significant for some senior medical specialists, GPs and clinicians working within Australia’s private sector. Australia

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: There are substantial opportunities across diagnostic imaging and allied health too, particularly where employers are struggling to recruit experienced clinicians. But Australia is an enormous and varied employment market. A salary in Sydney shouldn’t be treated as equivalent to the same salary in Adelaide, Hobart, Bunbury or a regional Queensland city. New Zealand

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: For many professions the equivalent New Zealand salary will be lower. That doesn’t automatically make it a worse financial move. The market is smaller, and many roles, particularly in the public system, sit within established salary scales or collective agreements. That makes remuneration relatively transparent, often with additional payments for overtime, weekends, nights or on-call. The point The number on the offer letter is only the beginning of the comparison. Everything below is the rest of it. Section 02 · Retirement contributions

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Both countries add employer-funded retirement savings on top of your pay. In Australia, how that’s worded in an offer can change the figure by thousands. Australia

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Superannuation is Australia’s retirement savings system, and employers generally make compulsory contributions for eligible employees. That makes the wording of an offer important: A$130,000 + super is not the same offer as… A$130,000 including super. When comparing two Australian jobs, or an Australian job against a New Zealand one. Establish exactly what the quoted figure represents before you do any arithmetic. New Zealand

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: KiwiSaver is New Zealand’s workplace retirement savings scheme. From 1 April 2026 , the default employee and matching employer contribution rate rose from 3% to 3.5% , subject to eligibility and your specific employment arrangement. The default rate is scheduled to rise again to 4% from 1 April 2028. Members who need to can apply to Inland Revenue for a temporary reduction back to 3%. Eligibility matters for new arrivals. Joining generally requires the right to live in New Zealand indefinitely, so on a temporary work visa you may not be able to join yet. Look wider than the base Also look for relocation assistance, professional registration costs, CPD funding, salary packaging, overtime and on-call payments. A good package is much more than its base salary, and two offers with the same headline can be thousands apart once these are counted. Section 03 · Housing

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: Housing can completely change the calculation
chunks.x: For most relocating healthcare professionals, housing is the largest household expense, and where broad country comparisons become unreliable. Sydney is not Australia. Auckland is not New Zealand. Australia

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: The difference can vanish into rent
chunks.x: A clinician earning considerably more in a major Australian city may spend much of that difference on housing. Conversely, a role in a regional centre can pair a strong salary with more affordable housing than some capital-city markets. New Zealand

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Auckland’s housing costs can be challenging, whereas a role in Palmerston North, Christchurch or another regional centre may produce a completely different household budget on a similar salary. How to compare properly Compare job plus location , not Australia plus New Zealand. The country is far too blunt a unit for a decision this specific. Section 04 · The commute

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Will you need two cars? Will you pay for parking? Could you live ten minutes from the hospital or clinic? Or are you likely to spend an hour each way? A shorter commute has financial value. It also has something harder to quantify: time . Saving an hour every working day means hundreds of additional hours with your family over a year. For a great many clinicians, that turns out to be the single biggest improvement after relocating, bigger than the salary. Section 05 · Family

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Families need to weigh housing size, school location, childcare, after-school care, transport and activities, and schooling often decides where you live rather than the other way round. Australia

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Arrangements differ between states and between school systems, so the relationship between where you live and where your children can enrol needs checking locally rather than nationally. New Zealand

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: School enrolment zones can make the link between your address and your children’s schooling particularly direct, worth knowing before you sign a tenancy. Look at the household, not the house The cheapest house isn’t necessarily the cheapest solution, if it creates additional transport, childcare or commuting costs. Add it up across the whole household. Section 06 · Everyday costs

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Everyday costs matter too, and the intuitions people arrive with about each country tend to be wrong in opposite directions. Misconception one

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: “Higher Australian salary means higher Australian costs”
chunks.x: It isn’t that simple. Australia’s cost of living varies substantially by location, and while housing remains an important contributor to household cost pressures, those pressures are not identical across cities or household types. A regional healthcare position can therefore be attractive: a strong salary, a shorter commute and potentially lower housing costs than one of the most expensive metropolitan markets. “Regional” doesn’t automatically mean remote. Misconception two

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Smaller cities and a relaxed lifestyle create an impression that living there must be inexpensive. That isn’t necessarily so. Housing in some areas is expensive, groceries can be costly and imported goods may cost more than new arrivals expect. Choose New Zealand because the overall proposition works for you, not because you assume everything will be cheaper. On groceries specifically: food can feel expensive in both countries, particularly at first, when you instinctively convert every price back into pounds. Over time most people stop shopping as though they’re still in Britain, different supermarkets, different brands, seasonal buying, local markets and suppliers. But food belongs in your initial relocation budget all the same. Section 07 · Your profession

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: There isn’t one answer for “healthcare professionals”
chunks.x: The pay structures themselves differ, so the comparison changes completely depending on what you do. An experienced radiologist considering Australian private practice is making a very different calculation from a radiation therapist comparing two public-sector positions. A GP considering an Australian percentage-of-billings arrangement cannot sensibly compare the headline number with a salaried New Zealand GP position. A sonographer in an area of significant workforce shortage may be able to command a different package again. Radiographers, psychologists, physiotherapists, anaesthetic technicians and others all have their own salary structures and employment markets. Which is why profession-specific advice beats country-level advice every time. Our profession guides go through each one, and the GP , radiologist and sonographer pages each carry a compared section. Section 08 · Career stage

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: An opportunity might offer experience in a new modality, greater autonomy, leadership responsibility or access to a specialist area that strengthens your career over the next decade. That can be worth more than the difference in salary. Later in your career

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: The priority may reverse: willingly exchanging some earning potential for fewer sessions, predictable hours, a shorter commute or more time with your family. Money matters. But so does what you’re being paid to do. Section 09 · The first year

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: Relocation assistance, and why year one isn’t year five
chunks.x: Two things that reshape the financial picture and rarely appear in a salary comparison. Relocation support

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: Depending on the employer and profession, a package may contribute towards flights, temporary accommodation, shipping, registration, immigration expenses or other relocation costs. For a family moving halfway around the world, that can be thousands of dollars. An employer offering a slightly lower salary but meaningful relocation assistance may well be the better financial proposition in your first year. Establish exactly what is included. Ask whether there are repayment conditions. Ask what happens if you leave the role earlier than expected. Year one

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.x: You may initially pay for temporary accommodation, rental bonds, furniture, a car, registration, immigration costs and flights. You may also arrive before your partner starts working. Your first six months can therefore feel considerably tighter than your eventual lifestyle suggests, and that doesn’t tell you whether the move was financially worthwhile. Once you’re established, household finances can look very different. Section 10 · The verdict

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: So, where does your salary go further?
chunks.x: Australia often comes out ahead if… Maximising earning potential is your priority You’re in a profession or sector where private earnings are substantially higher You’re open to regional as well as metropolitan roles You’d rather have the higher number and manage the costs New Zealand can still win if… A manageable commute and a smaller city appeal Predictable, transparent pay matters more than the ceiling You want to reduce the costs, and stresses, of a major city What you moved for isn’t primarily the money The summary A high income in an expensive metropolitan area can disappear surprisingly quickly. For some people Australia will leave substantially more money in the bank. For others, New Zealand will provide more of what they moved for. Before you accept anything

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: Compare the life, not just the salary
chunks.x: When you’re weighing an offer, write down more than the salary: expected take-home pay, retirement contributions, housing, transport, childcare, working hours, annual leave, relocation assistance and likely household income. Then write down something else entirely. What does an ordinary Tuesday look like? What time will you leave home? How long will it take to get to work? What time will you finish? How far away is your child’s school? Can you afford the kind of home you want? And what will you be able to do when the working day is finished? Those questions won’t appear on an employment contract. They may tell you far more about whether Australia or New Zealand offers the better deal. Sophie’s insight People are often slightly embarrassed to ask about money, as though wanting to be paid properly sits awkwardly beside wanting to do good work. It doesn’t. Earning more is important.

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: Compare the life, not just the salary
chunks.x: What I’d rather you didn’t do is make a decision this big from one number on one offer letter, because I’ve watched people arrive on a higher salary and feel poorer, and I’ve watched people take less and feel like they’d been handed their life back. Tell me what your household needs, and we’ll work through the whole picture together. The role, the package, the location and the cost of the life around it. Sophie Founder, Ethicare Resourcing Common questions

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: The money questions we’re asked most
chunks.x: Does Australia always pay more? Generally yes on the headline figure, and sometimes substantially, particularly for senior medical specialists, GPs and clinicians in the private sector. But Australia is many employment markets rather than one, and a Sydney salary isn’t an Adelaide, Hobart or regional Queensland salary. What you keep depends far more on where you live than on which country you choose. What does “plus super” mean? That the employer’s compulsory retirement contribution sits on top of the quoted salary rather than inside it. “$130,000 + super” and “$130,000 including super” are materially different offers. Always establish which convention an advert or offer is using before comparing it with anything else. How much does KiwiSaver add? The default employee and matching employer rate rose to 3.5% from 1 April 2026, and is scheduled to reach 4% from 1 April 2028.

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: The money questions we’re asked most
chunks.x: Eligibility matters for new arrivals: joining generally requires the right to live in New Zealand indefinitely, so on a temporary work visa you may not be able to join immediately. Confirm your position with a provider or Inland Revenue. Should I take a lower salary with relocation support? Often it’s the better first-year proposition. Flights, shipping, temporary accommodation, registration and immigration costs add up fast for a family. Just establish what’s included, whether there are repayment conditions, and what happens if you leave sooner than planned. Why won’t you just tell me which country pays more for my role? Because the answer changes with your profession, your seniority, public or private, the state or region, and your household. We work from the figures for your role, not an average. Tell us your profession and where you’re considering, and we’ll do it properly.

chunks.t: Australia vs NZ salaries compared
chunks.h: The money questions we’re asked most
chunks.x: I’m not from the UK, does this still apply to me? Yes. We support clinicians trained across the UK, Ireland, South Africa, the UAE and beyond. The currency you’re converting from changes, but the structure of the comparison, package, housing, commute, household, doesn’t. Free, any time

Because earning more is important, but the real goal is a life in which your career and your salary work for you.
