chunks.x: Split sea and air freight, be ruthless about what’s worth shipping, and mind New Zealand’s strict biosecurity rules on food, plants and outdoor gear. We’ve kept this deliberately short. Moving to New Zealand , our national guide, walks through housing, banking, tax, healthcare, schools and settling in, step by step, with the official links. Ethicare are recruitment specialists; for the move itself, we’re glad to introduce you to the relocation and shipping partners we rely on. Open Moving to New Zealand Setting up home

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: Most healthcare professionals build their home gradually: a few essentials first, the rest as they settle. New Zealand has a well-established second-hand market, and it’s often possible to furnish an entire home for a fraction of the cost of buying new. Online marketplaces, charity stores and used-furniture retailers are especially popular in the first few months, while you find your feet and work out what you need. Indicative second-hand prices · approximate, in NZD Item Typical price Sofa $150–800 Dining table & chairs $150–700 Queen bed frame $100–500 Mattress (buy new) $400–1,000 Bedside tables $30–100 each Chest of drawers $80–300 Coffee table $40–200 TV unit $50–250 Washing machine $250–700 Fridge freezer $300–900 As a rough guide, many couples comfortably furnish a rental for around NZ$2,500–5,000 by combining second-hand furniture with a few key new purchases, a mattress and good bedding being the ones most people choose to buy new. Prices vary by region and condition, so treat these as a starting point, not a quote. Buying second-hand

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: Facebook Marketplace, the busiest place for local, near-new pieces Trade Me — New Zealand’s big online marketplace Habitat for Humanity ReStores City Mission stores Salvation Army Family Stores Hospice shops Most regions also have well-loved used-furniture retailers, ask a local or your new colleagues for the nearest one. Buying new on a budget

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: Mocka Early Settler Furniture Clearance Centre These stores often offer starter furniture packages at gentler prices than premium retailers, handy for the few pieces you’d rather buy new. Ethicare insight One of the biggest misconceptions we hear is that you need a fully furnished home ready on day one. In reality, building it gradually tends to save money and gives you the chance to create a home that reflects your own style. Rather than rushing into expensive purchases before you even know which neighbourhood you’ll stay in. “I spent ages deciding what to ship and what to leave behind. In the end, the cost of shipping some of our furniture was more than it was worth. There’s so much available second-hand in New Zealand through Facebook Marketplace and Trade Me.

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: We arrived with far less than we originally planned and just bought things as we needed them.” A clinician on what they shipped, and what they left behind “Moving our two dogs cost far more than we expected, but for us it was non-negotiable — they’re part of the family and they were coming with us. My advice to anyone moving with pets would be to research everything early and budget for it properly. It can easily be one of the biggest costs of relocating.” A clinician on relocating with two dogs Moving with children

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: New Zealand schools are welcoming and used to new arrivals, and children tend to find their feet quickly.

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: State schools are generally free for residents, and enrolment is often tied to where you live, so school choice and housing go hand in hand. Start enquiries early and check zones before you commit to an address.

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: Bring school reports, immunisation records and any learning-support paperwork. Having your children’s history to hand makes enrolment and the right placement much smoother on arrival.

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: Involve children in the move, talk openly about what’s changing, and expect a settling-in period. An outdoor, friendly school culture usually does the rest faster than parents dare to hope. Sophie’s insight The move itself is the part people lose the most sleep over, and almost always it goes more smoothly than the dread suggests. My advice: don’t ship more than you need, and don’t try to arrive with everything perfect. Sort a soft landing, a place to stay, a bank account, a SIM card, and let the rest come together in the first few weeks. The families who travel light, in their heads as much as their boxes, are the ones who arrive ready to enjoy it. Sophie CEO & Founder, Ethicare Resourcing Worth knowing

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.h: Shipping takes longer than you think
chunks.x: Sea freight can take many weeks to arrive. Pack a generous "first weeks" bag and plan to live for a while. Your container won’t be there to greet you. 2

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: New Zealand has strict rules on bringing in food, plants, wooden items and used outdoor equipment. Declare everything and clean your gear: fines for getting it wrong are real. 3

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: Bonds, rent in advance, a car, setting up a home, the early outlay adds up before your first pay lands. A cash buffer takes a lot of pressure off those opening weeks. 4

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.x: Amid the admin, the emotional side of leaving can ambush you. Give it room, plan how you’ll stay in touch, and be gentle with yourself and the family. Common questions

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Should I find a permanent home before I arrive? Usually not: most people rent somewhere short-term to begin with and choose their longer-term home once they’re on the ground. It’s hard to judge a neighbourhood from the other side of the world, and arriving with a soft landing booked takes the pressure off making a big decision sight-unseen. Sort the first few weeks, then take your time. Do most rental properties come with appliances? An oven and cooktop are almost always included, and a rangehood is common. Beyond that, don’t assume: a fridge, washing machine and dishwasher are often not provided , which surprises people coming from places where white goods are standard. Many rentals are let unfurnished, with appliances varying property to property, so always check the listing or ask the landlord exactly what’s included.

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: If you need to buy, the second-hand options in our furnishing guide above make it quick and affordable to sort. What is the quality of rental houses like in New Zealand? it varies. Newer builds are warm, dry and well insulated, but some older homes can feel colder and damper than newcomers expect. Central heating is far less common than in the UK, and many homes rely on a heat pump and good sun instead. The good news is that all rentals must now meet the government’s Healthy Homes Standards , which set legal minimums for heating, insulation, ventilation, moisture control and draught-stopping. When you’re viewing, look for insulation, a heat pump or other fixed heating, double glazing where possible, and which way the home faces, a north-facing home gets far more winter sun here. It’s perfectly reasonable to ask for the property’s Healthy Homes compliance statement before you sign.

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Can I get a mobile phone plan straight away? Yes, a prepaid SIM is the quickest route, available the day you arrive from any provider (One NZ, Spark, 2degrees or the budget brand Skinny) with just your passport. A pay-monthly plan can require a New Zealand bank account and a little local credit history, so many people start on prepaid and switch to a contract once their banking is set up. Coverage is strong in the cities and main towns; if you’re heading somewhere rural, it’s worth checking the provider’s coverage map. How much should I ship? Less than you’d instinctively pack. Furniture and bulky items are often not worth the freight, while sentimental and hard-to-replace things usually are. Many people send a modest sea-freight shipment and bring essentials by air, then buy the rest here. Get a few quotes early and let the cost guide your cull.

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Can I sort banking and tax before I land? Partly. Some banks let you begin opening an account from overseas, which is worth doing. Your IRD number for tax is generally sorted once you’ve arrived and have a bank account and visa in place. Getting both done early in your first days matters, without an IRD number you’ll be taxed at a higher rate until it’s resolved. What about bringing pets? It’s very doable, but it has one of the longest lead times of anything in the move, with import rules, vaccinations and quarantine to arrange. If a pet is coming, start that process as early as you possibly can and consider a specialist pet-relocation company, it’s not something to leave to the final weeks. Can you help with the move itself? We’re not a removals firm, but we’ve helped enough families through this to know who is worth trusting.

chunks.t: Preparing to move | New Zealand
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: We’re happy to introduce you to relocation, shipping and settling-in partners we rate, and to answer the in-between questions that no checklist quite covers. You won’t be left to work it all out alone. The day it all becomes real One day the lists end, and it’s just a corridor, two suitcases and a sign that says welcome. Everything in this step is in service of that morning. Get the big things moving early, and the rest really is just packing. Next · Stage 08

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.h: Pay here is transparent, and that’s a good thing
chunks.x: In New Zealand’s public health system pay is openly structured rather than privately bargained, so you can read it. Most healthcare roles are covered by national collective employment agreements : negotiated between Health New Zealand / Te Whatu Ora and the relevant union or professional association (for many allied health and medical-imaging roles, that’s the agreements negotiated through APEX ). Your pay sits on a published step or grade within that agreement, based on your experience and qualifications. There’s no haggling, and no wondering whether the person beside you is on more for the same work. Think of it as a ladder, not a negotiation. The rungs are public, the same for everyone, and reviewed regularly : your job is to land on the right one for your experience. That’s the part we help you get right.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.h: Pay here is transparent, and that’s a good thing
chunks.x: A note on figures We deliberately don’t publish specific salary numbers on this page. Pay rates change as agreements are renegotiated, and the right figure depends on your exact role, step and hours. Rather than risk an out-of-date number, we’ll confirm the current, correct rate for your role directly against the relevant collective agreement before you make any decision. The system behind the number

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Most roles are covered by a national collective agreement negotiated between Health New Zealand / Te Whatu Ora and the relevant union or professional body. It sets the pay scale, hours, leave and conditions for everyone in that profession. The scale

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Within each agreement is a series of steps. You’re placed on a step that reflects your years of relevant experience and your qualifications, and you typically progress up a step at a time as you accrue service. The review

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Agreements are renegotiated periodically, which is when the scales are updated. Because it’s collective, increases apply across the board rather than depending on an individual conversation with a manager. Outside the public system Some private and community providers set pay differently, and senior or specialist roles can have their own arrangements. The same principle still applies: we’ll always tell you exactly how a particular role’s pay is structured before you consider it. Landing on the right rung

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Two clinicians doing the same role can sit on different steps, by design. These are the things that decide where you start. A

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Years spent working in your profession, including experience earned overseas, are recognised and usually count towards your starting step. Getting your full history credited matters. B

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Your registration, post-graduate qualifications and any specialist scope of practice can affect where you sit and which roles you’re eligible for. C

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Senior, charge or team-lead positions sit higher on the scale, with added responsibility allowances in many agreements. D

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: You move up steps as you accumulate service, so your pay grows steadily without you having to renegotiate each year.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Keep clear evidence of your years of practice and prior roles, it’s the basis for the step you’re placed on, so gaps or vagueness can cost you.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Make sure post-graduate study and specialist training are reflected in your application, they can lift both your step and your options.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Whether a role is full-time, part-time or includes on-call changes your total earnings, not just the headline rate. We’ll spell this out for any role.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: It’s reasonable to ask exactly which step an offer places you on and why. A good employer, and a good recruiter, will explain it plainly. The whole picture

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: A fair amount sits on top of base pay, and it changes what lands in your account.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Many agreements pay enhanced rates for weekends, nights, public holidays and overtime, so shift patterns can lift earnings well above base.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Depending on the role, there may be allowances for on-call, recall, qualifications or specific responsibilities, all defined in the agreement.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: New Zealand’s workplace savings scheme includes employer contributions on top of your pay, a quiet but real part of the package.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Annual leave, public holidays, sick leave and, in many agreements, extra service-related leave: time that’s yours.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Funded training days, CPD support and continuing-education allowances feature in many agreements, helping your career keep growing.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Some roles include relocation assistance for international hires. Where it exists, we’ll make sure you know what’s on offer. Who has your back

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Because pay is set collectively, unions and professional associations negotiate the agreements your pay sits within. Joining is your choice, and most clinicians do. Who negotiates your pay

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.h: The right body for your role
chunks.x: Which union covers you depends on your profession. For example, APEX represents many allied health, scientific and medical-imaging roles; the NZ Nurses Organisation covers nursing; and senior and resident doctors have their own associations. We’ll tell you which agreement and body apply to your role. What they do

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: They negotiate the national pay scales and conditions, but also support members with workplace questions, professional development and representation if an issue ever arises, a reassuring backstop when you’re new to a system. Your choice

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Membership is voluntary, and you’re generally covered by your agreement’s terms either way. Many people join for the representation and support, particularly in their first years finding their feet here. Good to know You don’t need to work any of this out alone. When we talk through a role, we’ll tell you exactly which collective agreement covers it and which union or association represents your profession, so you know who to turn to before you even arrive. What lands in your account

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Headline salaries are quoted before tax, and New Zealand’s system is simple compared with many places clinicians move from. Income tax ( PAYE ) is deducted automatically from your pay by your employer, so most people never file a complicated return. You’ll need an IRD number (your tax identification number) soon after you arrive, and giving it to your employer ensures you’re taxed at the right rate from the start rather than an emergency one. There’s also a small ACC levy that funds New Zealand’s no-fault accident cover, which means you and your family are covered for injury from day one. Crucially, there’s no separate National Insurance-style contribution as in the UK, and GST (the sales tax) is already included in displayed prices, so what you see on a shelf is what you pay. We’ll always talk in terms that help you picture your real monthly take-home, not just the gross figure.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: The practical upshot: once your IRD number and KiwiSaver choice are sorted in your first weeks, your pay runs smoothly and predictably. Our living & thriving guide covers setting up the everyday money side , bank account, IRD, KiwiSaver, step by step. Your safety net

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Some things are covered for everyone automatically; others are worth adding, especially with a mortgage or a family.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: New Zealand’s no-fault accident scheme covers treatment and a portion of lost income if you or your family are injured in an accident, from your first day, funded through levies. It’s one of the reassuring things about life here.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Residents and many work-visa holders can access the public health system. Our living & thriving guide covers who’s eligible and how it works.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Optional, but popular. Many take it out for faster elective treatment and more choice of specialist. Some roles include it as a benefit, which we’ll always flag.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Income protection, life and trauma cover are worth considering, particularly once you’ve a mortgage or dependents. A local adviser can tailor this to your situation.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: The everyday insurances. Car insurance isn’t legally compulsory here, but it’s strongly recommended, and contents cover is well worth it while you’re renting.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: In the public system you’re generally covered by your employer, and ACC changes how treatment-injury claims work compared with many countries. Some scopes or private work may need your own cover, confirm what’s required with your regulator and employer. A note on advice Insurance and ACC rules depend on your circumstances and visa, and they change, so always confirm the current position at the source. Ethicare are recruitment specialists, not financial advisers, but we’re glad to introduce you to advisers we trust. Earning, against living

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Housing and groceries are the costs that surprise most newcomers, and they vary a lot by region, a smaller city or town can stretch the same salary much further than a major centre. We’ll talk through the real numbers for where you’re considering.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Shorter commutes, the outdoors on your doorstep and a respect for time off mean many clinicians feel better off here even where the headline figure is comparable to home.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.x: Because base pay is national, the same role pays the same across the country, so your money goes noticeably further in more affordable regions. Our destination guides help you weigh this up.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.h: How pay is structured: New Zealand, Australia & the UK
chunks.x: New Zealand Australia United Kingdom How pay is set National collective agreements; published steps State/territory awards & enterprise agreements National pay bands (e.g. Agenda for Change) Negotiation Collective, not individual Mostly collective, some individual Collective banding On top of base Penal rates, allowances, KiwiSaver Penalty rates, superannuation Unsocial-hours pay, NHS pension Tax admin Simple PAYE; no NI; small ACC levy PAYG; Medicare levy PAYE plus National Insurance Variation by location Base is national; cost of living varies Varies by state Limited (London weighting) Why no numbers here Exchange rates, tax differences and cost of living make raw salary comparisons misleading. The more useful question is take-home against local costs and lifestyle, which is exactly the conversation we’ll have with you for your specific role. No surprises

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.h: Knowing your exact rate, before you decide
chunks.x: For any role we discuss, we’ll confirm the current rate against the relevant collective agreement , tell you the step you’d be placed on and the reasoning, and walk through the full package : base, penal rates, allowances, KiwiSaver and leave, so the picture is complete. Where pay sits outside a standard agreement, we’ll say so plainly and explain how it’s set instead. A move this big deserves clear numbers, straight answers and the time to think them over. Sophie’s insight Money is rarely the first reason people move, but it has to add up, and it’s one of the things clinicians feel most awkward asking about. I’d rather you ask us everything. Because pay here is set by published agreements, I can show you exactly where a role sits and why, with nothing hidden. My promise is simple: you’ll know your real take-home, against the cost of living where you’re headed, long before you have to make any decision. That clarity is what lets people move with confidence instead of crossed fingers. Sophie CEO & Founder, Ethicare Resourcing Common questions

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about pay
chunks.x: Why don’t you list salary figures on this page? Because the figure depends on your exact role, step and hours, and because the agreements are renegotiated over time. Rather than publish a number that could be out of date or misleading for your situation, we confirm the current, correct rate for your specific role against the relevant collective agreement when we talk. Can I negotiate my salary? In the public system, base pay follows a published scale rather than individual negotiation, which protects you as much as anything. What does matter, and where good representation pays off, is making sure you’re placed on the correct step for your experience and qualifications. That’s something we actively help you get right. Will my overseas experience count? Generally yes. Relevant experience earned abroad is usually recognised towards your step.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about pay
chunks.x: The key is documenting it clearly so it’s properly credited. We’ll help you present your history so nothing is overlooked. How does take-home compare to where I am now? It depends on your current country’s tax and cost of living, so a raw comparison can mislead. We’ll help you think in terms of monthly take-home against local costs, and factor in the things that don’t show on a payslip, like shorter commutes, strong leave and the lifestyle on offer. What’s KiwiSaver, and do I have to join? KiwiSaver is New Zealand’s workplace savings scheme, with contributions from you and your employer. If you’re eligible, new employees are usually enrolled automatically with the option to opt out, and you can choose your contribution level. We’ll point you to the basics so you can make an informed choice in your first weeks. Can I pay into KiwiSaver or a pension on the AEWV? Usually not straight away.

chunks.t: Salary & pay in New Zealand healthcare
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about pay
chunks.x: Joining KiwiSaver generally requires you to be entitled to live in New Zealand indefinitely, so on a temporary work visa such as the Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) you typically can’t join yet, and you wouldn’t receive the employer or government contributions until you gain residence. Many people save another way in the meantime and join KiwiSaver once they’re residents. The rules matter here, so confirm your eligibility with a KiwiSaver provider or Inland Revenue. Keep exploring

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: The visa usually follows the job, not the other way around
chunks.x: Reviewed October 2026 · checked against Immigration New Zealand’s current published guidance. Immigration rules change, always confirm at the source For most healthcare professionals, the visa follows a job offer from an accredited New Zealand employer. New Zealand has deliberately built fast, welcoming routes for the skills it needs most, and healthcare is high on that list. The Green List sets out in-demand roles with streamlined pathways to residence, and many of the professions we place are on it. Being on the list does not by itself qualify you: you still need to meet the occupation, qualification, registration, pay and other requirements of the route. One note up front: Ethicare are recruitment specialists, not licensed immigration advisers. We can explain how the recruitment side fits and point you to Immigration New Zealand’s official guidance. We can’t advise on which visa suits your individual circumstances; Immigration New Zealand decides eligibility. How it fits together

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Registration, your job offer and your visa progress alongside one another rather than in a strict queue. The offer

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: A job with an accredited employer
chunks.x: Most work visas require a job offer from an employer accredited by Immigration New Zealand. The employers we work with hold that accreditation, which is what makes the visa possible. The visa

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: With an offer in hand, the question becomes which visa fits: usually a work visa to begin, or, for some Green List roles, a direct residence application. The future

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: For many healthcare roles the destination isn’t a temporary stay but residence, the security of putting down roots, which is exactly what most families are really after. The Green List

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: The Green List, in plain terms
chunks.x: The Green List names roles New Zealand is short of, in two tiers. Being on it opens a residence route, but you still have to meet that route’s requirements for occupation, qualifications, registration, employment and pay. Tier 1

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Residence from the outset For the most in-demand roles, you can apply for residence directly with a qualifying job offer, rather than working for years first. Residence application from the start Your partner and dependent children can be included; each must meet health and character requirements You hold residence once it is granted, not when you apply Tier 2

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Residence after a period of work For other Green List roles, you generally work in the role in New Zealand for 24 months and can then apply for residence. You arrive on a work visa, settle in, and the residence pathway opens up as you go. Begin on an Accredited Employer Work Visa Apply for residence after the qualifying period Your partner and children apply for their own visas, depending on your role and pay

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: The Green List is set by Immigration New Zealand and reviewed periodically, so roles and tiers can change. Check the current answer for your profession on Immigration New Zealand’s Green List page . The main routes

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: The visas you’re most likely to meet
chunks.x: For healthcare professionals moving with Ethicare, a handful of visa types come up again and again. The usual starting point

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: The main work visa, tied to a job offer from an accredited employer. For many people it’s how they first arrive and begin working. Official details Green List · Tier 1

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: For eligible Tier 1 roles with a qualifying job offer: apply for residence directly, with your partner and dependent children included in the application. Official details Green List · Tier 2

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Work in a qualifying Tier 2 role for the required period, generally 24 months, then apply for residence. Official details For your family

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Your partner and children apply for their own visas. Whether you can support them depends on your visa, role and pay. Official details

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Lets you live and work in New Zealand for a set period, usually for a named employer and role. It ends when it expires unless you get another visa. Residence

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Lets you live, work and study in New Zealand indefinitely. Your first resident visa usually has travel conditions that limit how long you can re-enter as a resident. Permanent

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Removes those travel conditions. You can usually apply after holding a resident visa for two years and showing your commitment to New Zealand. Visa categories, criteria and names are set by Immigration New Zealand and can change. This is an orientation, not immigration advice. Always confirm current detail at immigration.govt.nz . You move as a family

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Partners and children can usually join you, but they apply for their own visas, and whether you can support them depends on your visa, role and pay. Check the current rules with Immigration New Zealand before you plan around them.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: Your partner may be able to work
chunks.x: If you hold an Accredited Employer Work Visa in a skilled role and earn above Immigration New Zealand’s minimum for supporting a partner, your partner can apply for a work visa of their own, often with open work rights. They must meet the requirements themselves.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Dependent children can usually get a student visa based on your work visa, which generally lets them attend state school as domestic students. Confirm it for your visa before you commit to a school.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: A residence application can include your partner and dependent children. Each of them must meet the health and character requirements, and residence is only yours once it is granted. The visa journey

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: An offer from an accredited employer is the foundation everything else rests on. This is where we focus first, because once it’s in place the visa options become clear. 2

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Using Immigration New Zealand’s guidance, work out which visa fits: a work visa, Straight to Residence or Work to Residence, depending on your role, the Green List and your circumstances. 3

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Passport, qualifications, job offer, registration progress, and health and character checks such as medicals and police certificates. Starting these early avoids the most common delays. 4

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Your application, and your family’s, goes to Immigration New Zealand with the relevant fees. From here it’s an assessment and processing period. Processing times vary, and a wait is not necessarily a sign of a problem with your application. 5

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Once granted, you can firm up flights, timing and the practical move. This is where Preparing to move takes over from the paperwork. Sophie’s insight People brace themselves for the visa to be the hardest part, and for many healthcare professionals it goes more smoothly than they feared. My one piece of advice is to take the health and character checks seriously and start them early; a delayed medical or a slow police certificate is what most often holds things up. Use Immigration New Zealand’s guidance, lean on us for the employer side, and keep your documents moving. Sophie CEO & Founder, Ethicare Resourcing In their words

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Three clinicians on the moment immigration stopped being an idea and became real. “Getting the job offer was exciting. Getting the work visa approved was the moment I knew I was actually moving to New Zealand.” On the moment it became real “I had assumed I would need to work in New Zealand for several years before I could even think about residence. Finding out there was a direct pathway for my profession was a very pleasant surprise.” On the direct pathway to residence “For me, residency meant security. I was moving my children to the other side of the world, so I needed to know there was a realistic long-term future for us in New Zealand.” On what residency means for a family Worth knowing

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Visa categories, the Green List and criteria are reviewed over time. Always confirm the current position at the source, and don’t rely on what was true for a friend a year or two ago. 2

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.x: Medicals and police certificates from every country you’ve lived in can be slow to obtain. Some countries also need your fingerprints before they will issue a certificate, which adds an appointment. Each certificate must be less than six months old when you submit the visa application, so time them for when the application is ready to go. Most are straightforward, but some applications need further health or character assessment, so they reward an early start more than almost anything else. How to get a police certificate, by country . 3

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: There are costs to budget for
chunks.x: Visa application fees, medicals, certificates and the levy add up across a family. They’re manageable and predictable, just plan for them from the beginning. 4

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: Take extra care with anything unusual
chunks.x: A complex history, a past visa refusal or a health condition are all navigable. Declare everything, and read Immigration New Zealand’s guidance on your situation closely before you apply. 5

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: Age limits sit on residence, not the work visa
chunks.x: The Accredited Employer Work Visa has no age limit. Straight to Residence , Work to Residence and the Skilled Migrant Category each require you to be 55 or younger when you apply. Common questions

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Do I need a job offer before I can get a visa? For the main work and residence routes, yes, a job offer from an accredited employer is usually the starting point. That’s why we focus on securing the right role first: once the offer is in place, the visa pathway becomes clear and the rest follows. It’s far less a queue than three pieces moving together. Can my profession get me residence? For many healthcare roles there is a residence route. Some Green List roles can apply directly; others after a period of work. Being on the list does not by itself qualify you: check the current list and the requirements for your route with Immigration New Zealand. Can my partner work and my children go to school? Often, yes, but it is not automatic. Your partner and children apply for their own visas, and whether you can support them depends on your visa, role and pay.

chunks.t: Immigration & visas | New Zealand
chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Children holding a student visa based on your work visa can generally attend state school as domestic students. Check the current rules with Immigration New Zealand. How long does a visa take? It varies by visa type, your circumstances and Immigration New Zealand’s current processing times, which it publishes on its website. Delays are not necessarily caused by anything you have done. What you can control is how quickly your documents, medicals and checks come together, so start those early. Do I need an immigration adviser? For straightforward cases, employers and Immigration New Zealand’s own guidance carry you a long way. Advisers can be expensive and are not always necessary: if you have the time to work through the process yourself, many people do, and it can save a good deal of money. We’re recruiters, not immigration advisers, so we don’t recommend one.

chunks.h: The things people ask us first
chunks.x: Is there an age limit? Not for the Accredited Employer Work Visa. The residence visas do have one: Straight to Residence, Work to Residence and the Skilled Migrant Category each require you to be 55 or younger when you apply. See Immigration New Zealand: Straight to Residence . Next · Stage 07 continues

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Moving pets to New Zealand works from many countries, but it requires considerably more planning than booking an extra seat on the flight. New Zealand operates strict biosecurity requirements designed to protect their unique environments and animal health. That means your pet’s move needs to be planned alongside your own — not a few weeks before departure. For most owners, a pet isn’t cargo to be transported after the move. They’re part of who’s moving. Section 01 · Timing

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: The process your pet follows depends on the country you are moving from . Requirements can include microchipping, vaccinations, rabies testing, parasite treatments, veterinary examinations, official documentation, import permits and quarantine. And the order matters: where a test or treatment has to happen within a specified window, getting the sequence wrong can delay the whole move. When to start As soon as New Zealand becomes a serious possibility — not when the removal boxes are packed. You don’t need a signed contract to start researching your pet’s requirements, and starting early is the cheapest thing you can do. Section 02 · The rules

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Requirements follow the biosecurity risk of your country of export, so the same breed can face different processes from different countries. New Zealand

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: As with Australia, what your dog or cat needs depends partly on where they’re travelling from. The process can involve: An import permit Microchip identification Vaccinations and testing Parasite treatments Veterinary examinations and official certification The regulator is the Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI). It puts every country into a category, and the category sets the process. A new import health standard came into force on 1 July 2026, with a transition period to April 2027, so check which one applies to your dates: mpi.govt.nz — bringing cats and dogs to NZ .

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: Where you are coming from changes the process
chunks.x: From Australia Category 1. No import permit and usually no quarantine if the paperwork is in order; a vet inspects at the border. The simplest route by far. From the UK or Ireland Approved countries. Import permit, microchip, vaccinations, parasite treatments, vet certification, then at least 10 days in an MPI-approved quarantine facility. From South Africa Category 3, so the same steps as the UK plus a rabies blood test (titre), with a waiting period of months between the test and the flight, then at least 10 days’ quarantine. Start earliest of all. From anywhere else If your country is not on MPI’s approved list, a cat or dog cannot come directly. Some families route the animal through an approved country first; it is slow and expensive. Check the list before you plan. Categories as published by MPI in October 2026.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: Where you are coming from changes the process
chunks.x: We don’t promise any animal is eligible: confirm your country and your pet on MPI’s list. Check the source Regulations change. A checklist somebody used a few years ago — or even relatively recently — should never replace current government guidance. Check the source, not the forum post. Section 03 · Quarantine

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: Will my pet have to quarantine?
chunks.x: For most cats and dogs, yes. Unless your pet is coming from Australia on compliant paperwork, it goes into an MPI-approved quarantine facility for a minimum of 10 days, and longer if an inspection finds a problem. There are three facilities, in Auckland and Christchurch, so availability becomes part of your relocation timeline . Facilities book up, and that’s one of the clearest reasons pet travel shouldn’t be left until the end of the process. Three dates, not one Your employment start date, your family’s flights and your pet’s travel date may not be the same. Plan them as three linked decisions rather than assuming everyone arrives together. Real story · Nova the dachshund “It was a big move for us, especially since we also relocated our dog, Nova. We stayed in a hotel at first before settling into a rental home.” Janita and Jonathan brought Nova from South Africa to Auckland in January 2024. How the whole move went → Section 04 · Sequencing

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: Your pet doesn’t necessarily have to travel with you
chunks.x: A clinician might travel first, begin work, move out of temporary accommodation and secure a pet-friendly long-term rental before their partner, children and pets follow. Other families move together and arrange for the pet to arrive separately. There isn’t one correct way. Think about what makes the transition easiest for both your family and your animal — and remember that arriving into a settled home is a much gentler landing for a dog than arriving into a serviced apartment and a house-hunt. Section 05 · Somewhere to live

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Getting your pet into the country is only half the problem. You also need somewhere to live that will have them. Check the rules around pets before assuming a property is suitable — and pay particular attention to temporary accommodation. A serviced apartment or short-term let that works perfectly for a family may not accept a dog or cat. If your pet is arriving after you, use that window to find suitable long-term accommodation. Then think beyond whether the landlord permits pets: Is there enough space? Is there a secure garden, if you have a dog? Are there good places nearby for walking? How long will your pet be alone while you’re working? The right home for your family needs to work for them too. Pet bonds Since December 2025, a landlord who agrees to a pet can ask for a pet bond of up to two weeks’ rent on top of the usual bond of up to four weeks. Tenants are responsible for pet damage beyond fair wear and tear. The rules are on Tenancy Services , and renting in New Zealand covers the rest of the upfront costs. Section 06 · Cost

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: The total depends on where you’re travelling from, the size and type of animal, veterinary requirements, transport and whether quarantine is required. Potential expenses include veterinary appointments, vaccinations, blood tests, official certification, permits, airline transport, travel crates, pet relocation companies and quarantine. For a large dog or multiple animals, the total can become a significant part of the family’s relocation budget.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: We don’t publish prices, because they vary with the animal, the route and the exchange rate. Use these lines to build your own, with quotes against each: Line What it covers Your quote Vet preparation Microchip, vaccinations, rabies titre test where required, parasite treatments, pre-export examination and certificates Permit and official fees MPI import permit, export certification in your country, border inspection on arrival Transport Airline freight, an airline-approved crate, transfers at each end, and any stopover handling Quarantine A minimum of 10 days at the daily rate, plus collection or delivery Relocation agent If you use one: their fee, and exactly what it includes Contingency A failed test, a missed window or a delayed flight can add weeks. Allow for it. Get quotes early It is far easier to plan for this six months out than to discover it once you’ve committed most of your savings to flights, accommodation and setting up the new home. Our relocation cost guide shows where this sits against everything else you’ll be paying for. Section 07 · The journey

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: Ask for it stage by stage
chunks.x: Depending on the route and airline arrangements, your pet may travel in a specially designed crate in an appropriate part of the aircraft rather than alongside you in the cabin. There may also be stopovers or transfers. A reputable pet transport specialist or airline should be able to explain the journey clearly, including where your animal will be during each stage. If your pet is elderly or has a medical condition, discuss the proposed route with your vet well in advance. Medication & sedation

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: Not your decision to make alone
chunks.x: If you’re worried about how your pet will cope, speak to your vet and the company responsible for transporting them. Sedation can create additional risks during air travel and may not be permitted or recommended in some circumstances. The right approach depends on the individual animal and the requirements of the carrier — so ask both, and follow the advice. Should you use a pet relocation company? You don’t have to manage all of this alone. Specialists can coordinate veterinary timelines, documentation, travel crates, flights and quarantine arrangements — at a cost. Some families value having someone run a complicated process while they’re simultaneously dealing with visas, registration, jobs, schools and their own move; others prefer to manage it themselves. If you do use one, establish exactly what the quote includes and what you’ll still need to arrange separately. Section 08 · Check before you spend

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: Older pets, restricted breeds & other animals
chunks.x: Three situations where the answer needs checking before you spend any money on the process. Older pets

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Moving a healthy three-year-old dog and moving a fourteen-year-old dog are very different decisions. For an older animal, the length of the journey, underlying conditions and ability to cope with transport all need careful thought. That doesn’t automatically mean an older pet can’t relocate. It means the decision belongs with your vet, rather than resting on whether the paperwork permits it. Breeds & species

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: New Zealand restricts the importation of certain dog breeds or types, and there can be restrictions affecting hybrid animals. If there’s any possibility your dog falls within a restricted category, check the official rules first — don’t rely on appearance, breeder descriptions or informal advice. For pets other than dogs and cats — birds, rabbits, reptiles — don’t assume the dog-and-cat process applies. Check whether your animal can legally be imported before making any plans. For some species and countries of origin, it may not be possible at all. Section 09 · Settling in

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: The first few weeks after arrival
chunks.x: The journey is only one part of your pet’s transition. Establish a predictable routine as quickly as you can. Find a local vet, update identification details where required, and learn the local rules for registration, microchipping and dog control. Then do the enjoyable part. Find the walks. Find the parks. Find the beach. For a lot of families, exploring the new neighbourhood with the dog is the first thing that makes the place feel like home. Section 10 · The package

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Pet relocation isn’t normally a standard employment benefit — but that isn’t quite the end of the question. If your employer is providing a general relocation allowance rather than paying only specified expenses, you may have some flexibility over how that money is used. Never assume pet transport is covered. Ask what the relocation contribution can and cannot be used for before making any bookings. Our offer guide covers how to raise this well — and relocation support is often more negotiable than the salary itself. Useful contacts

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Specialist relocation companies can coordinate veterinary requirements, documentation, flights, travel crates and quarantine. For candidates relocating from the UK, established providers include:

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: A vet-led international pet relocation company providing services to Australia and New Zealand.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Heathrow-based international pet transport specialist with veterinary and animal-handling facilities.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: UK pet relocation company arranging international transport for dogs, cats and other animals. Quarantine in New Zealand

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: New Zealand uses MPI-approved private quarantine facilities. Current facilities include: Pethaven Quarantine Services — Auckland Qualified Pet Services — Auckland Canterbury Quarantine Services — Christchurch Requirements for importing animals depend on the country your pet is travelling from, and they change without notice — always check the current Ministry for Primary Industries guidance before making arrangements. These are commercial companies. Ethicare doesn’t endorse them and receives nothing from them; they are listed because candidates ask who exists. Get several quotes and confirm current government requirements directly before you book anything. Sophie’s insight I should declare an interest: we are all completely soft about animals here, and there are two dogs in the Ethicare office on any given day.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: So when someone tells me they won’t move without their dog, I don’t treat that as a complication to be worked around — it’s just one of the things that has to work. What I’d say is that this is the part of a relocation people leave latest and regret most, because the timings are fixed by regulation and no amount of goodwill speeds them up. Raise it with us in the first conversation, not the last. It’s far easier to build the whole move around your pet’s timeline than to discover six weeks before departure that the sequence doesn’t work. Sophie Founder, Ethicare Resourcing Part two · Your belongings

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: The other half of this chapter. Most families ship less than they planned, and the ones who are glad of it decided early what was worth the journey.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Shipping is priced by volume, so the question for every item is whether it is worth more than the space it takes. Furniture rarely is: second-hand furniture is plentiful and cheap in New Zealand, and most clinicians furnish gradually after they arrive. Books, tools, children’s things, bikes and anything with a story usually are. Electrical goods work on 230 volts with a different plug; cars are a separate process with their own import rules.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: A shared container (groupage) suits most families: you pay for the space you use and wait for the container to fill, so allow 8 to 14 weeks door to door. Your own 20-foot container is faster and only makes sense for a full household. Air freight for a few boxes you need in the first fortnight, priced by weight.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: New Zealand inspects household goods closely. You complete a customs declaration and an unaccompanied personal effects form before the shipment lands, and MPI may inspect it. Anything that has touched soil, plants or animals (garden tools, boots, tents, bikes, sports gear, wooden items, vacuum cleaners) must be scrupulously clean, or it will be cleaned at your cost or destroyed. Most used personal effects come in free of duty and GST if you have owned and used them and are arriving to live here. Check New Zealand Customs: moving to New Zealand and MPI: bringing personal items .

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.x: Take marine transit insurance for the replacement value, not the purchase price. Check whether it covers the whole journey or only the sea leg. Get at least three quotes from international movers, and compare what each includes: packing, customs clearance, delivery to the door, and storage if your rental isn’t ready. Keep a numbered inventory with photographs. You need it for customs, for insurance, and for the day the boxes arrive. For where shipping sits against everything else you will pay for, use the moving cost calculator . Common questions

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about moving with pets
chunks.x: How far in advance should I start? As soon as the move becomes a serious possibility. Several of the veterinary steps have to happen in a particular order and within specified windows, and quarantine facilities have finite availability — so the timeline is set by regulation rather than by how organised you are. Starting early costs nothing and prevents the most common delays. Will my dog definitely have to go into quarantine? Not necessarily — it depends on the destination, the animal and your country of origin, since New Zealand categorises countries by biosecurity risk. Where quarantine does apply, treat facility availability as part of your relocation timeline rather than an afterthought. Can my pet travel on the same flight as me? Sometimes, but don’t assume it.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about moving with pets
chunks.x: Depending on the route and airline, your pet may travel in a specially designed crate in an appropriate part of the aircraft rather than in the cabin, and there may be stopovers or transfers. A reputable specialist or the airline should walk you through where your animal will be at each stage. Should my pet be sedated for the journey? That’s a decision for your vet and the transport company, not something to arrange yourself. Sedation can carry additional risks in air travel and may not be permitted or recommended depending on the animal and the carrier’s requirements. My dog is a restricted breed — is that the end of it? Check the official rules before assuming either way, and before spending anything. New Zealand restricts certain breeds or types, and there can be restrictions on hybrid animals.

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: The questions we’re asked about moving with pets
chunks.x: Don’t rely on appearance, breeder descriptions or informal advice — this is one to confirm at the source. What about a rabbit, bird or reptile? Considerably more complicated, and for some species and countries of origin importing simply isn’t possible. The dog-and-cat process doesn’t transfer. Confirm whether your animal can legally be imported before making any relocation plans around it. Will an employer pay for pet relocation? It isn’t a standard benefit, so never assume it. But if the employer offers a general relocation allowance rather than reimbursing only specified expenses, you may have flexibility over how it’s used. Ask what the contribution can and can’t cover before you book. Free, any time

chunks.t: Bringing your pets to New Zealand, and shipping your belongings
chunks.h: Plan the pet’s timeline with the rest of the move
chunks.x: Their travel date, the family’s flights and your start date are three linked decisions. Put them in your plan early, with the quarantine booking and the shipping dates beside them. chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: Housing ranges from city apartments to suburban homes and beachside properties. Costs vary widely by region — generally far more affordable outside Auckland and Wellington. Kettle on. About 7 min $300 /wk 1-bed apartment (from, regional) $500 /wk 2–3 bed house (from, regional) Left Side of the road you drive on Grocery prices are consistent nationwide, with abundant fresh local produce. The lower cost of living in regional centres — paired with the country’s natural and cultural offerings — makes them especially appealing for families. Driving is on the left, and a network of well-maintained highways connects the country. Public transport is strongest in the main cities; in smaller towns a car is recommended. Utilities are straightforward to set up once you have an address.

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: Rents vary widely by region and property type. These are indicative weekly ranges to help you budget — always check current listings for your area. Where you settle Flatshare 1-bed 3-bed house Major city (e.g. Auckland) $200–400 $400–700 $600–1,200 Smaller city $150–300 $250–450 $400–800 Town $100–250 $200–400 $300–600 Village / rural $80–200 $150–350 $200–500 Indicative weekly rent in NZD. Most rentals are unfurnished.

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: 1 · Search Most listings are on Trade Me Property and realestate.co.nz. Filter by suburb, then check the commute to your hospital and, if you have children, the school zone, before you fall for a house. 2 · View Agents usually run open homes at set times, and the better places go within days. From overseas, ask a colleague or the agent for a video walk-through, but try to see a place in person before signing anything long-term. 3 · Apply Have your pack ready: passport and visa, your employment contract or offer letter as proof of income, and references from previous landlords. Overseas references are accepted; make sure they can be reached by email. 4 · Sign Read the tenancy agreement before you sign. Fixed-term tenancies now roll into periodic ones at the end of the term unless notice is given, and tenants on a periodic tenancy give 21 days’ notice to leave. Trade Me and realestate.co.nz are commercial businesses. We don’t endorse them; they are simply where most rentals are listed.

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: Before you get the keys, expect to pay a bond of up to four weeks’ rent, lodged with Tenancy Services and returned when you leave, plus up to two weeks’ rent in advance. If the landlord agrees to a pet, they can also ask for a pet bond of up to two weeks’ rent. Example at NZ$600 a week Amount Bond (four weeks) $2,400 Rent in advance (two weeks) $1,200 Total before you move in $3,600 Example only. Furnishing, moving costs and any pet bond are on top. Bond and rent in advance are the legal maximums, so some landlords ask for less. Tenancy Services is the official source. For the whole move, use the moving cost calculator .

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: Since 1 July 2025 all private rentals must meet the Healthy Homes standards : a fixed heater that can heat the main living room, ceiling and underfloor insulation, opening windows in every living space, extractor fans in kitchens and bathrooms, good drainage and no unreasonable draughts. Older New Zealand houses can be cold and damp, so ask about them anyway. What heats the living room, and roughly what power costs in winter. Whether there is insulation in the ceiling and under the floor. Any signs of damp or mould, especially in bedrooms and wardrobes. Which way the house faces: north-facing rooms get the winter sun. Whether the rent includes water, lawns or anything else.

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: Most rentals come empty. New Zealand has a busy second-hand market, and most clinicians furnish gradually: a bed and the kitchen basics in the first week, the rest once they know what the house needs. Essentials Typical second-hand price Queen bed frame $100–500 Mattress (most people buy this new) $400–1,000 Sofa $150–800 Dining table & chairs $150–700 Washing machine $250–700 Fridge freezer $300–900 Indicative second-hand prices in NZD. They vary by region and condition, so treat them as a starting point for a budget, not a quote. Couples who mix second-hand furniture with a new mattress and bedding tend to furnish a rental for around NZ$2,500–5,000 all in. Where people look Second-hand — Facebook Marketplace is the busiest place for local, near-new pieces; then Trade Me, Habitat for Humanity ReStores, City Mission stores, Salvation Army Family Stores and hospice shops.

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: New, on a budget — several national retailers sell starter pieces and packages for the few things you would rather buy new, such as a mattress. Colleagues will tell you which are good value locally. Locally — most regions have a well-loved used-furniture dealer. New colleagues will know the nearest one. “I spent ages deciding what to ship and what to leave behind. In the end, the cost of shipping some of our furniture was more than it was worth. There’s so much available second-hand in New Zealand through Facebook Marketplace and Trade Me. We arrived with far less than we originally planned and just bought things as we needed them.” A clinician on what they shipped, and what they left behind Our view The misconception we hear most is that the house needs to be furnished by day one. Building it gradually costs less, and it means you are not buying a sofa for a suburb you may not stay in. Our advice is usually to arrive with less than you planned and buy as you go.

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: Groceries Prices are fairly consistent nationwide. Budget supermarkets like Pak’nSave are cheapest; New World and specialty stores sit higher. Fresh local produce is excellent. Utilities Power, internet and phone are quick to set up once you have an address — comparison sites make switching providers easy. Where it’s cheaper Regional centres cost noticeably less than Auckland and Wellington, especially on housing. Day-to-day banking EFTPOS is used everywhere, and most pay arrives by fortnightly direct credit.

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: A few of the things on your doorstep The outdoors — hiking and tramping (the Great Walks are world-famous), skiing in the Southern Alps, mountain biking, kayaking and surf beaches. Wildlife & wide skies — whale watching at Kaikōura, some of the Southern Hemisphere’s best stargazing, and native birdlife found nowhere else. Food, wine & culture — Marlborough and Central Otago wine regions, a strong café culture, festivals, and a sporting life built around rugby, cricket and netball.

chunks.t: Renting in New Zealand
chunks.x: New Zealand is religiously diverse and tolerant. Churches of many denominations sit alongside mosques, temples, gurdwaras and synagogues in the main centres, and there’s an easy acceptance of those who follow no faith at all. Go deeper Living & thriving in New Zealand → Ethicare Resourcing

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: In healthcare, te reo Māori arrives with a Treaty relationship that shapes how care is designed, measured and delivered. You are asked to arrive willing, not expert. Kettle on. About 7 min

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.h: Te Tiriti o Waitangi, in practice
chunks.x: Signed in 1840 between Māori and the Crown, Te Tiriti is the founding agreement of the country. The history sits in About New Zealand — what matters on your first shift is what the Treaty relationship asks of you as a clinician. Every health regulator in New Zealand expects culturally safe practice, though each sets its own standards and assesses them in its own way; check your own board’s. The three principles below are the familiar starting point, not the whole account. The Ministry of Health works from five: tino rangatiratanga (Māori self-determination), equity, active protection, options (including kaupapa Māori services) and partnership. The Ministry’s Te Tiriti framework sets them out.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Working with Māori patients, whānau and communities rather than delivering to them. Decisions made together, and plans the whānau has agreed to. In practice The person answering your questions may not be the person who decides. Ask who should be part of the conversation before you start, not after the plan is written.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Māori involvement at every level — in their own care, and in how services are designed and run. Kaupapa Māori providers deliver care by Māori, for Māori, and you will refer to them and work alongside them. In practice If a service is not reaching a group, that is treated as a service problem to solve — not a patient problem to record as non-attendance.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Actively protecting Māori health and wellbeing, and closing outcome gaps that are well documented and long-standing. In practice Equity is not equality. Two people with the same diagnosis may need different amounts of your time, and giving it to them is the standard rather than favouritism.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: One of the stated priorities of New Zealand healthcare is improving health outcomes and reducing inequities for Māori. Māori experience poorer outcomes across a range of health measures, alongside barriers to timely, appropriate care. Addressing that is a responsibility across the whole system, and it is the reason the Treaty principles above exist in health policy at all. For a clinician arriving from overseas, the central idea is this: giving everyone the same care does not always produce equitable outcomes. Equality gives everyone the same support. Equity gives people the support their circumstances need, so each has a fair chance of a good outcome. In practice it might mean: Recognising barriers such as transport, cost, language, or difficulty getting to appointments. Taking time to understand a patient’s circumstances, preferences and wider whānau needs.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Working alongside Māori health professionals and kaupapa Māori services where appropriate. Reflecting on how your assumptions, communication and clinical decisions may shape the care a patient receives. Supporting care that is culturally safe, accessible and responsive to the person in front of you. Nobody expects you to arrive knowing everything about Māori health. The expectation is that you arrive understanding why equity matters, willing to learn, and committed to care that works for the people receiving it.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: A Māori model of health you are likely to meet in your first week: wellbeing as a house standing on four walls, on the whenua beneath it. If one wall is weak the house is unstable — which is a more useful way to think about the person in front of you than a problem list is. Te Whare Tapa Whā: Sir Mason Durie’s model of health as a house with four walls. Physical Taha tinana The body — pain, function, mobility, strength, nutrition. What most of us were trained to assess first. Mind & emotions Taha hinengaro Thoughts, feelings and mood. Rarely separable from a clinical outcome, and increasingly assessed alongside it. Family & social Taha whānau Family and belonging. Who someone is caring for, and who is caring for them, is clinical information. Spirit & meaning Taha wairua Purpose, identity and meaning — what the person is trying to get back to.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Land & roots Whenua Connection to place and to whakapapa: the ground the four walls stand on. A person’s home, land and community are part of their health rather than the backdrop to it. Used well this is not an extra form to complete. It is a prompt that a goal recorded as “increase shoulder range to 140°” may matter far less to the person than being able to lift a grandchild, or to stand and speak at a family gathering.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Clinical competence is performing the technique correctly. Cultural safety is the patient’s judgement of whether your care was safe for them — which is why you cannot self-certify it, and why it is assessed as an ongoing competency rather than completed as an induction module. It starts with you, not the patient: the Medical Council’s standard asks clinicians to reflect on their own attitudes, assumptions and biases, and on how their own culture shapes the care they give. Arriving from another health system, that reflection is the first piece of work. In day-to-day terms the rest is unremarkable good practice. Nobody expects fluency on arrival. People do notice effort. Learn to pronounce names, place names and the local iwi correctly — and ask if you are unsure. Ask who should be part of the conversation before you begin, rather than after the plan is written.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Ask the patient whether they would like whānau involved in discussions and decisions, and respect their answer. Many will; some will not. Explain what you are about to do to someone’s body before you do it. Notice when someone has gone quiet, and do not read silence as agreement. Do not assume the patient is the decision-maker, or that they are not. Record goals in the person’s own words, not translated into clinical language. Accept correction without defending yourself. It is offered as help.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Kōwhaiwhai: the painted patterns you will see on a marae You may be welcomed onto a marae for a service opening, a team day or a pōwhiri. You will be guided throughout and nothing is expected of you beyond following your host’s lead.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Wait to be called on. Do not walk ahead of the group. Remove your shoes before entering the wharenui. No food or drink inside the wharenui, and do not sit on tables or pillows. Dress tidily and modestly; keep phones away and silent. A hongi — the pressing of noses and foreheads — is a greeting, not a kiss. Follow the lead offered to you. Koha is a contribution, usually collected by the group rather than by individuals. Speeches take the time they take. That is the point of them.

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: Ministry of Health Te Whare Tapa Whā Sir Mason Durie’s model, as the Ministry presents it. Ministry of Health Te Tiriti o Waitangi framework The five principles the health system works from. Medical Council Cultural safety standard The standard for doctors; other regulators publish their own. Medical Council He Ara Hauora Māori A pathway to Māori health equity (PDF). This guide is an introduction written by Ethicare. Your employer’s cultural safety training and local iwi guidance take precedence over anything here. What all of this means inside your own discipline — the assessments, the goal-setting and the situations that catch overseas clinicians out — sits on your profession’s page. Find your profession For the wider picture — the funders, the system priorities and what feels different across every profession — see practising in Aotearoa New Zealand .

chunks.t: Te ao Māori at work: a guide for clinicians
chunks.x: A quick guide to pronunciation Vowels are pure and consistent: a = "ah", e = "eh", i = "ee", o = "aw", u = "oo" — every time. "Wh" sounds like "f" — so whānau is "fah-now". "R" is lightly rolled , closer to a soft "d" than an English r. Macrons (ā ē ī ō ū) simply lengthen the vowel — Māori is "Maa-ori". Place names reward a go: Taupō is "Toe-paw", Whangārei is "Fong-ah-ray". Locals value the effort far more than perfection. Ethicare Resourcing
