chunks.x: For an internationally trained therapist, the clinical work travels well. What does not travel automatically is the credential, and the route in is not the one most health professions follow. The important difference

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.h: You do not register through a statutory health board.
chunks.x: Unlike physiotherapy or occupational therapy, speech-language therapy does not currently have a statutory registration board in New Zealand. NZSTA provides the professional framework for the profession instead. In practice this matters less than it sounds and more than it sounds, at the same time. Less, because there is no board application to sit alongside your visa. More, because most New Zealand employers require prospective speech-language therapists to hold Registered Membership of NZSTA, so it functions as the gate whether or not the law calls it one. For an internationally trained therapist there are two routes to that membership, and which one applies to you is decided by where your association is and where you trained. Work out which route applies to you NZSTA membership, on their own site Route one

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.h: You may have a more direct route.
chunks.x: NZSTA is one of six associations in the Mutual Recognition of Professional Association Credentials Agreement. If you hold the right credential from one of the other five, you may be able to apply to NZSTA through it. United Kingdom RCSLT Certified members of the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists. Ireland IASLT Full members of the Irish Association of Speech and Language Therapists. Australia Speech Pathology Australia Certified members. Canada SAC Certified members of Speech-Language & Audiology Canada. United States ASHA Certificate holders of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association. New Zealand NZSTA The association you would be joining.

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.x: If you completed an accredited UK speech and language therapy programme and hold Certified Membership of the RCSLT, the Mutual Recognition Agreement is likely to be your route to NZSTA membership. It is the shorter and cheaper of the two, and it is worth confirming your eligibility before you plan anything else around it. Check my eligibility Read this before you rely on it

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.x: Holding membership or certification with an overseas partner association does not mean NZSTA membership is granted automatically. There are two conditions that catch people out, and both are worth checking today rather than after you have handed in notice. You must have trained in your association’s own country. The agreement rests on the equivalence of training programmes, not on the membership card. NZSTA says directly that you cannot enter through the Mutual Recognition Agreement if you are a member of a signatory association but trained somewhere else. So a therapist who trained outside the six countries and later gained RCSLT certified membership through the RCSLT’s own overseas process does not qualify on this route. Dysphagia competency is not optional here. You cannot apply under the Mutual Recognition Agreement if you do not meet the dysphagia competency requirements. If that is you, the Qualifications Approval Process is the route instead, and since 12 June 2023 NZSTA has said so explicitly.

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.h: Do not assume your UK registration simply transfers
chunks.x: The route is shorter for eligible applicants from a mutual-recognition country. It is still an application, with its own evidence and its own fee, and NZSTA asks applicants to check its current requirements before submitting anything. Mutual Recognition NZ$225 processing Plus a pro-rated membership for the calendar year. Non-refundable. Qualifications Approval NZ$900 processing Plus a pro-rated membership for the calendar year. Also non-refundable, and the decision cannot be appealed. Qualifications Approval ~6 weeks NZSTA’s stated average once a complete application has been submitted. Incomplete ones take longer. Route two

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.h: Not eligible for mutual recognition? There is another way in.
chunks.x: Internationally qualified speech-language therapists who do not meet the Mutual Recognition criteria apply through NZSTA’s Qualifications Approval Process. NZSTA assesses whether your qualification, clinical experience and professional competence meet its requirements for Registered Membership. The current criteria are specific, and most of them are about evidence rather than judgement. Meeting them is what makes an application complete; it is not a guarantee of approval. An acceptable speech-language therapy or speech pathology qualification At least one year of supervised clinical practice, defined as no less than 36 weeks of full-time work at a minimum of 30 hours a week Certified evidence of 1,000 hours of practice within the past five years Demonstrated competency in communication disorders and in dysphagia A record of continuing professional development A criminal conviction record, or the equivalent, for every country you have lived in for 12 months or more in the last ten years since turning 18 English-language evidence, where it is required of you

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.h: The decision is final, and the fee is not refundable
chunks.x: NZSTA’s qualifications approval committee makes the decision and there is no appeal against it. That is the reason to establish which route applies to you before you pay, rather than after. The Qualifications Approval Framework in full Check your pathway English language

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.x: Not everyone will. For the Qualifications Approval Process, NZSTA requires IELTS Academic where your speech-language therapy qualification was completed in a language other than English, or where English is your second language. The current standard is a score of at least 7 in each of the four modules, with nothing below 7. Test requirements move, and they move without much notice. Confirm the current standard with NZSTA before you book and pay for a test. The detail that decides the most

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.x: If you are planning to work in New Zealand, do not leave your swallowing evidence to the end. NZSTA assesses dysphagia competence as part of both overseas processes, and it carries more consequence than any other single criterion. On the Mutual Recognition route it is a bar: without it you cannot apply. On the Qualifications Approval route it is a condition: applicants who do not meet the dysphagia competencies may still be granted Registered Membership, but with a scope of practice carrying a condition that they are not dysphagia trained. NZSTA is candid that this restricts the roles available in New Zealand, so we are candid about it too. If you work with adults, acute services or rehabilitation, check your dysphagia evidence early. chunks.x: Health services Hospital and community services for adults and children with communication and swallowing disorders, within Health New Zealand · Te Whatu Ora. Work can include stroke, neurological rehabilitation, acute care, developmental services and multidisciplinary rehabilitation. Education Speech-language therapists work with children and young people inside New Zealand’s education system, alongside families, teachers, caregivers and other specialists. Community Closer to people’s homes, whānau and everyday environments, often with wider health, disability and social-care teams around you. Private practice Opportunities exist outside the public system too, including specialist and community-based services. For many paediatric therapists here, the working week is built around the places children already are. Working with children

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.h: Your workplace might be a classroom, not a clinic.
chunks.x: For paediatric therapists, New Zealand offers work inside education as well as health. Therapists working in learning support may work across schools and communities rather than from one clinical base. The work means understanding a child’s communication needs in the context of their home, their education setting and their community, and working closely with parents, caregivers, teachers and other specialists. It is a different shape of week from a hospital caseload. For some therapists it is the reason to come. Pay

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.x: There is no single speech-language therapy salary in New Zealand, and anyone who quotes you one is guessing. Pay depends on the employer, the sector, your experience, your qualifications and which employment agreement covers the role. NZ$78,725 – NZ$116,481 Education sector · qualified speech language therapists · nine steps, effective 2 April 2026 That is the published base salary scale for qualified speech language therapists working in education, set under the Primary Teachers’ Collective Agreement with NZEI Te Riu Roa. Where you sit on it depends on your qualification group and your assessed step. What this figure is A published scale for one employment agreement , not the salary for every speech-language therapist in the country. What decides your step Your qualification group and how much of your previous service is recognised.

chunks.x: Recognition of overseas service is worth asking about early. Health and private work Sit outside this agreement entirely and are set differently. We give you the actual figure for an actual role rather than a range. What it buys A salary only means something next to what housing and everyday life cost where you would live. Compare salary and living costs How we verify pay. Every figure we print comes from a named, dated agreement. This one is Education Circular 2026/09. Where no published scale covers a role, we print no range and give you the offer instead. Immigration

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.h: And then there is the visa.
chunks.x: Your professional eligibility and your immigration eligibility are two separate processes, decided by two different organisations, on two different timetables. Speech Language Therapist is on New Zealand’s Green List , under the Straight to Residence tier, as ANZSCO 252712. The occupational requirements name membership of the New Zealand Speech-language Therapists’ Association, which is the neat part: the professional route on this page is not a separate errand from the immigration one, it sits inside it. What being on a list does not do is decide your case. Immigration settings change, and individual eligibility turns on your circumstances, your role, your employer and the criteria in force on the day you apply. We are not immigration advisers and we will not tell you that you can go straight to residence.

chunks.t: Speech & Language Therapy in New Zealand
chunks.h: And then there is the visa.
chunks.x: We will tell you where to read the current rules, and help you sequence the professional side so it is ready when the immigration side asks for it. Immigration New Zealand · Green List requirements How New Zealand visas work Explore your move to New Zealand The professional questions are rarely the ones that keep people awake. chunks.h: You are not just moving a career.
chunks.x: For most of the people we work with, the hardest questions are not about the job. Where should we live? What will housing cost? What are the schools like? Can my partner work? Can we afford the move? What will everyday life feel like? Moving with your family Schools in New Zealand What the move will cost Your career does not have to start in Auckland. Regional New Zealand Speech-language therapy work exists across New Zealand, not only in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch. For some international therapists a regional role offers exactly what made them look at New Zealand in the first place: a smaller community, easier access to the outdoors, a shorter journey to work, and the chance to become part of a local service rather than one name in a large department. Regional life does not suit everyone, and we are not going to pretend otherwise.

chunks.h: Four ways into the same theatre list
chunks.x: Different registers, different routes, and most days the same list. Choose the one that matches what you do, which may not be what your current job is called.

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: → The recognised New Zealand profession: theatre lists, day surgery and complex anaesthesia, on a defined scope of practice. Medical Sciences Council of New Zealand

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: → Operating department practitioner, anaesthetic practitioner, anaesthesia technologist, theatre technician — your route here is usually into anaesthetic technology. Where your title lands in New Zealand

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: → Consultant-delivered lists, and a scope that reaches into intensive care, obstetrics, retrieval and pain. Medical Council of New Zealand · College comparability assessment

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: → Scrub, circulating and recovery nursing sit on the nursing register rather than this one — a different council and a different application. Nursing Council of New Zealand A list runs on the whole team being in step — which is why the questions employers ask here are usually about how you work with people, not only what you can do. If you trained overseas

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.h: Your job title may not translate. Your scope usually does.
chunks.x: New Zealand regulates anaesthetic technology through the Medical Sciences Council. If you have worked as an operating department practitioner, an anaesthetic practitioner, an anaesthesia technologist or under another theatre title, the question that decides your route is not what the job was called — it is whether your training and your clinical scope line up with the New Zealand profession. That cuts both ways, and it is worth knowing which way before you spend anything. A UK ODP diploma and a decade of lists is a strong position. A job title that sounds close but covered a narrower scope is a harder one. We have taken people through this in both directions and would rather tell you which you are early. In New Zealand

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: Anaesthetic technicians register with the Medical Sciences Council of New Zealand against a defined scope of practice. Registration is what allows you to work, and it runs on its own timeline. The practical upside: the role carries formal standing here, and your experience is assessed and recognised rather than taken on trust. Where you may have trained

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: In several countries the people doing this work are unregulated. If that is you, expect the evidence requirements to focus on demonstrating scope rather than on matching a qualification. In practice that means gathering the detail of what you do — the lists, the techniques, the equipment, the supervision arrangements — and it is worth starting that long before you apply. Check where my title lands Ask Ethicare about scope The shape of the day

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.h: Where do you fit around the patient?
chunks.x: Perioperative work is defined by handover — one patient through five settings in a few hours, with a different combination of the team around them at each. Find the stages you own now, and you can see quickly where an overseas role lands in a New Zealand theatre. Stage 1

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: The patient is worked up before the day — history, medications, airway, comorbidities — so that surprises happen here rather than in the anaesthetic room. Anaesthetists · pre-assessment nursing · the referring team Stage 2

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: Where anaesthetic technicians and anaesthetists work most closely: equipment checked, drugs drawn, monitoring on, airway secured. Anaesthetists · anaesthetic technicians Stage 3

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: The list itself. Position, monitoring, drugs and equipment managed continuously while the surgical team works. Anaesthetists · anaesthetic technicians · surgical and nursing teams Stage 4

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: Emergence, airway, pain and observation until the patient is safe to move — a handover that has to be complete rather than quick. Recovery nursing · anaesthetists Stage 5

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: Back to the ward, or home the same day for day-surgery lists, with the plan handed on to whoever picks up the care. Ward and day-surgery teams · the patient and their whānau The list only runs if the whole team is there. That is why theatre recruitment is a team problem, not a vacancy. Where the work happens

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: A theatre is not a theatre. The size of the hospital decides your case mix, how specialised your lists are, how often you are on call and how much of the equipment you are expected to know cold. Tertiary theatres Cardiac, neuro, paediatric, transplant and major trauma, concentrated in a handful of cities. Deep specialisation, and the complex end of the equipment list. Regional & secondary hospitals General, orthopaedic and obstetric lists with a much broader personal case mix, a smaller team, and acute work that reaches you rather than somebody more senior. Private surgical hospitals Elective lists, predictable finishing times, different team structures and terms outside the collective agreement. Many people hold both a public and a private commitment.

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: Day surgery High throughput, short cases, fast turnarounds — and a working week that fits around a family more reliably than an acute roster does. Rural & remote lists Small theatres a long way from a tertiary centre, where the team is three or four people and the transfer plan matters as much as the anaesthetic. Obstetric & emergency cover Out-of-hours work for maternity, the emergency department and critical care — in smaller hospitals this is a substantial part of the job rather than an occasional call.

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.h: Auckland, Wellington, Palmerston North and Whangārei are not the same job
chunks.x: Two theatre posts with the same title, four hours apart, can differ more than two posts in different specialties. Before you shortlist a city, ask what is on the list, how many of you there are, and how far the nearest tertiary centre is. Explore the destination guides → The practical side

chunks.t: Theatre & perioperative careers in New Zealand
chunks.x: Registration Anaesthetic technicians register with the Medical Sciences Council; anaesthetists with the Medical Council. Either way it is your scope that is assessed, not only your certificate. Registration is the critical path, and for an unregulated overseas title the evidence-gathering is the slow part, so gather it before you look at jobs. Check your pathway → Pay Public-sector theatre pay is set by a national collective agreement, so your base salary comes from a published scale. Your step, your hours and your on-call commitment move the total. Private and ACC-funded work sits outside the agreement. What you could earn → Immigration Most clinicians move on a work visa tied to an accredited employer.

chunks.t: Working in New Zealand
chunks.h: Kia ora. I’m so glad you’re here
chunks.x: New Zealand shaped my own family’s story, and I’ve walked many healthcare families through this same decision. Whatever stage you’re at, I hope this reads like advice from someone who has done it. One of the things I loved most about living in New Zealand was the blue sky and the quality of the light. Of course there were cloudy days too, but I really noticed the difference from home. Even on a crisp, chilly morning the sun would often be shining. You’d wrap up, step outside into the fresh air and feel glad to be out in it. It’s one of the everyday things I still miss. And then there’s the coffee. New Zealanders take it almost as seriously as the Italians, which suited me perfectly. A really good coffee, a crisp morning and a blue sky — sometimes it’s the little things you remember most.

chunks.x: An IRD number in New Zealand, a tax file number in Australia. Payroll, a bank account that behaves properly, and KiwiSaver or super all wait on it — so this is the one to do in week one. What you need to apply 2

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: Your first pay needs somewhere to land, and a rental bond usually has to come from a local account. Some banks let you start the process before you fly, which is worth knowing. Banking and what to bring 3

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: A GP, and how the health system works
chunks.x: Enrolling with a practice is what makes routine care cheap, and it is far easier done before anyone is unwell. Not urgent, until it suddenly is. How enrolment works 4

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: Your current licence works for a limited period and then it does not. The deadline is shorter than most people expect, and the conversion route depends on where the licence was issued. Converting your licence 5

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: Most people arrive into something temporary. Once you know the commute and the school run in practice rather than on a map, the permanent decision gets much easier. Renting, bonds and inspections If you are moving with children, school enrolment usually sits alongside items one and two — it is tied to your address, so it shapes the housing decision. Moving with your family has the sequence for a household rather than an individual.

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: My Plan carries the arrival stage as well as the planning one. It shows one next step rather than twelve, remembers what you have done, and adjusts if your dates or your household change. If you built a plan before you flew, it is still there. Open my plan → What nobody warns you about

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: The bit that is harder than the paperwork
chunks.x: The errands get done in a fortnight. Feeling at home takes longer, and in our experience this is where people are least prepared — because it is the part no checklist can carry for you.

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: Month three is often the hardest
chunks.x: The novelty has worn off, the friends you left are getting on with their lives, and the new ones are still colleagues rather than friends. Almost everyone we have placed describes some version of this, and almost everyone comes out the other side of it.

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: A partner who is not working feels it first
chunks.x: You have a team, a routine and a reason to leave the house. They may have none of those yet. Worth naming out loud early rather than discovering it in an argument.

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: Distance from family is not a one-off cost
chunks.x: It is a birthday, a funeral, a grandchild growing up on a screen. Some households build an annual flight into the budget from the start; it helps more than people expect.

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: Finding your people takes effort here
chunks.x: Communities exist — national, cultural, professional, sporting — but they rarely come to you. The people who settle fastest are usually the ones who joined something in the first month, whatever it was. If we placed you and it is not going well, tell us . We would rather know at month three than read it in a resignation. And we are glad to introduce you to someone who made the same move — often that is the thing that helps. Finding your people

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: Not a list of societies. Where people from your country gather, what happens on a weekend, how newcomers tend to meet each other, and which specialist shops mean you can cook the food you grew up with. New Zealand

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: Cultural and national communities, sport, faith, volunteering, and how the first six months tend to go. Community in New Zealand → Australia

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: The same ground for Australia, state by state, including the big migrant communities in each city. Community in Australia → Your region

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: Every destination guide has a chapter on what a weekend looks like there — the local version, not the postcard. Destination guides → Later on

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: The things that come after the first year
chunks.x: Not urgent now, and worth knowing they exist. Both are decisions rather than errands, and both are easier if you have kept your paperwork tidy from the start. Your visa

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: Residency, and what leads to it
chunks.x: Which routes lead where, how time on a temporary visa counts, and what changes for your family when it does. Visas and residency → Your career

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.x: How seniority, scope and pay steps work once you are inside the system rather than applying to it. Working here → Still us

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: We do not stop at the placement
chunks.x: Long-term careers, not vacancies — so if something comes up in year two, we are still the same phone number. Get in touch → Where this sits

chunks.t: Settling in: the first weeks after you arrive
chunks.h: If you came in at the end
chunks.x: This page is the last of five. If you are earlier in the process than it assumes, start wherever fits. Also worth asking

chunks.x: Registration, your Board, and the route you would be assessed under. Can I work there? → Also worth asking

chunks.x: Housing, hospitals, schools and the commute, region by region. Where could we live? → Also worth asking

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.x: Take-home pay What reaches your bank account An advertised salary is not what you get paid. This works out what comes off the top in New Zealand and Australia, so you can set a budget against a number rather than a headline one. Read this before you budget

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.h: What this figure does not include
chunks.x: The estimate above is deliberately narrow. These are the things that will move your real pay, and the first one will affect almost everybody reading this.

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.h: Your first year is not a full year
chunks.x: If you arrive in November you earn part of a tax year, not all of one. Annualising overstates the tax you will pay, sometimes by thousands. This tool assumes a full year in the country, so treat your arrival year as a separate question and ask us or an accountant about it.

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.x: A New Zealand student loan is repaid through PAYE above a threshold. An Australian HECS-HELP debt is collected the same way, and follows you even if you took it out years ago. Neither is included here, and either will reduce what lands.

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.h: Tax codes and residency in year one
chunks.x: Your New Zealand tax code depends on your circumstances, and getting it wrong is the most common cause of a surprise bill. In Australia, whether you count as a resident for tax purposes in your first year changes the rates entirely.

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.x: Australian earners above a threshold without private hospital cover pay an additional surcharge on top of the 2% levy. For a full-time clinical salary that is a live question, and it is usually cheaper to hold the cover than to pay the surcharge.

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.h: Everything that is not base salary
chunks.x: Penal rates, overtime, on-call and availability allowances, higher duties and salary sacrifice all change the number. In New Zealand much of this is set by the collective agreement covering your role rather than by negotiation.

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.x: Working for Families in New Zealand and the family payments in Australia can make a material difference to a household with children, and neither shows up in a salary calculation. IRD’s own calculators The ATO’s own calculators Ask Ethicare How this is kept honest

chunks.t: Take-home pay calculator
chunks.h: Every rate here has a date on it
chunks.x: A calculator on a website does not update itself. Ours holds each figure with the date it took effect and the official page it came from, and stops answering once it is due for review rather than quietly serving a stale number. That matters more than it sounds. In the year to September 2026 New Zealand’s income tax brackets did not move at all, while the ACC earner’s levy rose from 1.67% to 1.75% and the KiwiSaver minimum went from 3% to 3.5%. Australia’s second tax bracket fell from 16c to 15c. The headline rates are the ones everybody checks. The quiet ones are what make a calculator wrong. Where a future rate is already published, it is loaded with its own start date and takes over on the day. ACC has published the 2027-28 levy, so this tool will use it from 1 April 2027 without anybody touching it.
